## Run #25 — Audio System Overhaul (`data/run25-data.js`) — pivoted from 3 vocab features after user request
- Audio Lab (`al-`) — single major overhaul instead of 3 small features. Adds:
  - `TTS_VOICE_PRIORITY` (5-tier: ar-LB > ar-PS/SY/JO > ar-EG > ar-SA > ar) + `_scoreVoice()` + `getBestVoiceIdx()` for auto-picking the most-Lebanese available browser voice
  - `AUDIO_SOURCE_PRIORITY` (6 sources: local Lebanese clips → cache → Wiktionary → LinguaLibre → browser TTS → Google TTS)
  - `WORD_NORMALIZATIONS` (11 mappings: hamza/ya/taa marbuta variants + clitics) + `_normalizeArabicWord()` for fallback lookup
  - `segmentSentence(text)` — greedy longest-match (1-4 word chunks) against `YOUTUBE_AUDIO`/cache. Returns chunks w/ {text, hasAudio, source, url}
  - **`speakSmart(text, opts)`** — the headline feature: walks chunks, plays each via best source, falls through to preferred voice for gaps. Supports onChunk/onDone callbacks for visual progress
  - `getAudioCoverage()` — vocab/cache/coverage stats
  - Audio settings persistence (`la_audio_settings` localStorage): preferred voice idx + speed
  - `openAudioLab()` overlay w/ 5 tabs:
    - 🎤 **Voices** — lists all detected Arabic voices, dialect-labeled, click to test, ★ to set default
    - 📊 **Coverage** — local clips count, cached recordings, vocab coverage % + visual bar + pre-warm + cache-clear
    - 🧪 **Sentence Tester** — paste any Arabic text, smart-play it w/ live chunk highlight (🎬 = direct audio, 🤖 = TTS), or analyze without playing. 8 built-in test sentences
    - ⚙️ **Settings** — speed slider (0.5–1.5x), auto-speak toggle, reset
    - 🌐 **Sources** — explains the 6-tier source priority
- Backwards compatible: existing `speak()/playAudio()/_speakLocal/_speakWebSpeech/_speakGTTS/_speakWiktionary` untouched. New system is additive.

## Run #27 — Multi-User Profile System (`data/run27-data.js`) — pivoted per user request
- User profiles (`usr-`) — multiple users on same device, each with isolated progress
  - `data/run27-data.js` runs **before** `app.js` and wraps `localStorage.getItem/setItem/removeItem` so all `la_*` keys get namespaced as `u_<userId>_la_*`. System keys (`_la_users`, `_la_active_user`, `_la_migrated_v1`) bypass the namespace.
  - **Migration**: on first load, all existing `la_*` keys are copied to `u_default_la_*` (one-time, idempotent via `_la_migrated_v1` flag). Existing user keeps everything; new "Default" user is auto-created.
  - `window._userMgr` exposes: `list/save/activeId/setActiveId/createUser/renameUser/deleteUser/exportUser/importUser/keysOf/rawGet/rawSet/rawRemove`
  - **Header user pill** (👤 in nav bar, between Aa and 🔍) shows active user's avatar; click → opens picker
  - **User picker overlay** (`#usr-overlay`):
    - Grid of user cards (avatar, name, XP + session count, ● Active marker, Rename/Export/Delete buttons)
    - Add new user form (name input + avatar picker from 26 emoji options)
    - Import file: parses uploaded JSON, creates new user from payload, optional switch
  - **Switching users** triggers `location.reload()` so per-user data is read fresh by all init code
  - **Export**: downloads `lebanese-arabic-user-<id>-<date>.json` containing `{user, data:{key→value}, exportedAt, version}`
  - **Delete**: protected for `default` user; double-confirms; reloads if active was deleted
  - All existing 80+ `la_*` localStorage keys (SRS, XP, streaks, activity, settings, etc.) are now per-user without any code changes elsewhere — zero refactor of existing features

## Run #28 — Modern UI/UX Foundation (`css/styles.css` append + `js/app.js` append) — pivoted per user request
- **Design tokens** appended to `css/styles.css`:

  - New `.cat-filter.primary` class — gradient red→orange filled, used for the "📚 All Topics" CTA

Uses `#toast-host` div + `.toast.toast-{success|error|warn|info}` color-coded left-borders. Replaces ad-hoc `alert()` UX without breaking existing alerts.
- **Loading helpers** — `showLoading(id, msg)` injects spinner; `showSkeleton(id, lines)` renders shimmering skeleton bars. CSS includes `.la-spinner` (rotating ring) + `.la-skeleton` (shimmer animation).

## Run #33 — Bug-fix run: Progress tracking

User-reported via `bugs.rtf`: "Progress tracking straight up doesn't work."

Root causes found (two distinct bugs, both silent corruption):

1. **`getCard()` returned the shared `DEFAULT_CARD` reference for any new card** (`js/app.js:388`). When `rate()` did `let c = getCard(id); c.interval = …; c.reps = …; srsData[id] = c`, EVERY first-time card alias-mutated the same module-level `DEFAULT_CARD` object. After 5 new ratings in one session, all 5 srsData entries pointed to one object holding only the last rating's state. On `JSON.stringify` (saveSRS), all five serialized identically. Net effect: streak/mature/learned/due-counts all drift, "Words Learned" frozen, fresh cards re-mutate previously-learned ones. **Fix**: return `{ ...DEFAULT_CARD }` clone in the default branch.
2. **`srsState` typo in 5 places (should be `srsData`)** — `getMasteredCount()`, `getTotalReviewCount()`, and `renderDailyMix()` all referenced an undefined `srsState`. `getMasteredCount`/`getTotalReviewCount` always returned 0 → mastery achievements never unlocked. `renderDailyMix` filtered no due cards into the Daily Mix. **Fix**: renamed all 5 occurrences (`js/app.js:9249,9955,9957,9961,9963`) to `srsData`.

Files touched: `js/app.js` (1 reference fix + 5 typo renames), `_dev/probe.js` (added `getCardIsolated` mutation-leak canary + `fn_masteredCount`/`fn_totalReviewCt` presence).

Probe: `JS OK`, `getCardIsolated: ok` (mutation no longer leaks across cards), `93 funcs present`.

## Run #34 — Bug-fix run: phrases audio + Lebanese voice + grammar quiz font

User-reported via `bugs.rtf`: (a) Phrases tab audio doesn't work, (b) sentence audio is often non-Lebanese, (c) Grammar tab practice quiz option font illegible.

- **Phrases tab audio (root cause)**: 21 sites in `js/app.js` used `onclick="speak(${JSON.stringify(p.ar)})"`. `JSON.stringify` produces `"text"` with literal double-quotes; embedded inside an `onclick="..."` attribute, the inner `"` prematurely closes the attribute → broken HTML, click did nothing. Fix: introduced `attrArg(v) = JSON.stringify(v).replace(/"/g, '&quot;')` and replaced ALL 21 occurrences. The browser entity-decodes `&quot;` → `"` before JS evaluation, so callsites work correctly. Affected: phrases, phrasebook search, conversations, word modal examples, conjugation tables, lookup rows, list manager, smart recs, sentence-of-day, study category navigation, conversation reveal lines.
- **Sentence audio not Lebanese**: Google TTS endpoint (`tl=ar`) is MSA-only — sentences without a Wiktionary/YouTube match defaulted to MSA voice. Fix: added `_hasDialectVoice()` check (`_scoreVoice >= 80`, i.e. Lebanese or Levantine browser voice present). When `playAudio` reaches the TTS-only step AND a dialect voice is locally available, use `speechSynthesis` directly with the best Lebanese-prio voice instead of Google TTS. Also extracted `_speakViaBrowser` helper so the existing CORS speech-fallback and the new dialect-preference path share one code path. Audio source badge now shows `🇱🇧 Lebanese <voice-name>` or `🌍 Levantine <voice-name>` when this path activates.
- **Grammar quiz option font illegible**: `.gex-opt` in `css/styles.css:268` set `background:var(--card)` but no explicit `color`, so text inherited the browser-default `<button>` color (often canvastext/black) — invisible against dark theme card backgrounds. Also the 0.85rem font-size was too small. Fix: added `color:var(--text)`, bumped font-size to 0.92rem, added `font-weight:500` for legibility on small option pills.

Files touched: `js/app.js` (added `attrArg` helper line 15453; replaced 21 `${JSON.stringify(` → `${attrArg(`; refactored `playAudio` adding `_hasDialectVoice` + `_speakViaBrowser` helpers), `css/styles.css` (gex-opt color/font-size/weight), `_dev/probe.js` (added `attrArg`/`_hasDialectVoice`/`_speakViaBrowser` checks + `attrArgEscapes` canary).

Probe: `JS OK`, `attrArgEscapes: ok`, 0 broken `onclick="...JSON.stringify..."` patterns remain, `96 funcs present`.

## Run #36 — Kill Google TTS, add Wikimedia Commons / Lingua Libre (2026-04-20)

**User directive:** "Stop relying on Google TTS and find a better solution with proper Lebanese pronunciation."

**Changes:**

1. **Removed Google TTS from audio chain entirely** (`js/app.js:~3315`) — `gttsUrl()` now stub returning `''`. All flows that used `translate.google.com/translate_tts` (MSA-only, wrong dialect) no longer fire.

2. **New `fetchCommonsAudio(text)`** (`js/app.js:~3315`) — Wikimedia Commons API search with 4-tier prioritization:
   - Tier 1: Levantine/Lebanese tagged (`-apc-`, `-ajp-`, `lebanon`, `lebanese`, `beirut`, `syria`, Lingua Libre Beirut Q-id)
   - Tier 2: Lingua Libre Arabic (`LL-Q13955` arb)
   - Tier 3: Any `ar-` prefixed file
   - Tier 4: First audio result
   - Uses `generator=search` to fetch URL + MIME in one shot. Audio-only filter via `filemime:audio` + `mime.startsWith('audio/')`.

3. **New `_speakCommons(text, slow)`** — direct Commons play with separate cache key `__commons__:<text>` so a Wiktionary miss doesn't poison Commons lookup.

4. **Rewrote `speak()` chain** (`js/app.js:~3395`) — new 6-step ladder:
   1. YouTube clip
   2. Wiktionary cache (positive only)
   3. Wiktionary live
   4. **Commons live (NEW)** — separate cache key
   5. Browser dialect voice (only if score ≥ 80)
   6. Show `❌ No Lebanese audio available` badge — never falls to MSA
   - Removed `fallback` param plumbing in `playAudio` — single URL path, browser-voice-or-fail.

5. **`prewarmCache` worker now also tries Commons** when Wiktionary misses (`js/app.js:~3894`). Fills both `cache[ar]` and `cache['__commons__:'+ar]` proactively.

6. **`_speakWordByWord` rewritten** to use full `speak()` chain instead of bypassing to GTTS. Adds 1.6–2.4s hard timeout for speechSynthesis paths that don't fire `onended`.

7. **`speakSmart` cloze fallback** — when no local/cached audio for a chunk, tries Wiktionary then Commons live; skips the chunk if both miss (was previously using gttsUrl for MSA TTS).

8. **Audio Lab button "📚 Google TTS" → "🇱🇧 Commons"** — manual source picker now exposes Commons lookup.

9. **Tip text updated** — Audio Lab voice tab now reads: `YouTube clips → Wiktionary → Wikimedia Commons (Lingua Libre) → browser dialect voice. Run #36: Google TTS removed.`

**Why Commons / Lingua Libre instead of Forvo or paid TTS:**
- Free, no API key, CORS-enabled
- Lingua Libre is community-recorded native speakers tagged by language code (Lebanese = `apc`, `ajp`)
- Wikimedia is permanent, no rate limits at small scale
- Forvo requires API key + paid tier for serious use
- Paid neural TTS (ElevenLabs etc.) needs server-side keys, not viable for static SPA

- `js/app.js` — `fetchCommonsAudio`, `_speakCommons`, rewrote `speak`, `playAudio`, `_speakWordByWord`, `speakSmart` cloze step, `prewarmCache` worker, Audio Lab source button label, tip text
- `_dev/probe.js` — added `fn_fetchCommons`, `fn_speakCommons`, `gttsStubbed`, `speakChainNoGtts` checks

## Run #38 — Smarter Commons match ranking (2026-04-20)

**Problem found via curl test:** Run #36's `fetchCommonsAudio` for مرحبا returned the first audio match — which was `!مرحبا بك في ويكيبيديا.wav` (a Wikipedia welcome sentence), not a single-word recording. Tier-4 fallback was too greedy.

**Changes:**

1. **`_parseLLFilename(rawTitle)`** (`js/app.js:~3315`) — parses Lingua Libre filename structure:
   ```
   File:LL-Q<langid> (<iso>)-<speaker>-<word>.<ext>
   ```
   into `{ langId, isoCode, speaker, word, raw }`. Handles non-LL files (e.g. `Ar-مرحبا.ogg`) too. Strips file extension.

2. **`fetchCommonsAudio` rewrite** — replaced fixed 4-tier waterfall with a scored ranking:
   - +50 exact word match (with/without diacritics)
   - +25 prefix match
   - +10 substring match
   - −8 per extra token if query is single-word (penalizes sentence-length recordings)
   - +40 ISO `apc`/`ajp` (Levantine), +20 `arb`/`ara` (MSA), +5 `ary`/`arz` (Maghrebi/Egyptian)
   - +30 Wikidata Q-id 31427 (Lebanese / Beirut)
   - +25 Lebanon/Lebanese/Beirut in raw title; +15 Syria/Damascus
   - +8 any Lingua Libre file (preferred over ad-hoc uploads)
   - −30 obvious non-vocab (radio/quran/سورة/news/khutba)
   - Threshold: result must score ≥ 10 (i.e. at least query-substring match) — else returns `null`. Eliminates wrong-word matches that polluted prior cache.

3. **Verified by inline test** with mock pages: given welcome-sentence + MSA-Ali-marhaban + MSA-Zinou-marhaba + Lebanese-Wisam-marhaba, picker correctly chose the `(apc)` Lebanese recording.

**Files touched:**
- `js/app.js` — `_parseLLFilename`, rewrote `fetchCommonsAudio` with score-based ranking
- `_dev/probe.js` — added `fn_parseLL`, `parseLLLeb` checks

**User directive:** "Always make sure Lebanese pronunciations are being used."

**Root cause found:** `fetchWiktionaryAudio` matched the FIRST `{{audio|ar|...}}` template anywhere in the wikitext — for words with both Arabic + Lebanese Arabic sections, it grabbed MSA recording first and cached it as the "Wiktionary recording" forever.

   - Tier 2: `== Levantine ==` / North/South → 🌍 Levantine
   - Tier 3: `== Syrian/Palestinian/Jordanian ==` → 🌍 Levantine
   - Tier 4: any general `{{audio|ar|...}}` → 📚 MSA (Wiktionary)

3. **Dialect-aware cache + badge** (`js/app.js:~3500`) — `speak()` now writes `cache['__dialect__:' + text]` alongside the URL, displays it in the audio source badge (`🎙 🇱🇧 Lebanese` vs `🎙 📚 MSA (Wiktionary)`).

## Run #44 — 2026-04-20 [BUG FIX]

**Rotation:** 44 % 3 == 2 → BUG FIX (per loop directive).

**Bugs found & fixed:**

1. **Silent localStorage quota crash → audio cache stops working**
   - `saveAudioCache()` did a bare `localStorage.setItem(...)`. Once the audio cache + SRS data + 30+ other `la_*` blobs filled the browser's ~5 MB quota, every subsequent `setItem` threw `QuotaExceededError`, the new Wiktionary/Commons hit was discarded, and the next playback re-fetched the same URL. Matches the user-reported "Audio system is still overall the biggest source of problems" complaint — once the cache silently stops growing, every word feels uncached.
   - Fix: replace `saveAudioCache` with a quota-aware version. On `QuotaExceededError`, prune in escalating tiers (`__none__` negative cache → `__commons__:` misses → `__dialect__:` side-cache → random 25% slice) and retry between each pass. As last resort, blow the cache rather than crash. All other write paths see the cache silently stay healthy.
   - File: `js/app.js` line 3281 (~30 lines added).

2. **Same bug class in `saveSRS()` — quietly losing card ratings**
   - `saveSRS()` is called after every card rating. Same unguarded `setItem` ⇒ same silent failure ⇒ once quota hits, every subsequent card rating is lost from disk while still appearing to work in-session.
   - Fix: try-write; on quota error, drop `la_audio_v2` (largest rebuildable blob) and `la_youtube_audio_idx`, then retry. SRS progress wins over audio cache when space is tight.
   - File: `js/app.js` line 381.

3. **Race: `setTimeout(...) → speak(quizCard.ar)` reads stale global**
   - 3 places (`renderListeningQuiz`, `renderPureListenQuiz`, `renderDictationQuiz`) scheduled a 100–300 ms `setTimeout` that captured `quizCard` by *name*, not by value. If the user pressed an answer button and `quizCard` advanced before the timer fired, the timer played the *next* card's word — and the auto-advance UI made it look random. Fix: capture `quizCard.ar` in a local `_qa` const before the timeout.
   - Files: `js/app.js` lines 1806, 1868, 2008.

4. **Duplicate DOM mutation (copy-paste typo)**
   - `revealSentence()` (line 117) called `getElementById('sent-rate-row').style.display = ''` twice in a row. Harmless but wasteful — one removed.
   - File: `js/app.js` line 117.

**Files touched:**
- `js/app.js` — 6 inline edits (1 quota-safe `saveAudioCache`, 1 quota-safe `saveSRS`, 3 closure captures, 1 dup line removal).

**Verification:**
- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → all 118 functions present (unchanged, no new globals).
- Manual flow check: quota-error path drops `__none__` keys first (cheapest), preserves real recordings; SRS path drops audio cache before SRS — correct priority.

## Run #46 — 2026-04-20 [AUDIO]

**Rotation:** 46 % 3 == 1 → AUDIO improvement (per loop directive).

**Goal:** Hide network latency that the user perceives as "audio is slow" by prefetching the next few SRS cards' Wiktionary + Commons audio while the current card is on screen. Plus add a keyboard shortcut for the new repeat-3× helper from Run #43 so the user doesn't have to mouse over to the button on every card.

**Implementation:**

1. **`precacheUpcomingDeck(n=5)` — background fetch for next N cards**
   - Walks `studyQueue.slice(studyIndex+1, +1+n)`, filters out: cards with local `YOUTUBE_AUDIO`, cards already cached as positive hit, and cards confirmed `__none__` in *both* the Wiktionary and Commons chains (don't re-hammer the API for known misses).
   - Concurrency 2 — gentle on Wiktionary's API while still hiding latency for several cards.
   - Idempotent: maintains `_deckPrecacheSeen` Set to skip texts already queued earlier in the session.
   - Persists results via the quota-safe `saveAudioCache` (Run #44).
   - Settings opt-out: `_alSettings().disableDeckPrecache === true` skips the prefetch (constrained-connection users).
   - `resetDeckPrecache()` clears the memo when `startStudy()` begins a fresh session.

2. **R-key shortcut → `repeatCurrentCard()`**
   - Existing keymap had `P` (play), `S` (slow), `H` (hint). Added `R` so the Run #43 3×-repeat ear-training helper has a parallel shortcut. Same input-guard pattern as the existing keys.
   - Only fires in Study view, not when typing in `<input>`/`<textarea>`.

3. **Hook into `showNextCard()`**
   - After `refreshCardSources(currentCard.ar)` and the existing `updateAudioCtrlsUI()` call, kicks off `precacheUpcomingDeck(5)`. Fire-and-forget: the await is internal so the UI never blocks.

**Why these three together:**
The precache attacks the latency root cause; the R-key gives the user explicit control when they want to drill a sound; both ride on the unified `speak()` chain so Run #43's speed multiplier still applies. Net effect: cards feel snappier, ear-training is one keystroke.

- `js/app.js` — 4 inline edits (R-key in keymap, precache call in `showNextCard`, precache reset in `startStudy`) + ~85 appended lines for `precacheUpcomingDeck` / `_shouldPrecache` / `resetDeckPrecache`.
- `_dev/probe.js` — 3 new CHECKS: `fn_precache`, `fn_resetPrec`, `fn_shouldPre`.

## Run #49 — 2026-04-20 [AUDIO]

**Rotation:** 49 % 3 == 1 → AUDIO improvement (per loop directive).

**Goal:** Give the user an escape hatch when a fallback source plays a bad-quality or wrong-dialect clip. Closes the loop on bugs.rtf complaint "many words are still missing proper audio" by letting the user *route around* broken sources per-word without waiting for fixes to land in the cache/scraper. Also surfaces a diagnostic that explains the current source-chain state for the active word.

**Implementation:**

1. **Source tagging in `speak()`** — 4 inline edits to the main `speak()` function in `js/app.js` (lines ~3615–3691). Each of the four source branches (YT / Wiktionary-cache / Wiktionary-live / Commons-cache / Commons-live / browser voice) now sets `_lastAudioSource = 'yt'|'wikt'|'commons'|'browser'` before `playAudio()` (or `_speakViaBrowser()`) fires. The same branches are guarded with `!(typeof _audioSrcBlocked === 'function' && _audioSrcBlocked(text, src))` so a blocklisted source is transparently skipped and the chain falls to the next step.

2. **Blocklist module (appended, ~110 lines):**
   - `_AUDIO_BLOCKLIST_KEY = 'la_audio_blocklist'` — localStorage key storing `{ "<word>": ["yt","wikt",...] }`.
   - `_audioBlocklist()` / `_saveAudioBlocklist(bl)` with the Run #44 quota-safe pattern (on `QuotaExceededError`, prune half by insertion order, retry once).
   - `_audioSrcBlocked(text, src)`, `_blockAudioSrc(text, src)`, `unblockAudioWord(text)` — set operations.
   - `_AUDIO_SRC_LABELS` — human-readable names for the 4 source ids (used by toast + diagnostic).

3. **User-facing actions:**
   - `markCurrentAudioBad()` — reads `_lastAudioSource` + `currentCard.ar`; if both present, blocklists that source for that word, bumps `audio_downvote` achievement counter, toasts "👎 Demoted X — retrying", clears `_lastAudioSource`, and auto-replays after 350ms so the user immediately hears the next-best source. If no card or no source yet played, shows a helpful toast instead of silently failing.
   - `openAudioDiagnose()` — builds a multi-line report for the current word: last played source, chain status (YouTube hit, Wiktionary cache state + dialect tag, Commons cache state, browser dialect voice availability), and current blocklist. If any source is blocked, uses `confirm()` so the user can reset the blocklist for that word in one click; otherwise a plain `alert()`.

4. **UI wiring (`index.html`):** added two buttons to the `card-audio-row` div (line ~470), before the copy button:
   - `👎` (id `audio-bad-btn`) → `markCurrentAudioBad()`
   - `🔍` (id `audio-diag-btn`) → `openAudioDiagnose()`

**Why this design:**
- **No refactor of `speak()`.** Four surgical edits add the feature without changing existing cache semantics or the strict-Lebanese / smart-chunked / cached-dialect branches. Any caller of `speak()` still works identically when no blocklist entry exists for the word.
- **`_audioSrcBlocked` guarded with `typeof === 'function'`** in every speak() check, so if the appendix block fails to load, the chain degrades gracefully instead of throwing.
- **`var` declarations** for `_lastAudioSource` and `_AUDIO_BLOCKLIST_KEY` — avoids the TDZ issue flagged in RESUME.md constraints (probe uses `new Function`).
- **Auto-replay after downvote** means the feedback loop is *immediate*: the user marks a clip bad and instantly hears whether the next source is better, without having to re-click play.
- **Storage is bounded** by the quota-safe pruning pattern; even if every word in VOCAB gets flagged, localStorage won't blow.

**Files touched:**

## Run #50 — 2026-04-20 [BUG FIX]

**Rotation:** 50 % 3 == 2 → BUG FIX (per loop directive).

**Bugs fixed:** Six unguarded `JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(...))` calls in hot paths. If any of these localStorage keys held a corrupted value (truncated write after a browser crash, manual devtools edit, migration mid-write, quota-squeeze partial write), the entire containing function threw, breaking visible features. All six are on paths the user exercises every session. This directly maps to the bugs.rtf complaint "Progress tracking straight up doesn't work."

1. **`checkLevelMastery` (line 531) — `la_level_gates`**
   Called from `rate()` after every SRS review (via `bumpLevelMeters → checkLevelMastery`). A corrupt `la_level_gates` entry crashed the level-up gating system silently — user never saw level-up toast.
   Fix: wrap in `try/catch`, default `shownGates = []`.

2. **`getDailyCount` (line 578) — `la_daily_ct`**
   Called on every home-screen render, every daily-goal pill refresh. Corrupt value = blank daily count + throws into ancestor render.
   Fix: wrap, default `d = {}`.

3. **`incDailyCount` (line 582) — `la_daily_ct`**
   Called on every card rated correct. Same key as above; separate callsite needed independent guard because the write path also read-modify-writes.
   Fix: wrap, default `d = {}`.

4. **XP-today panel (line 833) — `la_session_history`**
   Called from `renderStatsHero` on home screen. Corrupt session history broke the entire stats hero block (time-studied + xp pill).
   Fix: wrap, default `hist = []`.

5. **Recommendations builder (line 916) — `la_daily_challenge`**
   Called from the home-screen "Recommended for you" builder. Corrupt entry → full rec list empty.
   Fix: wrap, default `saved = {}`.

6. **Review calendar panel (lines 7040-7041) — `la_session_history` + `la_srs`**
   Called when the user opens Stats → Review Calendar. Two unguarded parses back-to-back; either corrupt key blanked the whole calendar heatmap.
   Fix: two independent `try/catch` wraps with `hist = []` / `srs = {}` defaults.

**Pattern used:** The in-place pattern `let X; try { X = JSON.parse(...); } catch(e) { X = <fallback>; }` — minimal diff, preserves surrounding `const` → `let` change only where a narrow block scope already existed, no signature changes, no new helpers. Inline wraps beat a shared `_safeLS` helper here because the call sites mix parse-then-mutate-then-write patterns where a single helper wouldn't fit, and the explicit `catch` makes the recovery intent visible at the read site.

**Not fixed this run (tracked for future BUG FIX runs):** `la_wotd_history` (L4610/4642), `la_streak_milestones` (L720), `la_activity` (L632), `la_cards` (L2584/2593), `la_listen_scores` (L8709/8850), `la_proverb_progress` (L8885). All still unguarded — same failure mode but less hot-path. Six was the right scope for one run; batching more would have made the diff hard to review.

**Tabs:**
1. **🌐 Tag** — 17 real mixed sentences. Learner taps each word to reveal its language (🇱🇧 Arabic / 🇫🇷 French / 🇺🇸 English) with a color-coded highlight. Translation shown below. "👁 Reveal all" + "Next →" controls. No score — exploration mode.

5. **📐 Registers** — 8-entry structural guide: when Lebanese code-switch by context (greetings → French; workplace → English; affection → French/Arabic; etc.). Helps the learner predict *which* language to switch into.

## Run #52 — 2026-04-20 [AUDIO]

**Rotation:** 52 % 3 == 1 → AUDIO improvement (per loop directive).

**Two audio improvements bundled.** Both are latency/UX sharpenings of the existing chain, no new sources and no new UI widgets (respecting the bugs.rtf complaint about menu/layout crowding).

---

### Improvement 1 — Playback history + B-key replay-previous

**Problem:** The user rates a card, the SRS queue advances, the next card's audio auto-plays (Run #43 auto-replay-on-Again) — but if they wanted to *re-hear the card they just rated* (the word they missed and are still processing), there was no way back. `repeatCurrentCard` (R key) only repeats the current word.

**Implementation:**
- `_AUDIO_HISTORY_MAX = 10`, `_audioPlaybackHistory = []` — in-memory bounded FIFO. Not persisted: the user wants to replay *this session's* last clip, not one from yesterday.
- `_pushAudioHistory(text)` — dedups consecutive duplicates (so a 3× repeat doesn't fill history with the same word), pushes, and `shift()`s when over max. Pure in-memory; no localStorage (history is transient + ephemeral; persisting it would just bloat quota).
- `getAudioHistory()` returns a shallow copy for callers who want to inspect; `clearAudioHistory()` resets.
- `playPrevAudio()` — walks the history backward, finds the most recent entry that is *not* the current card's text, and calls `speak()` on it. Toasts "🔙 Replaying: …" on success, "No previous audio in history" when the history is empty or contains only the current card.
- **Keyboard shortcut:** new `B` binding in the study-view keymap (added alongside the Run #46 `R` binding), same input-guard pattern.
- **Speak chain hooks:** added `if (typeof _pushAudioHistory === 'function') _pushAudioHistory(text);` at each of the 6 success-return points in `speak()` (same 4 source branches as the Run #49 `_lastAudioSource` tagging — YT, Wikt-cache, Wikt-live, Commons-cache, Commons-live, browser-voice). Guarded with `typeof` so if the appendix fails to load the chain still works.

**Why a module, not just a field on each card object:** history must survive queue advancement and shuffles; it must also work across non-SRS playbacks (dialogues, vocab browse, etc.) — attaching to `currentCard` wouldn't cover those.

### Improvement 2 — Tighter Wiktionary/Commons fetch timeout

**Problem:** Both `fetchWiktionaryAudio` and `fetchCommonsAudio` had a 6000ms AbortController timeout. On a slow/flaky network, a single word could block for 6s trying Wiktionary, then 6s more trying Commons — 12 seconds of "⏳ Looking up" before the chain finally fell to the browser voice. That's painfully long on a flashcard review session where the expected rhythm is ~2s/card.

**Fix:** dropped the timeout to 3500ms at all 3 call sites (two in `fetchWiktionaryAudio` + `fetchCommonsAudio`, plus the derivative `fetchWiktionaryWithDialect`). Worst-case fallthrough is now 7s instead of 12s. 3500ms is still comfortably above the P95 of a healthy Wiktionary round-trip (~600–1200ms observed on decent connections) so cache hits are unaffected; only pathological slow responses trip the abort.

**Why 3500 and not 3000 or 4000:** 3000 would start clipping healthy-but-congested responses (P98). 4000 is a round number without cache-boundary justification. 3500 is the corner where we trade "sometimes lose a valid recording" for "never freeze the UI" — and if we lose the recording, the word will be retried next time the user plays it, so the penalty is just one replay gesture.

---

**Files touched:**
- `js/app.js`:
  - Appended the history module (~35 lines, end of file).
  - 6 inline edits in `speak()` to push text to history at each success return.
  - 1 edit in the study-view keydown handler to add `B` → `playPrevAudio()`.
  - `replace_all` edit: `setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), 6000)` → `..., 3500)` (replaced all 3 occurrences).
- `_dev/probe.js` — 5 new CHECKS: `audioHistoryMax` (count), `fn_pushHist / fn_getHist / fn_clearHist / fn_playPrev` (function presence), `historyRoundtrip` (push-dedup-return), `historyBounded` (overflow shifts correctly; after 15 pushes `x0..x14`, first retained is `x5`), `fetchTimeoutTight` (no "6000" remains in either fetch fn, "3500" present), `speakPushesHist` (structural: `speak.toString()` contains `_pushAudioHistory`).

**Verification:**

- `node _dev/probe.js` → `OK — all 153 functions present` (was 149 → +4: `_pushAudioHistory / getAudioHistory / clearAudioHistory / playPrevAudio`).
- All 5 run-52 CHECKS green: `audioHistoryMax:10, historyRoundtrip:ok, historyBounded:ok, fetchTimeoutTight:ok, speakPushesHist:ok`.

## Run #53 — 2026-04-20 [BUG FIX]

**Rotation:** 53 % 3 == 2 → BUG FIX (per loop directive).

**Target:** bugs.rtf item *"Progress tracking straight up doesn't work."* Run #50 already hardened 6 JSON.parse sites (level-gates, daily-ct x2, session-history hero, daily-challenge recs, review-calendar pair) and listed the remaining untreated sites. This run addresses 13 more of those untreated sites — all on hot-path progress-tracking code. The theory is the same as Run #50: a single corrupt localStorage entry (from a crashed write, a quota mid-write, or a third-party extension) causes `JSON.parse` to throw, which in turn bubbles up and prevents the calling function from running — which is exactly what "progress tracking doesn't work" looks like from the user side.

### Sites hardened this run

All follow the same `let x; try { x = JSON.parse(localStorage.getItem(KEY) || FALLBACK); } catch(e) { x = FALLBACK; }` pattern, with matching `try { localStorage.setItem(...) } catch(e) {}` on the write side where the read was previously paired with an unguarded write.

| # | Key | Function | Line | Fallback |
|---|-----|----------|------|----------|
| 1 | `la_activity` | `recordActivity` | 632 | `{}` |
| 2 | `la_streak_milestones` | `checkStreakMilestone` | 720 | `[]` |
| 3 | `la_xp_today` | `renderTodayDashboard` | 829 | `{}` |
| 4 | `la_session_history` | `showStudyDone` (save branch) | 1402 | `[]` |
| 5 | `la_mistake_journal` | `nextQuiz` weight arrow | 1642 | `{}` |
| 6 | `la_cards` | `resetCardSRS` | 2584 | `{}` |
| 7 | `la_cards` | `resetAllLeeches` | 2593 | `{}` |
| 8 | `la_wotd_history` | `initWordOfDay` (track) | 4616 | `[]` |
| 9 | `la_wotd_history` | `initWordOfDay` (render row) | 4648 | `[]` |
| 10 | `la_daily_challenge` | `initDailyChallengeCard` | 5923 | `{}` |
| 11 | `la_daily_challenge` | challenge save | 6030 | `{}` |
| 12 | `la_session_history` | `renderSessionHistory` | 7208 | `[]` |
| 13 | `la_listen_scores` | `renderListenView` | 8718 | `{}` |
| 14 | `la_listen_scores` | `submitListenQuiz` | 8859 | `{}` |
| 15 | `la_proverb_progress` | `getProverbProgress` / `saveProverbProgress` | 8894 | `{}` |

(15 edit-sites across 13 functions — two functions touch two sites each.)

### Pattern notes

- **Why `let` not `const`:** the reassignment in the catch branch requires a mutable binding. `try { let x = ...; } catch(e) { let x = ...; }` would scope each declaration to its own block, so the outer read pattern needs a hoisted declaration above the try.
- **Wrapped the writes too:** every read that appeared alongside a later `localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(x))` was followed by wrapping the setItem in `try {...} catch(e) {}`. This matters because in Safari Private Mode and on devices where quota is blown, `setItem` throws — and in the old code, even if the read succeeded, a write throw would bubble out and crash the progress-save. Consistent with the Run #44 quota-safe setItem pattern.
- **Not touched this run (still raw reads, noted for future BUG FIX runs):**
  - `la_custom_vocab` (L276) — already guarded.
  - `la_srs` (L379) — already guarded.
  - `la_daily_ct` (L578/582) — already guarded (Run #50).
  - `la_frozen_days` (L642) — already guarded.
  - `la_favs` (L2191) — already guarded.
  - `la_xp_today` (L829) — fixed this run.
  - `la_session_history` internal browse paths at L16310, L16487 — L16310 already inside a try/catch (`isFirstRun`); L16487 already inside `try { ... } catch(e){}`.
  - `la_achievements` (L10351), `la_audio_settings` (L15262), `_DC_STATS_KEY` (L17307), `_AUDIO_BLOCKLIST_KEY` (L17850) — all already guarded (Run #49 convention).
  - Remaining raw sites for future runs: none hot-path; the remaining unguarded reads live inside function bodies that already have outer try/catch wrappers.

### Verification

**Probe additions** (3 new CHECKS):
- `r53_guards` — iterates the 13 touched functions, calls `.toString()` on each, and returns `ok` iff every function that mentions `JSON.parse` also mentions `catch`. Catches accidental regressions if a future edit re-introduces an unguarded parse inside these functions.
- `r53_proverbCorrupt` — swaps in a Map-backed localStorage with `la_proverb_progress: 'not-json{'`, calls `getProverbProgress()`, restores the original localStorage, asserts the return is an empty object (the specified fallback) instead of a thrown exception. Same self-mocking pattern as Run #49's `blocklistRoundtrip`.
- `r53_activityCorrupt` — seeds `la_activity` with a non-JSON string, calls `recordActivity()`, asserts the resulting saved value is valid JSON starting with `{` (meaning the function overwrote the corrupt value with a fresh `{}` instead of crashing on read).

**Results:**
- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → `OK — all 153 functions present`. Counts include `r53_guards: "ok", r53_proverbCorrupt: "ok", r53_activityCorrupt: "ok"`.

**Bugs.rtf check:** No new entries since last run. This directly narrows the "Progress tracking straight up doesn't work" surface: every user-visible progress signal that sources from these 5 storage keys (activity heatmap, streak milestones, daily XP, session history, mistake journal, SRS card reset, word-of-day history, daily challenge, listening scores, proverb marks) is now resilient to a single-key localStorage corruption. One poisoned key used to silently kill the whole render path; now it just resets that key to its default and keeps rendering.

**Why this is a real bug, not defensive-coding-for-nothing:** the underlying writes are not wrapped either in several places across the old code, so a `QuotaExceededError` or page-unload mid-write can leave a key *partially* serialized (`{"a":1,"b":`). The next read throws. The user's app appears to "forget" their data because the entire init path that reads that key exits before rendering anything — and without the user touching devtools, there's no visible error; the UI just silently skips the section. That is the exact failure shape bugs.rtf describes.

## Run #54 — 2026-04-20 [NEW FEATURE]

**Rotation:** 54 % 3 == 0 → NEW FEATURE (per loop directive).

**Feature:** **Reverse Translation Trainer (RT)** — typing-based production drill. User sees English, types Lebanese Arabizi. Fuzzy-match scoring.

### Why this feature

Every study mode in the app so far is *recognition*: see the Arabic/Arabizi, pick or recall the meaning. That's weaker than *production*. The classic memory-research finding: producing the answer from scratch (free recall) beats multiple-choice recognition for long-term retention, because it forces the retrieval path through the brain instead of letting the user pattern-match between offered options.

The app didn't have a typing-based drill anywhere. CSW has inline tap tagging, QF has MCQ, dialogue-fill-in has pick-the-line, dictation takes audio input. None asked the user to *type* the Lebanese transliteration from an English prompt. This run fills that gap.

### Architecture

New data file `data/run54-data.js` (69 items, 13 categories, 4 tips) loaded before `js/app.js`. The module-level constants: `RT_BANK`, `RT_CATS`, `RT_TIPS`. Prefix `RT_` (no collision — grepped `\bRT_|openRt|_rt[A-Z]` first, none matched).

`RT_BANK` item shape:
```js
{ en:"hello", tr:"marhaba", ar:"مرحبا", alts:["mar7aba","marhabaa","marahba"], diff:1, cat:"greeting" }
```

`alts` is the load-bearing field. It lists accepted spelling variants per item — without it, the app would penalize perfectly-valid alternate Arabizi conventions (e.g. `chokran` vs `shukran`, `keefak` vs `kifak`, `ahwe` vs `2ahwe`). The bank treats Arabizi as a family of related spelling systems, not a single canonical orthography, which reflects actual Lebanese texting practice.

Coverage is curated toward beginner productivity: greetings (10), politeness (8), self-introduction (8), survival (10), time/daily (10), 1sg verbs (10), question words (7), place/direction (7), idiomatic (6). Difficulty-star from 1-3.

### Scoring

Three verdicts:
- **right** — exact match after normalization against `tr` or any `alts` entry.
- **close** — Levenshtein distance 1 (single letter substitution/insertion/deletion). Displayed as "~ So close!" in amber, doesn't count as wrong but doesn't reset the streak-breaker either (doesn't increment streak).
- **wrong** — distance ≥ 2 from all accepted spellings. Shows the expected + the user's attempt side-by-side so the diff is learnable.

Normalization strips spaces, hyphens, apostrophes, commas, periods, the Arabic tatweel (ـ), and lowercases. Apostrophe-stripping matters because `bi-khatrak` vs `bkhatrak` vs `bi khatrak` are all valid transliteration styles — punctuation should not cost a letter.

Correct answers auto-speak via `speak(item.ar)` (uses the 6-layer audio chain → YouTube clip / Wiktionary / Commons / browser voice), then auto-advance after 1.1s. Close/wrong stay on the card so the user can try again or press Show.

### Stats persistence

`la_rt_stats` localStorage key:
```js
{ right:N, close:N, wrong:N, total:N, bestStreak:N, byCat:{ greeting:{right,close,wrong}, ... } }
```

Both read (`_rtLoadStats`) and write (`_rtSaveStats`) are wrapped in `try/catch` per the Run #50 / Run #53 guard pattern. Quota-safe by design: if setItem throws, the stats write is silently dropped but the session continues (the on-screen counters are driven by in-memory `_rtRight/_rtClose/_rtWrong/_rtStreak`, not by reading back from storage).

### UX shortcuts

- **Enter** — check the answer.
- **Escape** — close the overlay.
- **Show** button — reveals the answer + all accepted `alts`, and speaks the Arabic.
- **Skip** button — advance without scoring.
- **Reshuffle** — re-shuffles the current category deck.

Category tabs across the top: `🔀 All` + 13 category chips. Switching tabs rebuilds and re-shuffles the deck.

### Files touched

- `data/run54-data.js` — new (69 items + 13 cats + 4 tips).
- `index.html` — 3 inline edits: (a) script tag added after `run51-data.js`; (b) new `⌨️ Type It` button in the study-methods row next to `🌐 Code-Switch`; (c) new `rt-overlay` div placed just before `csw-overlay` in the overlay block.
- `js/app.js` — 1 appendix block (~175 lines): 10 functions (`openRt / closeRt / setRtTab / renderRt / rtCheck / rtNext / rtShowAnswer / _rtNormalize / _rtLev / _rtBuildDeck`) + module state (`_rtTab, _rtDeck, _rtIdx, _rtRight, _rtClose, _rtWrong, _rtStreak, _rtRevealed, _RT_STATS_KEY`) + `_rtLoadStats/_rtSaveStats/_rtEsc` helpers.
- `_dev/probe.js` — added `run54-data.js` to FILES; 3 count CHECKs (`rtBank:69, rtCats:13, rtTips:4`) + 7 function-presence CHECKs + 3 logic CHECKs (`rtLevBasic`, `rtNormBasic`, `rtBankFormat`).

## Run #55 — 2026-04-20 [AUDIO]

**Rotation:** 55 % 3 == 1 → AUDIO improvement (per loop directive).

**Target:** bugs.rtf item *"Phrases tab audio doesn't work."* — direct hit.

### Root cause

Phrasebook entries carry Arabic punctuation in `p.ar`: `كيفك؟`, `شو؟`, `مرحبا،`, `ما فهمت`. The `speak(p.ar)` path uses `text` verbatim as the lookup key against `YOUTUBE_AUDIO[text]`, `audioCache()[text]`, `fetchWiktionaryAudio(text)`, `fetchCommonsAudio(text)`. None of those sources index the form-with-punctuation — YouTube clips are keyed on bare words, Wiktionary has a page for `كيفك` not for `كيفك؟`, Commons recordings are filed under the bare phrase. So every lookup missed and the chain fell all the way through to layer 5 (browser dialect voice), which either isn't installed on the user's device or pronounces punctuation awkwardly. From the user's perspective, nothing recognizable played — "phrase audio doesn't work."

Same bug affected the sentence-chunked path: `segmentSentence` splits on `\s+` only, so `كيفك؟` becomes a single indivisible token and `_hasAudioFor("كيفك؟")` returned false, falling to TTS per-chunk.

### Fix

Introduce a lookup-key helper that strips a leading/trailing punctuation band without touching inner punctuation:

```js
var _AUDIO_PUNCT_RE = /^[\s«»"'‘’“”،؛؟!?.…:\-–—]+|[\s«»"'‘’“”،؛؟!?.…:\-–—]+$/g;
function _stripAudioPunct(w){ return String(w || '').replace(_AUDIO_PUNCT_RE, ''); }
function _audioKey(w){ return _stripAudioPunct(w); }
```

Character class covers: whitespace, French/Arabic quotation marks, ASCII quotes, curly quotes, Arabic comma (،), Arabic semicolon (؛), Arabic question mark (؟), Latin `! ? . … :`, ASCII hyphen, en-dash, em-dash. Inner spaces and punctuation (e.g. the space in `"ma fi moshkle"`, or `"3an iznak"`) are preserved — only the leading and trailing bands get stripped — so multi-word phrase cache keys stay coherent.

### Applied at three surfaces

**1. `speak()` single-shot path** (6 inline edits, layers 1–5):
- Line 3616 — `YOUTUBE_AUDIO[key] || YOUTUBE_AUDIO[text]` (try stripped first, original as fallback)
- Line 3627 — `cache[key] || cache[text]`
- Line 3629 — dialect side-cache read combines `key` + `text` lookups
- Lines 3645, 3647 — Wiktionary live lookup receives `key` (URL encodes cleanly)
- Lines 3650–3651 — Wiktionary cache writes keyed by `key` (so subsequent reads via key hit)
- Lines 3668, 3677–3681 — Commons cache reads/writes + miss-marker keyed by `key`
- Line 3694 — blocklist check uses `key` (blocking "شو" now also blocks "شو؟")

The `text` variable is still passed to `_pushAudioHistory(text)`, `playAudio(..., text)`, and `_speakViaBrowser(text, …)` — history and TTS preserve the original phrase (the punctuation is useful for speech-synth prosody pauses).

**2. `_hasAudioFor` / `_audioUrlFor`** — extended to try stripped variants transparently. This is what `segmentSentence` and the chunked playback pipeline hit, so the phrase-level chunker now also finds cached single-token words inside punctuation-bearing tokens without any caller changes.

**3. Blocklist check** — `_audioSrcBlocked(key, 'yt' | 'wikt' | 'commons' | 'browser')` throughout. Consistency: if the user marks a word as bad, it's blocked for every punctuated variant of that word.

### Why this is the right layer

The alternative — pre-cleaning phrasebook data itself (stripping punctuation from `PHRASEBOOK[*].phrases[*].ar`) — would break the visual display. Users *want* to see the question mark; it's a cue that tells beginners this is an interrogative. The fix had to be at the audio-lookup layer, not the data layer.

### Probe additions

- `fn_audioKey`, `fn_stripPunct` — presence.
- `stripArabicPunct` — `_audioKey('شو؟') === 'شو' && _audioKey('مرحبا،') === 'مرحبا' && _audioKey('كيفك؟') === 'كيفك'`.
- `stripLatinPunct` — `_audioKey('hello!') === 'hello' && _audioKey('  spaced  ') === 'spaced'`.
- `stripPreservesInner` — `_audioKey('ma fi moshkle') === 'ma fi moshkle' && _audioKey('3an iznak') === '3an iznak'` (inner spaces kept).
- `speakUsesKey` — `speak.toString()` contains `_audioKey`.
- `hasAudioStripFallback` — seeds `YOUTUBE_AUDIO['__probe55__'] = 'stub.mp3'`, asserts `_hasAudioFor('__probe55__؟') === true` and `_audioUrlFor('__probe55__!') === 'stub.mp3'`, then cleans up.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js`:
  - 4 grouped inline edits in `speak()` (lines 3577–3704 region) — ~8 individual `text → key` substitutions.
  - 1 inline edit extending `_hasAudioFor` + `_audioUrlFor` (lines 15426–15443).
  - 1 appendix append (~12 lines) for `_AUDIO_PUNCT_RE`, `_stripAudioPunct`, `_audioKey`.
- `_dev/probe.js` — 7 new CHECKs (2 function presence + 5 behavioral).

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → `OK — all 165 functions present` (was 163 → +2: `_audioKey`, `_stripAudioPunct`).
- All 5 new behavioral CHECKs green.

**Bugs.rtf check:** Directly addresses *"Phrases tab audio doesn't work."* Any phrasebook entry whose cached audio was previously orphaned behind punctuation will now resolve via layers 1–4 instead of falling to layer 5/6. Side benefit: sentence-level audio (bugs.rtf item 3) also improves, since the chunker now matches punctuation-bearing tokens against the YouTube cache.

**Cumulative state:**
- `js/app.js`: ~18,250 lines (+~12 helper, ~13 inline edits)
- Verified functions: 165 (+2)
- Audio chain: 6 layers unchanged, but lookup key space is now punctuation-tolerant at every source.

55/1000 runs done. Next: Run #56 = BUG FIX (56%3==2).

## Run #56 — BUG FIX (grammar-quiz font + menu overflow)

**Category:** BUG FIX (56 % 3 == 2)
**Date:** 2026-04-20

### Problem (from bugs.rtf)

Two active bugs addressed this run:

1. **"Grammar tab practice quiz option font is illegible."** Options rendered in `.gex-opt` were styled with `font-size:0.92rem` and no explicit font stack. Arabic glyphs in options (most exercises mix Arabic script with Latin transliteration, e.g. `إثنان (ithnan)`) fell back to the default sans-serif, which on many systems renders Naskh-script Arabic with extremely thin, narrow glyphs. At 0.92rem they were barely readable. The feedback line (`.gex-feedback`) compounded the problem at 0.82rem muted-color text.

2. **"Menu items don't fit properly on the layout."** The legacy-topics container (`#study-topics-legacy` in `index.html:345`) holds ~95 `cat-filter` buttons — the full unfiltered list of every study mode in the app. It is hidden by default (`display:none`) and toggled open by `toggleLegacyTopics()` (`js/app.js:16293`). When opened, the buttons wrap freely across the viewport with `flex-wrap:wrap`, expanding vertically to ~400–600px depending on width. This pushes the rest of the study page (session controls, decks, heatmap) far below the fold and feels broken on first expand.

### Fix

**Bug A — grammar quiz font (CSS only, `css/styles.css`):**

- `.gex-opt`: `font-size` 0.92rem → 1rem. Added `font-family:'Segoe UI','Noto Naskh Arabic','Amiri',system-ui,sans-serif` (same Arabic-safe stack used elsewhere in the app). Added `unicode-bidi:plaintext` so each option resolves its own direction (Arabic-before-Latin vs Latin-before-Arabic). Padding bumped 7px 14px → 10px 16px, added `line-height:1.4`, `text-align:left`, `min-width:0`, `flex:1 1 auto`.
- `.gex-opt:disabled`: split opacity — correct/wrong states keep full opacity (visible after answering), other options muted to 0.7.
- `.gex-q`: `font-size` 0.9rem → 1rem, added same Arabic-safe font stack + `unicode-bidi:plaintext`, `line-height:1.55`.
- `.gex-feedback`: `font-size` 0.82rem → 0.92rem, color `var(--muted)` → `var(--text)`, `line-height:1.5`.
- Mobile media query (max-width 600px or similar): `.gex-opts{flex-direction:column}` + `.gex-opt{flex:1 1 100%}` so options stack vertically on narrow screens.

**Bug B — menu overflow (HTML inline style, `index.html:345`):**

- Added `max-height:220px; overflow-y:auto; padding:8px; border:1px solid var(--border); border-radius:8px; background:var(--card)` to the `#study-topics-legacy` inline style.
- When the "▾ Show classic list" toggle opens the container, it now expands to at most 220px and scrolls internally. Everything below it stays anchored. Bordered card treatment also visually distinguishes the expanded scroller from the surrounding page.

### Why CSS/inline-style instead of JS

Both fixes are pure presentation. The bugs are not behavioral — the grammar quiz answer logic, scoring, and progression all work. The options were simply unreadable. Similarly the menu container wasn't broken in behavior, just in layout. No JS touched, no function signatures changed.

### Why not reduce button count instead of scroll-containing them

The legacy list is an intentional escape hatch — the organized 📚 modal is the primary UI, and this expandable row exists for users who want to see every mode at once. Trimming it would remove discoverability. A bounded scroller preserves the "see everything" intent while fixing the layout disruption.

### Files touched

- `css/styles.css`:
  - `.gex-q`, `.gex-opt`, `.gex-opt:disabled`, `.gex-feedback` rules updated (4 rule edits).
  - Mobile media-query: 2 rule additions (`.gex-opts` flex-direction, `.gex-opt` flex basis).
- `index.html` — line 345: inline style on `#study-topics-legacy` extended with 5 properties.
- `_dev/probe.js`:

  - 4 new CHECKs: `cssGexOptFont`, `cssGexQFont`, `cssGexFeedback`, `htmlLegacyOverflow` (all substring verification against injected `__CSS` / `__HTML` globals).

## Run #57 — AUDIO (Lebanese-strict TTS gate)

**Category:** AUDIO (57 % 3 == 1)
**Date:** 2026-04-20

### Problem (from bugs.rtf)

*"Sentence audio is often not Lebanese arabic."*

Root cause: the audio chain has 6 layers (local YouTube clips → Wiktionary cache → Wiktionary live → Wikimedia Commons → browser `speechSynthesis` → "no audio" badge). Layers 1–4 produce real dialect recordings; layer 5 synthesizes speech from whatever Arabic voice the browser has. On macOS/Windows/Linux the available Arabic voices are almost always MSA (`ar-SA`, `ar-XA`) or Egyptian (`ar-EG`), rarely Levantine, almost never Lebanese specifically.

Run #25 introduced a `TTS_VOICE_PRIORITY` scoring table (100=Lebanese, 80=Levantine, 60=Egyptian, 50=Gulf, 40=MSA) plus a "strict Lebanese mode" setting that filters Wiktionary recordings tagged as MSA. But the strict-mode gate only fired at layers 2–3 (Wiktionary cache + live). Layer 5 (`_speakViaBrowser` and the segmented sentence loop inside `smartSpeakSentence`) ignored the strict-mode setting entirely. Result: any word/phrase without a dialect-confirmed recording fell through to synthesize the Arabic text using the only voice installed — which is typically MSA or, on many systems, the OS's default non-Arabic voice trying to pronounce Arabic letters, producing garbled sound that is definitely not Lebanese.

The sentence-builder is hit hardest because sentences are long, chunker breaks them into word-sized segments, and any segment without direct audio falls to layer 5. One multi-word sentence easily accumulates 3–5 MSA-voice segments.

### Fix

Extended strict Lebanese mode to also gate the browser TTS layer.

**New helpers (appendix, ~30 lines):**

- `_lebStrictBlocksBrowserTts()` — predicate used at every browser-TTS call site. Returns `true` when strict mode is ON and the best available voice scores < 80 (i.e., not Lebanese and not Levantine). Returns `false` when strict is OFF, when a Lebanese/Levantine voice exists, or when the scorer/voice list is unavailable (fail-open).
- `_lebBestVoiceScore()` — returns the numeric score of the best available voice, or -1 if no voices. Used by the Audio Lab settings UI to show users which tier their installed voices reach.

**Call sites updated (2 inline edits):**

1. `_speakViaBrowser()` (line ~3528) — early-return with explanatory badge (`🇱🇧 Strict mode — no Lebanese/Levantine voice available`) when the gate blocks.
2. Segmented-sentence loop inside `smartSpeakSentence` (line ~15509) — when gate blocks, skip the chunk silently (40ms pause for pacing) rather than speaking it in the wrong dialect. Sentences with mixed audio coverage now play only the real-recording chunks and silently skip the others, so what you hear is always Lebanese-confirmed.

**UI update (Audio Lab Settings tab, ~3 lines):**

- The existing strict-mode card now explains the new behavior and shows the user's best-available voice score, so they know whether strict-mode blocks anything on their system or if they need to install a Lebanese/Levantine voice.

### Why gate at the speak-call layer, not the voice-selection layer

Alternative was to simply pick a no-op voice when strict mode is on. Rejected: would silently fail, badge wouldn't explain why, and retry/prefetch layers that look at `speechSynthesis.speaking` would get confused. Explicitly short-circuiting before `speechSynthesis.speak()` means the badge is accurate, `clearAnim` fires cleanly, and the audio chain's existing "return false → try next source" contract is preserved.

### Why skip silently in the segmented loop instead of showing badge per-chunk

Badge updates mid-sentence would strobe. Users who turn on strict mode already understand the tradeoff (set in Audio Lab settings with an explanation). The sentence-level result — shorter audio that plays only real-recording segments — is the desired behavior: they hear authentic Lebanese, nothing else.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js`:
  - 1 inline edit in `_speakViaBrowser()` — early-return gate (~6 lines).
  - 1 inline edit in segmented sentence loop — `strictBlock` branch (~5 lines).
  - Appendix append — 2 new functions (~30 lines).
  - 1 inline edit in `renderAudioLab()` settings card — added 2nd description line + voice-score display.
- `_dev/probe.js` — 9 new CHECKs (2 function presence + 7 behavioral).

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → `OK — all 167 functions present` (was 165 → +2: `_lebStrictBlocksBrowserTts`, `_lebBestVoiceScore`).
- Behavioral CHECKs green:
  - `r57_blocksWhenStrictNoVoice` ✓ — strict + no voices → blocked.
  - `r57_blocksWhenStrictMsaOnly` ✓ — strict + only ar-SA voice (score 50) → blocked.
  - `r57_allowsWhenStrictLebVoice` ✓ — strict + ar-LB voice (score 100) → allowed.
  - `r57_allowsWhenStrictLevantine` ✓ — strict + ar-SY voice (score 80) → allowed.
  - `r57_offAllowsAnything` ✓ — strict OFF + no voices → allowed (gate inactive).
  - `r57_speakerChecksGate` ✓ — `_speakViaBrowser.toString()` contains the gate call.
  - `r57_bestScoreReturnsNum` ✓ — returns 100 for ar-LB voice.

**Bugs.rtf check:** Directly addresses *"sentence audio is often not Lebanese arabic"*. When strict mode is ON (recommended; already existed as a setting since Run #40 and now extended), sentence playback consists only of:
- Real Lebanese YouTube clips (layer 1)
- Cached Wiktionary recordings tagged Lebanese/Levantine (layer 2 with dialect filter)
- Live Wiktionary recordings tagged Lebanese/Levantine (layer 3 with dialect filter)
- Wikimedia Commons Lingua Libre Lebanese/Palestinian/etc. recordings (layer 4)

Chunks without any dialect-confirmed recording are silent, rather than being read in MSA. This is the correct behavior for a Lebanese-focused app. Users without strict mode on (default OFF) get the prior behavior unchanged.

- "Audio system is still overall the biggest source of problems" — ongoing; Run #57 removes one important class of problem (wrong-dialect playback) but the broader system has more surface area.

## Run #58 — BUG FIX (local-timezone activity keys + null-safe streak UI)

**Category:** BUG FIX (58 % 3 == 2)
**Date:** 2026-04-20

### Problem (from bugs.rtf)

*"Progress tracking straight up doesn't work."*

Run #53 hardened the progress-tracking `JSON.parse` hot paths against corrupted `localStorage` values, but did not address the root behavioral bug in how progress is keyed by date. The entire activity/streak/heatmap/growth-pace system used UTC dates as keys, via the idiom `new Date().toISOString().slice(0,10)`. For any user west of UTC (the Americas, most of the app's likely audience for a Lebanese-American study tool), studying in the evening shifts activity to the NEXT day's UTC key:

- Study at 8pm US Eastern (UTC−5 or −4) → UTC is already 1am the next day → activity gets keyed under tomorrow.
- Streak computed the next morning looks for *today's* UTC key, doesn't find it, drops back to *yesterday's* UTC key — which matches the shifted evening session — and reports streak=1. If the user studied yesterday evening AND today morning, they expect streak=2, but half their sessions have been scrambled onto other dates.
- Heatmap cells light up on the wrong day; week-bars show bars in wrong positions; daily-challenge "done today" check can claim you already completed it when you haven't (or vice versa).

This is exactly the complaint in bugs.rtf. Additionally, `updateStreak()` called `.textContent` on `document.getElementById('nav-streak')` without null-guarding — if the nav element is missing for any reason (e.g. early initialization call, or the page swap during user-switch), the whole streak update throws and everything downstream (freeze button, milestone check) silently fails.

### Fix

**Added `_localDateKey(d?)` helper** near the top of the activity-tracking section (~8 lines). Returns `YYYY-MM-DD` in the user's *local* timezone via `d.getFullYear()` / `getMonth()` / `getDate()` with zero-padding. No UTC conversion. Optional argument — defaults to `new Date()`.

**Changed `todayKey()`** to `return _localDateKey()` — one-liner.

**Replaced `d.toISOString().slice(0,10)` at 9 activity-tracking sites:**

1. `getStreak()` — both the initial today/yesterday-rollback check AND the day-by-day backwards walk (lines ~650–660).
2. `isStreakAtRisk()` — today + yesterday keys (line ~665).
3. `useFreezeToken()` — yesterday key to freeze (line ~678).
4. Smart-recs daily-challenge date check (line ~929).
5. `initWordOfDay()` — today key for WOTD rotation (line ~4627).
6. Week-bars renderer — 7 days of `k2` keys (line ~2946).
7. Heatmap cells — 90 days of `key` keys (line ~2968).
8. Smart-recs pace-14 window — growth totals (line ~6879).
9. Profile stats pace window — same growth totals pattern (line ~7336).
10. Power-user stats day-counter (line ~10568).

File-download timestamps (lines 4216, 4263, 16098) intentionally left as UTC — filenames are cosmetic and UTC is universally parseable.

**Null-guard added to `updateStreak()`** — now wraps the `.textContent` / `.title` assignments in `if (el) { ... }`. The rest of the function (`updateFreezeButton()`, `checkStreakMilestone()`) still runs so freeze-button state and milestone toasts aren't suppressed just because the nav badge is temporarily absent.

### Why local timezone is the right call

The user's lived day is the local day. "Did I study today?" means today *to me*. A calendar-based streak that flips at midnight UTC feels broken to anyone not living in the UK/Lisbon/Reykjavik. All the activity UIs (heatmap, week-bars, "X days in a row") speak in terms of days-lived-by-the-user, so the key space must match.

### Why not offer a timezone picker

Unnecessary complexity. The browser already knows the user's local timezone (it's how `getDate()` works). A setting would just add config surface for no behavioral gain.

### Why leave file-download UTC timestamps alone

Export filenames like `lebanese-arabic-progress-2026-04-20.json` are identifiers, not activity tracking. UTC there is fine — actually slightly preferable for users who share exports across timezones.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js`:
  - Added `_localDateKey()` helper (~8 lines inline, line 630 region).
  - 10 inline edits replacing `d.toISOString().slice(0,10)` with `_localDateKey(d)` or `_localDateKey()` at activity-tracking sites.
  - 1 null-guard in `updateStreak()` wrapping DOM write (~3 lines).
- `_dev/probe.js` — 7 new CHECKs (1 function presence + 6 behavioral).

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → `OK — all 168 functions present` (was 167 → +1: `_localDateKey`).
- Behavioral CHECKs green:
  - `r58_todayKeyLocal` ✓ — `todayKey()` returns the local YYYY-MM-DD exactly.
  - `r58_localKeyFormat` ✓ — `_localDateKey(Date(2026,3,20))` = `'2026-04-20'`.
  - `r58_localKeyPadsDay` ✓ — single-digit months/days zero-padded.
  - `r58_getStreakUsesLocal` ✓ — `getStreak.toString()` contains `_localDateKey`.
  - `r58_updateStreakNullSafe` ✓ — `updateStreak()` does not throw when `nav-streak` is null.
  - `r58_recordActivityUsesLocal` ✓ — `recordActivity.toString()` contains the `todayKey` call (which now routes to `_localDateKey`).

**Bugs.rtf check:** Directly addresses *"Progress tracking straight up doesn't work"*. Combined with Run #53's JSON.parse hardening, the activity/streak subsystem is now both corruption-safe (Run #53) and timezone-correct (Run #58). Heatmap cells will now light up on the day the user actually studied, week-bars will place today in the right column, streaks won't mysteriously reset after late-evening sessions, and the "daily challenge done today" check matches the user's sense of "today."

## Run #59 — BUG FIX (parseInt NaN-safe localStorage readers)

**Category:** BUG FIX (59 % 3 == 2)
**Date:** 2026-04-20

### Problem (continued from bugs.rtf "Progress tracking straight up doesn't work")

Runs #53 (JSON.parse corruption guards) and #58 (local-timezone date keys) fixed two of the three progress-tracking root causes. The third: **raw `parseInt(localStorage.getItem(key) || '0')` sites** silently return `NaN` on corrupted values and then persist the corruption.

Failure pattern (real-world):

1. Some write path stores an invalid number — e.g. an in-flight `xp + delta` where `xp = parseInt(...)` returned `NaN`, giving `next = NaN + 5 = NaN`, then `localStorage.setItem('la_xp', String(NaN)) // 'NaN'`. This is permanent.
2. Next session: `parseInt('NaN', 10)` → `NaN`. All XP math breaks, level badge shows `NaN`, `amount+` arithmetic yields `NaN`, and every subsequent write re-saves `"NaN"`.
3. Same cascade for streak-freeze tokens (`la_freeze_tokens`), font-size index (`la_font_idx`), session size (`la_session_size`), daily goal (`la_daily_goal`).

Once corrupted, the counter is stuck until the user manually clears localStorage. From the user's perspective: "progress tracking straight up doesn't work" — XP stops accumulating, freeze tokens disappear, daily goal progress bar is broken.

Two existing sites (`getSrsNewLimit`, `getSrsReviewLimit`) already used the correct pattern (`const v = parseInt(...); return isNaN(v) ? Infinity : v;`). Everywhere else was missing the guard.

### Fix

**Added `_parseIntSafe(key, def)` helper** next to `_localDateKey` (~9 lines). Returns `def` when:
- `localStorage.getItem(key)` throws (private-mode edge cases).
- value is `null` (key not set).
- value is `''` (empty).
- `parseInt` returns a non-finite number (covers `"NaN"`, `"Infinity"`, `"abc"`, leading punctuation, etc.).

Returns the parsed integer otherwise. Uses `Number.isFinite(n)` rather than `isNaN(n)` because `isNaN` is lenient about non-number types that coerce to NaN — `Number.isFinite` rejects everything that isn't a finite real integer.

**Replaced all 7 raw parseInt(localStorage) read sites** with `_parseIntSafe(key, def)`:

1. Line 343 — `let sessionSize` top-level init.
2. Line 578 — `getDailyGoal()`.
3. Line 658 — `getFreezeTokens()`.
4. Line 1458 — `getXp()` (hottest path — hit on every card rating).
5. Line 4409 — `fontSizeIdx` top-level init.
6. Line 16358 — `isFirstRun()` internal XP check.
7. Line 16410 — welcome flow's `cur` daily-goal display.

Writes were left alone — because reads now never produce `NaN`, all downstream math (e.g. `prev + amount`, `tokens - 1`, `(fontSizeIdx + 1) % len`) can no longer yield non-finite values, so `String(next)` can no longer persist `"NaN"`. The corruption cycle is broken at the read layer, which is also the only layer a bad pre-existing value could enter from.

### Why a helper instead of inline isNaN checks

7 call sites, all identical shape (`key → integer with fallback`). DRY is cheap here and the helper is a tight 9-line function. The bigger win: anyone adding a new integer-keyed setting in future runs will naturally reach for the named helper, so this class of bug should not regress.

### Why `Number.isFinite` not `isNaN`

`isNaN("abc")` returns true (the string is coerced first). `Number.isFinite("abc")` returns false without coercion. They behave the same for most integer-parsing outcomes, but `Number.isFinite` more precisely says what we mean: *"is this a finite number I can do arithmetic on?"*. No downside, slightly better semantics.

### Why leave writes unguarded

Defense-in-depth could add `Number.isFinite` checks on the write side too, but:
1. Every write path now sources its value from a now-hardened read plus bounded arithmetic, so non-finite results require upstream bugs that don't currently exist.
2. Adding guards on ~7 write sites doubles the touched surface for a diminished return.
3. If a future write path somehow produces `NaN`, the next read recovers via the helper. Self-healing, no data loss beyond what was already corrupt.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js`:
  - 1 new helper `_parseIntSafe()` (~9 lines, adjacent to `_localDateKey()`).
  - 7 inline edits at the identified parseInt-localStorage sites.
- `_dev/probe.js` — 9 new CHECKs (1 function presence + 8 behavioral covering null/empty/"NaN"/garbage/valid inputs and the 3 hardened accessor functions).

## Run #60 — NEW FEATURE (Dialect Compare Drill)

**Category:** NEW FEATURE (60 % 3 == 0)
**Date:** 2026-04-20
**Prefix:** `dlc-`

### What it does

A side-by-side drill of Modern Standard Arabic (MSA — what textbooks and apps like Duolingo teach) against Lebanese colloquial (what's actually spoken). Directly addresses the #1 learning gap for anyone coming to Lebanese from formal Arabic classes: you can read a novel in MSA and still not understand a Beirut taxi driver.

Three tabs:

1. **Learn** — the full pair list grouped by 7 categories (question words, pronouns, present tense, negation, want/need, time & place, everyday phrases). Each pair shows MSA on the left with transliteration, Lebanese on the right with transliteration, English in the middle. Tap a pair to expand a short "why" note explaining the pattern (e.g. "Lebanese present uses b- prefix for habitual meaning; MSA has no b-").
2. **Drill** — multiple-choice quiz. Two direction toggles: MSA → Lebanese ("which is the Lebanese equivalent?"), or Lebanese → MSA (reverse). Shows the prompt phrase at 1.4rem with transliteration + English gloss, then 4 options. Distractors preferentially same-category (harder — tests that you know *which* "what" is Lebanese, not just that you know something is). After answering: correct option highlights green, wrong highlights red, explanation appears with the pair's note, then a Next button.
3. **Tips** — 7 pattern tips distilled from the pairs list ("Lebanese verbs often take b- prefix for present", "MSA ق often becomes glottal stop in Lebanese", etc.). These are the portable rules users can apply beyond the 41-item bank.

Session stats (correct/total with percentage) show in the header as you drill.

### Why this feature

- Bugs.rtf doesn't name this directly, but it's the highest-impact missing feature for the app's target use case (Lebanese dialect study). Existing features teach Lebanese *in isolation*. This one teaches Lebanese *against MSA*, which is how most learners actually encounter the distinction.
- Production-recall pressure: the drill isn't asking for comprehension of Lebanese. It's asking you to choose the right dialect — a tighter, more learnable task than open-ended translation.
- Pattern-level transfer: the Tips tab promotes rules over rote. After internalizing "ق → 2" the learner correctly guesses قلب → "2aleb" even if the word isn't in the bank.

### Data file: `data/run60-data.js`

- `DLC_PAIRS` — 41 pairs. Shape: `{id, cat, msa, lb, msaTr, lbTr, en, diff:1-3, note}`. Covers 7 categories with 4–13 pairs each. Every pair includes a one-sentence "why" explaining the pattern, not just the swap.
- `DLC_CATS` — 7 category descriptors `{id, label}`. Labels use emoji prefixes matching the app's visual style.
- `DLC_TIPS` — 7 portable rules (the patterns recurring across pairs).

41 pairs is the minimum for a non-repetitive drill session (random picker with 3 distractors each means you can play ~10 rounds without the same correct answer appearing twice).

### Module: `js/app.js` appendix (~165 lines)

State: `_dlcTab`, `_dlcMode` ('ms2lb' / 'lb2ms'), `_dlcCurrent`, `_dlcOpts`, `_dlcStats`, `_dlcLast`. All module-level `var` (matches existing appendix conventions; avoids TDZ in probe's `new Function` context).

Functions (7):
- `openDlc()` / `closeDlc()` — overlay toggle; `openDlc` bumps achievement counter with graceful `typeof` guard.
- `setDlcTab(t)` — renders tab bar, calls `renderDlc()`.
- `dlcNextItem()` — picks a random pair, builds 4-option set with `_dlcPickDistractors` (internal helper that prefers same-category distractors), Fisher-Yates shuffle.
- `dlcAnswer(idx)` — records result, increments stats, sets feedback state, re-renders.
- `dlcSetMode(mode)` — switches direction, immediately picks a new item.
- `renderDlc()` — dispatches on `_dlcTab`. All three tabs are self-contained HTML strings (app-style inline rendering).

Design notes in the code: Arabic-safe font stack (Run #56 legacy: `'Segoe UI','Noto Naskh Arabic','Amiri',system-ui,sans-serif` + `unicode-bidi:plaintext`) applied to every Arabic-script element. Direction `rtl` set on Arabic text. No localStorage — this is a session-scoped drill, stats reset on close.

### UI wiring

- `index.html` — study-topics row (the visible, non-legacy one above the 📚 modal): added button `🆚 MSA vs Lebanese` next to `⌨️ Type It`. Overlay added before the REVERSE TRANSLATION OVERLAY anchor. Script tag `data/run60-data.js` added before `js/app.js`.

## Run #61 — AUDIO (variant-expansion lookup)

**Category:** AUDIO (61 % 3 == 1)
**Date:** 2026-04-20

### Problem (from bugs.rtf)

*"A lot of words are still missing proper audio."*

Data-side coverage is one dimension of this (more recordings). But a lot of apparent gaps are actually **lookup-key mismatches** against recordings that already exist. Examples:

- `YOUTUBE_AUDIO` has an entry for `"قلب"` (heart). User sees the word in a sentence as `"القلب"` (definite-article form, "the heart") → miss.
- `YOUTUBE_AUDIO` has `"اهلا"`. User-facing text uses Hamza variant `"أهلا"` → miss.
- `YOUTUBE_AUDIO` has `"ست"`. Sentence chunker produces `"ست،"` with trailing comma → Run #55 fixed punctuation strip. But the reverse also exists: recording stored as `"ست،"` (from an older scrape), text asks for `"ست"` → Run #55 fixed that direction too. Not today's gap.

The missing variant after Runs #55 / #25: **definite-article stripping**. Arabic nouns extremely commonly appear with/without `"ال"` (the). A single recording should serve both forms. Before Run #61, the lookup chain was:

1. raw text
2. punctuation-stripped (Run #55)
3. normalized hamza/ya/ta-marbuta on raw
4. normalized on stripped

But `ال` stripping was nowhere. And each fallback was called individually with subtly-different code branches in `_hasAudioFor` vs `_audioUrlFor`, making it easy to miss a combination (e.g. `cache[norm]` wasn't actually checked in the old impl — only `YOUTUBE_AUDIO[norm]` was).

### Fix

**Added `_audioKeyVariants(text)` helper** that emits a single ordered, de-duplicated list of all lookup keys to try. Current variants (in priority order):

1. Raw text.
2. Punctuation-stripped (Run #55 behavior preserved).
3. Hamza/ya/ta-marbuta normalized (Run #25 behavior preserved).
4. Normalized + punctuation-stripped.
5. Definite-article `ال` stripped from front (new this run).
6. Stripped + def-article-stripped.
7. Normalized + def-article-stripped.

Dedup via a seen-set, so callers get a tight list without redundant lookups.

The `ال` strip only fires when the remaining stem would be >1 character (guards against pathological keys like `"الم"` where stripping turns a 3-char word into 1-char). Arabic words genuinely shorter than 4 chars are rare enough that false-positive collisions (e.g. a real word `"الم"` colliding with an unrelated `"م"` entry) would outweigh coverage gains.

**Rewrote `_hasAudioFor` and `_audioUrlFor`** as straight iterations over `_audioKeyVariants()`. Replaces ~12 lines of branching code per function with ~8 lines of tight loops. Same priority semantics: `YOUTUBE_AUDIO` beats cache; within each, earlier variants beat later.

### Why a variant list instead of adding more per-site fallbacks

Single source of truth. Any future variant (e.g. feminine-marker ة→ه stripping, vowel-diacritic stripping) can be added by extending `_audioKeyVariants()` — both callers immediately benefit. No risk of `_hasAudioFor` returning `true` while `_audioUrlFor` returns `null` due to diverged fallback paths, which was possible (though not observed) in the pre-Run-#61 code.

### Why not strip `ال` wherever it could appear (mid-word)

Only leading `ال` carries definite-article meaning. Mid-word `ال` is coincidental letter sequence (e.g. inside `"سلام"` — nobody thinks stripping there is useful). Keep the strip positional.

### Why keep Run #55's `_audioKey` / `_stripAudioPunct` exposed

They're called from Run #55-era code elsewhere (the `speak()` lookup sites). Keeping them lets the variant generator reuse them (`stripped = _audioKey(text)`) without touching the other call sites.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js`:
  - 1 new helper `_audioKeyVariants()` (~20 lines).
  - Rewrote `_hasAudioFor()` — now 8 lines, down from ~14.
  - Rewrote `_audioUrlFor()` — now 11 lines, down from ~13.
- `_dev/probe.js` — 10 new CHECKs (1 function presence + 9 behavioral covering variant generation, dedup, def-article round-trip, normalization round-trip, short-word guard).

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → `OK — all 177 functions present` (was 176 → +1: `_audioKeyVariants`).
- Behavioral CHECKs green:
  - `r61_variantsIncludeRaw` ✓ — `قلب` in its own variants.
  - `r61_variantsIncludePunctStripped` ✓ — `قلب؟` → variants contain `قلب`.
  - `r61_variantsIncludeDefArticleStripped` ✓ — `القلب` → variants contain `قلب`.
  - `r61_variantsIncludeNormalized` ✓ — `أهلا` → variants contain normalized `اهلا`.
  - `r61_variantsDedupe` ✓ — no duplicate keys in the list.
  - `r61_hasAudioDefArticle` ✓ — seeded `STEM` entry is found via `ال+STEM` lookup.
  - `r61_urlForDefArticle` ✓ — same round-trip returns the stubbed URL exactly.
  - `r61_hasAudioNormalized` ✓ — seeded `اهلا` entry is found via `أهلا` lookup.
  - `r61_doesntStripShortWord` ✓ — `الم` does not get stripped to `م` (short-word guard active).

**Bugs.rtf check:** Directly addresses *"A lot of words are still missing proper audio"* at the lookup layer. Vocab entries that differ from recording keys only by article-prefix or hamza-variant now resolve to the real recording instead of falling to TTS / "no audio". Users won't see coverage numbers change (the recording count is the same), but the sentence-builder's *effective* audio hit rate should rise — especially for chunks bearing the `ال` prefix, which the segmenter emits whenever the sentence text uses the definite form.
