## Run #62 — BUG FIX (Phrases tab audio — variant-aware `speak()`)

**Category:** BUG FIX (62 % 3 == 2)
**Date:** 2026-04-20

### Problem (from bugs.rtf)

*"Phrases tab audio doesn't work."*

Symptom: tapping 🔊 on a phrasebook entry often produces silence or falls through to "No Lebanese audio" even when a recording genuinely exists for the same word under a slightly different key. Examples surfaced during manual testing:

- Phrase stored as `"أهلاً"` (with hamza-over-alif + fatha tanween). `YOUTUBE_AUDIO` has the recording under `"اهلا"` (bare alif, no tanween). **Silently missed.**
- Phrase stored as `"القلب"` (with definite article). Recording under `"قلب"`. **Silently missed.**
- Phrase stored as `"كيفك؟"` (Arabic question mark). Recording under `"كيفك"`. This one *did* work — Run #55 fixed punctuation via `_audioKey` — but only because the punctuation case was already routed through `_audioKey`. The hamza/ال cases bypass that.

Why it slipped past Run #61: Run #61 added `_audioKeyVariants` / `_hasAudioFor` / `_audioUrlFor` that handle all these variants, but `speak()` — the entry point for every 🔊 button in the app — was written before Run #61 and still did raw 2-key lookups:

```js
// speak() line 3654 before Run #62:
const ytLocal = YOUTUBE_AUDIO[key] || YOUTUBE_AUDIO[text];
// speak() line 3665 before Run #62:
const cached = cache[key] || cache[text];
// speak() line 3635 before Run #62:
const wholeHasAudio = YOUTUBE_AUDIO[text] || (audioCache()[text] && audioCache()[text] !== '__none__');
```

Two keys (`text` = raw, `key` = punctuation-stripped). Run #61's normalized + ال-stripped variants were never tried. Effect: phrase audio hit rate was capped at whatever `_audioKey` could fix (punctuation only), despite the richer lookup table already being available.

### Fix

Three new helper functions mirror `_audioUrlFor` / `_hasAudioFor` but return **both the URL and the matched variant key**. `speak()` needs the matched key (not just the URL) because the dialect side-cache (`'__dialect__:' + k`) and various `_lastWiktDialect` / block-list checks are all keyed by the exact string that matched.

- `_audioYtMatchFor(text)` → `{ key, url }` or `null`. Walks Run #61 variants, returns the first YOUTUBE_AUDIO hit with the key that matched.
- `_audioCacheMatchFor(text, cache)` → `{ key, url, dialect }`, or `{ key, url: null, miss: true }` if a variant is explicitly cached as `'__none__'`, or `null` if absent. The `miss` shape surfaces cached negative results so `speak()` can short-circuit the live Wiktionary lookup for known misses.
- `_audioCommonsMatchFor(text, cache)` → same shape as cache match, scoped to the `'__commons__:'` prefix.

`speak()` now uses these helpers with a graceful typeof guard and a **fallback to the pre-#62 2-key lookup** if the helper is somehow unavailable. The guards matter because `speak()` is called from many sites (including during app init before all appendix funcs are attached); falling back to the old behavior means the worst case is what we had before, not a crash.

Specific lines changed in `speak()`:

- **Line 3635** — `wholeHasAudio` check. Was `YOUTUBE_AUDIO[text] || cache[text]`. Now `_hasAudioFor(text)`. Widens the skip-speakSmart decision from 1 key to 7 variants. Impact: multi-word phrases with a whole-phrase recording stored under a normalized key now play the single clip instead of being chunked into word-by-word TTS.
- **Line 3654** — `ytLocal` assignment. Was `YOUTUBE_AUDIO[key] || YOUTUBE_AUDIO[text]`. Now tries `_audioYtMatchFor(text)` first.
- **Line 3665** — `cached` / `cachedDialect` assignment. Was 2-key cache read. Now variant-aware via `_audioCacheMatchFor`. Dialect resolution follows the matched key so the badge still shows the right 🇱🇧/🇸🇾/📚 marker.
- **Line 3718** — Commons cache read. Was `cache['__commons__:' + key] || cache['__commons__:' + text]`. Now variant-aware via `_audioCommonsMatchFor`.

### Why a separate `*MatchFor` helper instead of reusing `_audioUrlFor`

`_audioUrlFor(text)` returns just the URL. `speak()` needs the matched key for:
1. Dialect side-cache lookup (`cache['__dialect__:' + k]`).
2. `_lastWiktDialect[k]` lookup for labeling post-fetch.

Reusing `_audioUrlFor` would mean a second pass through the variants to re-discover which key won, which is both redundant and error-prone (if the two passes diverge, the badge shows the wrong dialect). Returning `{key, url}` is the cleaner contract.

Also, the cache path needs to distinguish "no entry at all" vs "entry explicitly cached as `__none__`" — the former should fall through to live Wiktionary, the latter should skip it. `_audioUrlFor` collapses both to `null`. `_audioCacheMatchFor` surfaces the miss via `{miss: true}`.

### Why keep the 2-key fallback

Belt-and-braces. If a future refactor removes or renames `_audioKeyVariants`, or if this code somehow loads before the appendix, the old behavior is preserved. The cost is ~30 bytes of fallback code per call site. Worth it.

### Why not also patch `segmentSentence`

`segmentSentence` already uses `_hasAudioFor` and `_audioUrlFor` — it was built correctly against Run #61's API from the start. No change needed there.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js`:
  - 3 new helpers `_audioYtMatchFor`, `_audioCacheMatchFor`, `_audioCommonsMatchFor` (~45 lines, appended right after `_audioUrlFor`).
  - 4 inline edits in `speak()` (lines 3635, 3654, 3665, 3718) to use the helpers with 2-key fallbacks.
- `_dev/probe.js` — 3 function-presence CHECKs + 9 behavioral CHECKs covering: YT variant match returns `{key,url}`; YT match returns null on miss; YT match normalizes hamza; cache match via ال; cache match surfaces `__none__` as `miss`; cache match returns null for absent; commons variant match; commons `__none__` → `miss`; positive hit beats `__none__` hit in the variant list; returned `.key` is the *matched* variant, not the caller's input string.

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → `OK — all 180 functions present` (was 177 → +3 new helpers).
- All 12 new CHECKs green. All prior CHECKs remain green.

### Bugs.rtf check

Directly addresses *"Phrases tab audio doesn't work"* at the dispatch layer. Every 🔊 button in the Phrases tab calls `speak(p.ar)`. Each of those calls now routes through variant-aware lookup for YOUTUBE_AUDIO, Wiktionary cache, and Commons cache — the three sources that serve the vast majority of phrase hits. Users should see `🎬 Lebanese speaker (YouTube)` or `🎙 Wiktionary` badges appear for phrases that previously silently fell to TTS or "no audio".

Also incidentally improves:
- Vocab flashcard audio (same `speak()` entry point).
- Any overlay with a 🔊 button (survival phrasebook, religious phrases, sentence builder single-shot replay).
- Reduces unnecessary Wiktionary live fetches: when a variant is cached as `__none__`, that miss is now seen regardless of which variant the caller used.

Remaining audio items:
- Data-side coverage ("add more recordings") — still outstanding.
- Phrase-level recordings for longer multi-word phrases — currently most are chunked via speakSmart.

**Cumulative state:**
- `js/app.js`: ~18,710 lines (+~50 helpers, 4 inline edits).
- `_dev/probe.js`: +12 CHECKs (136 behavioral + 180 funcs).
- Verified functions: 180 (+3).

## Run #63 — NEW FEATURE (Proverb Completion drill)

**Category:** NEW FEATURE (63 % 3 == 0)
**Date:** 2026-04-20

### Feature

Four-tab drill that turns the existing 65-proverb `PROVERBS` dataset into a real learning surface. Previously proverbs only existed as a scrollable browse list in `view=proverbs`. This run adds:

1. **Learn** — same browse-list UI but with category filter chips (All / Wisdom / Life / Speech / etc.). Each card shows Arabic (large, RTL + Arabic-safe font), transliteration, literal gloss, meaning, and when-to-use context. Cards are visually consistent with the Dialect Compare (Run #60) card style.
2. **Complete** — first-half / second-half drill. Shows the opening clause of a proverb (with transliteration), learner picks the closing clause from 4 options. Distractors are real second-halves from other proverbs, deduped so two distractors never display identical text.
3. **Situation** — English scenario → proverb match. Shows a one-sentence real-life scenario from the new `PC_SITUATIONS` bank. Learner picks which proverb fits. Distractors prefer same-category proverbs, fall back to any-category when needed.
4. **Tips** — 7 portable meta-rules about how Lebanese speakers actually use proverbs (split patterns, social register, when rhyming/parallelism helps memorization).

Session stats (correct/total with %) shown in the header bar as you drill.

### Why this feature

- Proverbs are high-value social currency in Lebanese — dropping the right one at the right moment signals fluency in a way vocabulary alone doesn't. But learners see them as decorative content in browse lists rather than something to retrieve on demand.
- The Complete tab tests **memory of the closing clause** — the hardest part of a proverb to produce. First halves tend to carry the image (patience, time, smoke); second halves carry the resolution (relief, gold, fire). Learners recognize the image faster than they produce the resolution, so drilling the gap is where real retention happens.
- The Situation tab tests **mapping from context to proverb** — the production-side skill that separates "I know what this means" from "I know when to say this." The scenarios are written to be culturally plausible (job interviews, family dinners, traffic, permits) rather than abstract.
- Both drills are tight round-trips (4 options, single click, feedback + Next). No typing, no complex state. High iteration count per minute.

### Data file: `data/run63-data.js`

- `PC_SITUATIONS` — 25 English scenarios. Shape: `{id, scenario, proverbId}`. Each `proverbId` references a real id in `PROVERBS`. A probe CHECK enforces referential integrity so future proverb-bank edits can't silently break this drill.
- `PC_TIPS` — 7 meta-rules, displayed in the Tips tab.

25 scenarios is the minimum for a non-repetitive session (random picker means roughly one pass of unique prompts before repetition). Several high-frequency proverbs (patience, smoke-fire, patience-delay, caught-laughing-last) intentionally get 2+ scenarios so learners encounter them in multiple contexts.

### Module: `js/app.js` appendix (~265 lines)

State: `_pcTab` (learn / complete / situation / tips), `_pcCatFilter`, `_pcCurrent` (for Complete), `_pcScenCurrent` (for Situation), `_pcOpts`, `_pcLast`, `_pcStats`. All module-level `var` (appendix convention; avoids TDZ in probe's `new Function` context).

Functions (10):
- `openPc()` / `closePc()` — overlay toggle, `openPc` bumps achievement counter with `typeof` guard.
- `setPcTab(t)` — renders tab bar, kicks off the relevant drill's first item when switching to Complete / Situation.
- `_pcSplitProverb(ar)` — splits a proverb into halves. Tries Arabic comma (`،`), ASCII comma, space-waw (` و`), then midpoint whitespace fallback. Returns `null` for too-short proverbs so the Complete picker can skip them.
- `_pcShuffle(arr)` — Fisher-Yates on a copy (doesn't mutate input).
- `pcNextComplete()` — filters `PROVERBS` to splittable ones, picks a random proverb, builds a 4-option set with 3 deduped distractor second-halves.
- `pcAnswerComplete(idx)` — records result, increments stats (`complete` counter), sets `_pcLast`, re-renders.
- `pcNextSituation()` — picks a random `PC_SITUATIONS` entry, resolves its `proverbId`, builds 4 options with same-category-preferring distractors.
- `pcAnswerSituation(idx)` — same shape as answer-complete but increments `situation` counter.
- `pcSetCatFilter(cat)` — Learn-tab category filter.
- `renderPc()` — dispatches on `_pcTab`, renders each tab as a self-contained HTML string (matches the app's inline-rendering style).

### Design notes

- **Arabic-safe font stack applied to every Arabic-script element.** The `ARFONT` constant inside `renderPc` holds `font-family:'Segoe UI','Noto Naskh Arabic','Amiri',system-ui,sans-serif;unicode-bidi:plaintext;direction:rtl`. This is the fix from Run #56 that unblocks Arabic display on macOS Safari. Every proverb display (Learn card, Complete prompt, Complete options, Situation option labels, feedback card) carries it.

## Run #64 — AUDIO (Tashkeel-strip audio variant)

**Category:** AUDIO (64 % 3 == 1)
**Date:** 2026-04-20

### Problem (from bugs.rtf)

*"A lot of words are still missing proper audio."*

Runs #55 / #25 / #61 / #62 widened the variant list to cover punctuation, hamza / ya / ta-marbuta normalization, definite-article stripping. One major gap remained: **Arabic diacritics (tashkeel)**.

Diacritics commonly appear in:
- Beginner vocabulary lists (`أَهْلاً` rather than `اهلا`)
- Proverb corpora (`العَقْل زينة`)
- Qur'anic or religious text
- Dictionary-style entries
- Anything pasted from Wikipedia / Wiktionary (which often preserves the diacritized form)

Recording keys, by contrast, are almost universally stored **undiacritized** (the recording corpus was built from colloquial transliteration-first sources). Result: a learner studying a card that reads `أَهْلاً كيف حالكَ` hits the 🔊 button, and the variant chain generated by Run #61 is:

```
أَهْلاً كيف حالكَ
أهلاً كيف حالكَ  (punctuation strip — no punct here, same)
اهلاً كيف حالكَ  (hamza normalize — but tashkeel survives)
اهلاً كيف حالكَ  (+ punct strip — same)
… (def-article variants, none help here)
```

None of those match the recording stored under `اهلا كيف حالك`. Silent miss.

### Fix

Added `_stripTashkeel(s)` — a 3-line helper that replaces all 9 standard Arabic diacritic codepoints + tatweel + superscript-alif (dagger alif `ٰ`, U+0670) with empty string.

Codepoints covered:
- U+064B fathatan `ً`
- U+064C dammatan `ٌ`
- U+064D kasratan `ٍ`
- U+064E fatha `َ`
- U+064F damma `ُ`
- U+0650 kasra `ِ`
- U+0651 shadda `ّ`
- U+0652 sukun `ْ`
- U+0640 tatweel `ـ` (kashida elongation — visual stretch, no phonetic content)
- U+0670 superscript alif `ٰ` (dagger alif, used in a handful of words like `هَٰذا`)

Single regex, one pass, no normalization table needed — purely drop-some-codepoints.

**Refactored `_audioKeyVariants()`** so the existing 8-variant ladder (raw / strip / norm / norm+strip × {untouched, def-article-stripped}) is extracted into an inner `addLayer(t)` helper. Then the outer function calls `addLayer(text)` once, and — **only if the input actually carried tashkeel** — calls `addLayer(_stripTashkeel(text))` as a second pass. The dedup set naturally collapses any overlap, so a bare-input word still produces exactly 8 variants, while a diacritized word produces up to 16.

### Why the refactor rather than inline the 8 extra calls

Every time we add a new variant dimension (hamza, def-article, tashkeel, and inevitably feminine-ta-swap or kasra-i-to-y-shift in the future), we need all the cross-products with existing dimensions. Inlining 16 `add(stripDef(stripTashkeel(norm(strip(text)))))`-shaped calls is unmaintainable. The `addLayer` indirection lets us treat tashkeel as a **preprocessor** rather than another node in the product — future dimensions that belong at the same level (stripping vowel-ya before matching) slot in as sibling preprocessors without combinatorial expansion of the function body.

### Why not strip tashkeel unconditionally in `_audioKey`

`_audioKey` is reused by many call sites outside the variant generator (e.g., the `speak()` raw-key fallback, dialect side-cache key construction, `_lastWiktDialect` lookups). Changing its output would require a user's existing cache to re-key itself or become invisible until re-fetched. The variant list is the safer place because callers iterate it looking for *any* hit — adding more keys is non-breaking, mutating existing keys is.

Also: for `speak()` to render a dialect badge correctly, it needs to know **which exact key** a recording was found under. `_audioKey` stays the primary "canonical" key; tashkeel-stripped keys are strictly additional probes.

### Why `U+0670` (dagger alif) even though it's rare

Non-zero cost to include, zero cost to exclude. But the word `هَٰذا` ("this") is extremely high-frequency — it appears in hundreds of sentences in the data, and some sources preserve the superscript alif. Including U+0670 means one regex char, no measurable perf hit, and catches a real-world case.

### Why tatweel (U+0640) belongs in the tashkeel strip

Tatweel is not a diacritic, but it has the same character — purely visual, no phonetic content. `مرحـــبا` and `مرحبا` are pronounced identically. Any string that contains tatweel almost certainly won't match the recording key without stripping. Including tatweel in the same regex reuses the replacement pass.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js`:
  - New `_AUDIO_TASHKEEL_RE` regex + `_stripTashkeel(s)` helper (~10 lines).
  - Rewrote `_audioKeyVariants()` around an inner `addLayer(t)` closure; outer adds bare-text layer, then tashkeel-free layer only if the text carried any. Functionally a superset — no call site loses coverage.
- `_dev/probe.js` — 13 new CHECKs:
  - 1 function-presence (`_stripTashkeel`).
  - 7 strip-behavior unit tests (fathatan, shadda, fatha+damma+kasra combo, tatweel, dagger alif, bare word left alone, null/undefined/empty safety).
  - 2 variant-list integration tests (diacritized input produces tashkeel-free variant; diacritized + def-article combo produces bare stem).
  - 2 dedup tests (bare input: no dupes; diacritized input: no dupes).
  - 2 round-trip tests (seeded `YOUTUBE_AUDIO` stub key hit via diacritized query through `_hasAudioFor` and `_audioUrlFor`).

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → `OK — all 191 functions present` (was 190 → +1: `_stripTashkeel`).
- All 13 new CHECKs green. All prior CHECKs remain green.

### Bugs.rtf check

Extends Runs #55 / #25 / #61 / #62's variant coverage to tashkeel-bearing inputs. Words that appear diacritized in vocab cards, proverbs, dictation sources, or reading passages now hit the same recording as their bare-consonant form would. No new recordings added — pure lookup-layer improvement.

Also flows downstream:
- `_hasAudioFor` / `_audioUrlFor` (Run #61): automatic (they iterate the variant list).
- `speakSmart` / `segmentSentence` (already built on `_hasAudioFor`): automatic — diacritized chunks from dictation now play the recording instead of dropping to TTS / silent skip.
- Run #62's `_audioYtMatchFor` / `_audioCacheMatchFor` / `_audioCommonsMatchFor`: automatic (they iterate the variant list).

## Run #65 — Register missing topics in menu (BUG FIX)

The 📚 All Topics modal is the canonical surface for discovering features — powered by `TOPICS_CATEGORIES`. But many features added in recent runs (Csw, Rt, Dlc, Pc, Qf, DialogueComp, Etym, Dialect, Survival, Names, Songs, Phone, Flirt, AudioDiagnose) existed only as functions + inline study-row buttons. They never got registered in `TOPICS_CATEGORIES`, so searching or browsing the modal never surfaced them. Users with many features installed hit the "Menu items don't fit properly" complaint in `bugs.rtf` — the real fix isn't CSS tweaks, it's directing users to the searchable modal instead of scrolling a cluttered row.

### Fix

Added 14 entries to `TOPICS_CATEGORIES` across the 6 base categories:

## Run #66 — Sentence Pattern Drill (NEW FEATURE)

### Feature

**`SPD_PATTERNS`** (20) + **`SPD_EXERCISES`** (26) + **`SPD_TIPS`** (8) — high-frequency Lebanese sentence templates with a single slot (___) plus fill-in-the-blank drills tied to each pattern.

Three-tab overlay:
- **📖 Learn**: browse all 20 patterns — see template (`ما بقدر ___`), translit (`ma b2dir ___`), English meaning ("I can't ___"), category, register
- **🎯 Drill**: fill-in-the-blank. User sees English gloss + Arabic sentence with blank, picks correct word from 4 options. Shuffled order, score tracked
- **💡 Tips**: 8 portable takeaways about the patterns (why `بدي` doesn't take an infinitive, why Lebanese questions don't invert, etc.)

### Patterns included

- **Modals**: ما بقدر (can't), لازم (must), ممكن (may I), بدي (want)
- **Tense**: عم + verb (progressive), رح + verb (future), كنت + adj (was), بعدني + adj (still am), صار (became)
- **Existence/Possession**: ما في / في (no/is there), عندي / ما عندي (have / don't have)
- **Questions**: شو/ليش/كيف/وين ___
- **Conditional/Wish**: إذا ___ بخبرك, يا ريت ___
- **Reference**: بالنسبة لـ___ (formal register)

### Why patterns over isolated vocab

The pedagogical rationale: ~10 frozen templates cover the grammatical skeleton of most daily Lebanese speech. Learners who know `بدي + verb` can generate infinite new sentences; learners who know 200 verbs without the template can't say "I want to eat." The drill explicitly separates the template from the content-word slot so the learner internalizes the skeleton first and then fills it.

## Run #67 — Audio variant: strip clitic prefixes/suffixes (AUDIO)

### Problem

`bugs.rtf` line: *"A lot of words are still missing proper audio."* One mechanical cause: Lebanese glues short particles onto the next word with no space. Text says `بحبو` ("I love him"), but the recording is keyed as `حب` (the bare stem). Prior variant work (Run #61 def-article strip, Run #64 tashkeel strip) covers two major classes but leaves the whole clitic family untouched. Every unstripped proclitic or enclitic is a silent audio miss.

### Fix

Extended `_audioKeyVariants()` with two new in-function helpers and three new addLayer branches:

**`stripProcliticPrefix(s)`** — strips leading Lebanese clitic particles:
- Single-letter (when length > 3): `و` (and), `ب` (at/imperfect), `ف` (so/then), `ل` (to/for), `س` (future)
- Two-letter (when length > 4): `ما` (negation), `رح` (future), `عم` (progressive)

**`stripPronounSuffix(s)`** — strips trailing pronoun clitics:
- Two-letter (when length ≥ 5): `ـها` (her), `ـنا` (our), `ـكم/ـكن` (your-pl), `ـهم/ـهن` (their)
- Single-letter (when length ≥ 4): `ـي` (my), `ـك` (your-m), `ـه` (his-MSA), `ـو` (his-Leb)

**Combined strip**: if proclitic strip fired, also try stripping a pronoun suffix from the result (`بحبو` → `حب`).

All stripped forms are pushed through the existing `_normalizeArabicWord` and `stripDef` pipeline, so a variant like `وكتابها` expands into the full cross-product: `وكتابها`, `كتابها`, `كتاب`, normalized versions, def-article-stripped versions, etc. The dedup set `seen{}` prevents redundancy.

### Why these particular particles

These are the eight highest-frequency Lebanese clitics by token count (rough ranking: `و` > `ب` > `ما` > `ل` > `عم` > `رح` > `ف` > `س`). Together they prefix the vast majority of verb-carrying utterances in everyday speech. Enclitic pronouns (10 forms) exhaust all 8 Lebanese pronouns plus MSA/Lebanese variants of "his" (`ـه` vs `ـو`).

### Why the length guards matter

Lebanese has many legitimate short words that **start** with these letters but aren't clitics:
- `ماي` (water) — length 3, `ما` strip requires length > 4, safe
- `بيت` (house) — length 3, `ب` strip requires length > 3, safe (only strips from `بكتاب` etc.)
- `في` (in) — length 2, no strip fires
- `شك` (doubt) — length 2, no suffix strip

The min-length guards are hard-coded rather than configurable because the "sweet spot" depends on Lebanese-specific word shapes. Validated with `r67_doesntStripMay` check (probe crashes if `ماي` would be stripped to `ي`).

### Files touched

- `js/app.js`:
  - `_audioKeyVariants()` body: +2 helper fns (`stripProcliticPrefix`, `stripPronounSuffix`), +3 addLayer branches (proclitic, enclitic, combined)
  - ~50 lines added
- `_dev/probe.js` — 20 new CHECKs:
  - 8 prefix-strip unit tests (و/ب/ف/ل/س/ما/رح/عم)
  - 6 suffix-strip unit tests (ي/ك/و/ها/نا/هم)
  - 1 combined prefix+suffix test (بكتابي → كتاب)
  - 1 min-length preservation test (في stays 1-variant)
  - 1 false-positive guard (ماي doesn't strip to ي)
  - 1 dedup test (no duplicate variants on complex input)
  - 2 round-trip tests (seeded YOUTUBE_AUDIO stub key hit via prefixed/suffixed query through _hasAudioFor and _audioUrlFor)

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → `OK — all 197 functions present` (unchanged — no new top-level functions, inner helpers only)
- All 20 new CHECKs green on first run

Primary: **"A lot of words are still missing proper audio"** — directly mechanical. Every verb that appears in text with `ب` / `عم` / `رح` / `ما` prefix (which is most verbs in most sentences) now has a fallback variant path to the bare-stem recording. Every noun in possessive form (`كتابي`, `بيتو`, `أمها`) now fallbacks to the bare-noun recording.

## Run #68 — Progress tracking doesn't update live (BUG FIX)

### Problem

Top-line complaint from `bugs.rtf`: *"Progress tracking straight up doesn't work."* Verified by tracing the review path:

1. User rates a flashcard → `rate()` → `recordActivity()` → `updateStreak()` (streak chip only)
2. `nav-due` chip stays stale (still shows pre-review count — card just reviewed should be removed from due)
3. `nav-total` (words learned) stays stale
4. `nav-xp-badge` was actually fine because `addXp()` calls `updateXpBadge()` independently — but not all rate paths go through addXp (wrong answers don't)
5. `today-dashboard` (the hero panel with "X/Y goal" progress ring) stays stale
6. Stats tab stat-cards "Words Learned / Due Now / Current Streak / Total Reviews" stay stale until user leaves the tab and returns

Trace of `updateNavStats` callers before the fix: `init`, `resetProgress`, `importData` — but not `recordActivity`. So the only way for nav-due to update was to navigate away and back to the Study view, which retriggers the init chain indirectly. Matches exactly what the user reports.

### Fix

In `js/app.js` `recordActivity()` (~line 655):

1. Replaced the direct `updateStreak()` call with `updateNavStats()` — which internally already does `updateStreak()` plus refreshes nav-due, nav-total, nav-xp-badge, and `renderTodayDashboard()`. Single source of truth for "review just happened; refresh everything the user can see."
2. Added a fallback: if `updateNavStats` isn't defined yet (can happen during very early init before the function hoists in exotic environments), fall back to the original `updateStreak()` call. Belt-and-suspenders.
3. Added a second branch: if the Stats view is currently `.active` (user is sitting on it while reviewing cards from elsewhere — e.g. quiz mode which can be accessed while stats tab is open in another pane), re-run `renderStats()` so the stat-cards, badges, and weekly chart update in place.

The second branch is the non-obvious part: `renderStats` is expensive (it rebuilds ~40 stat-cards + 5 badge groups + charts), so we only call it if the user is actually looking at it. The `.contains('active')` check makes this a no-op in the common case.

### Why not just call `updateNavStats()` at every rate site

There are 9 `recordActivity()` call sites (main rate, sentence rate, phrase rate, quiz-correct, quiz-type-correct, scramble-correct, plus 3 more per-feature drills). Adding `updateNavStats()` at all 9 is call-site churn + future drills would miss it. Putting it inside `recordActivity` means every current and future path that logs activity automatically refreshes the UI. One place to maintain.

### Why `la_activity` storage logic stayed identical

No change to the activity-writing code — this fix is purely about UI refresh. The bug wasn't that activity wasn't being recorded (it was), it was that the UI wasn't re-reading it.

## Run #69 — Dialogue Pragmatics Drill (NEW FEATURE)

### Feature

**`DPR_ITEMS`** (18) + **`DPR_TIPS`** (7) — pragmatics/subtext drill. Each item is a common Lebanese expression whose surface translation diverges from what a native speaker actually means by it. User sees the Arabic sentence + translit + literal gloss, then picks the real implication from 4 options.

Three-tab overlay:
- **📖 Learn**: browse all 18 expressions with their correct implication pre-revealed and a cultural/usage note
- **🎯 Quiz**: one at a time, 4-option multiple choice. Options shuffled each question. Score tracked (correct/total)
- **💡 Tips**: 7 portable takeaways about Lebanese pragmatics (tone > vocabulary, deferral formulas default to soft-no, etc.)

### Expressions included

- Deflection/deferral: `بكرا الصبح`, `بعدين منشوف`, `إن شاء الله` (context-dependent)
- Polite brush-off: `ولا يهمك`, `ما عليك`, `ما في مشكلة`, `هيدا عادي`
- Agreement/enthusiasm: `تكرم عيونك`
- Confrontation/challenge: `شو قصدك؟`, `شو هالقصة؟`
- Confirmation/surprise: `عن جد؟`
- Imperative softening: `روق`, `يا الله`
- Idiom with opaque literal: `إجت معي` ("fortune smiled"), `شو بدي قلك` (rhetorical sigh)
- Attention-grab: `لك شو`
- Face-save: `عم بمزح`
- Tone-dependent: `قديش حلو` (genuine vs sarcastic)

### Why a pragmatics feature specifically

Existing features teach vocabulary, grammar, fixed phrases, situational dialog. None teach **pragmatic competence** — the listener-side skill of reading what's meant vs what's said. Vocabulary says "بكرا الصبح" means "tomorrow morning"; pragmatic competence says it usually doesn't. A learner with 2000-word vocabulary but weak pragmatics can still miss half the meaning in a normal Lebanese conversation, because so much daily speech runs on idiom + tone + cultural convention rather than literal composition.

The 4-option multiple-choice format forces the learner to commit to one reading, and the distractors are constructed to be plausible but wrong (literal readings of the surface form, or readings from other contexts) — so guessing doesn't work. The learn tab shows the full note afterward, so wrong answers in the quiz get explained in context.

Run #68 patched the `rate()` and quiz paths, but 6 other drill modes scored "correct" without ever calling `recordActivity()` / `incDailyCount()`. From the user's perspective, "I just answered 20 minimal pairs correctly and the dashboard still says 0 reviews today" = "progress tracking doesn't work."

**Fix**: 7 surgical patches to `js/app.js`:

|------|----------|------|--------|
| Minimal pairs drill | `mpAnswer` | 4636 | `+ recordActivity(); incDailyCount();` on correct |
| Grammar exercises | `gex*Answer` | 5394 | `+ recordActivity(); incDailyCount();` on correct |
| Conversation challenge | `answerChallenge` | 6076 | `+ recordActivity(); incDailyCount();` on correct |
| Passage quiz | `answerPassageQ` | 8001 | `+ recordActivity(); incDailyCount();` on correct |

Also a defensive guard added to `_pushAudioHistory` (line 18436): re-init `_audioPlaybackHistory = []` if it's undefined or non-array. The user observation "progress tracking doesn't work" sounds like a state/render problem, but the actual cause is a **counting** problem: the events that should count as "I studied something" never reached the counter. Once they do, all the downstream surfaces (Today dashboard, streak chip, XP bar, heatmap) already work — Run #68 made sure those re-render on `recordActivity`. ## Run #72 — Loanword Spotter (NEW FEATURE)

**Category**: NEW FEATURES (72%3==0)

**Feature**: Identify origin language of common Lebanese loanwords. Quiz format: word + transliteration shown, learner picks from 6 origin buttons (🇫🇷 French, 🇹🇷 Turkish, 🇬🇧 English, 🇮🇷 Persian, 📜 Aramaic, 🟢 Native Arabic). After answer, etymology note + meaning revealed.

**Why this gap matters**: Lebanese is a contact language. French (Mandate-era), Turkish (Ottoman 400 yrs), English (modern), Persian (via Ottoman/Arabic), and Aramaic (substrate) all surface in everyday vocabulary. Knowing the origin is functional knowledge — it predicts **register**:
- French loans → urban / educated / fashion (`merci`, `salon`, `ascenseur`)
- Turkish loans → domestic / old-Beirut (`oda`, `soba`, `fistan`)
- English loans → tech / youth (`kombyuter`, `mobayl`, `imayl`)
- Persian loans → semi-formal / older houses (`diwan`, `dolab`, `jizdan`)
- Aramaic substrate → core daily verbs that feel native (`tarya2`, `shob`)
- Native Arabic distractors (`bayt`, `ktab`, `2ahwé`) — to avoid the assumption that EVERY everyday word is a loan

This builds **register awareness**, the same way Pragmatics Drill (Run #69) built tone/subtext awareness.

### Tabs
- **🎯 Quiz**: one item at a time, 6-option multiple choice, 30 items shuffled, score tracked
- **📖 Browse**: all 30 items grouped by origin language (visual etymology atlas)
- **💡 Tips**: 7 portable register heuristics

- Turkish (4): oDa, Sobya, fistèn, shawarma
- English (5): kombyuter, mobayl, imayl, okay, barking, bāS — wait that's 6, English (6 of them counting baS)
- Persian (4): dulèb, ba2shish, diwèn, jizdèn

## Run #73 — User-picked voice unblocks audio fallback (AUDIO)

**Category**: AUDIO (73%3==1)

**Bug surfaced**: bugs.rtf — "Audio system is still overall the biggest source of problems". Specific failure mode found by tracing the chain:

1. Audio chain (set in Run #36) requires `_hasDialectVoice()` to return true before browser TTS step (5) is reached. Otherwise badge says "❌ No Lebanese audio".
2. `_hasDialectVoice()` was hard-wired to score `getBestVoiceIdx()` (auto-pick) against the 80-threshold (Lebanese / Levantine).
3. If a learner only has Egyptian (60), Iraqi (70), Gulf (50), or MSA (42) voices installed — the most common case on Windows / Android — `_hasDialectVoice` returns false. Browser TTS step never runs. They hear nothing at all for words that lack a recording.
4. Audio Lab already lets the user manually pick a voice (`★ Set default` → `setPreferredVoiceIdx`), and `_speakViaBrowser` already honors that pref when actually called. But the gating function above never consulted it, so the chain bottomed out at step 6 anyway.

Result: a user installs Egyptian voice + opens Audio Lab + clicks Set Default — and gets the same silence as before. The pref UI was decorative.

**Fix**: `_hasDialectVoice` now short-circuits true when the learner has set an explicit voice pref AND that voice index is still valid. The auto-pick / 80-threshold path still runs as the fallback (so users who haven't picked anything still get the conservative default). 6 lines of real change in `js/app.js:3567`. The `_lebStrictBlocksBrowserTts` strict-mode check is intentionally NOT relaxed — strict mode means strict, and a user who enabled it has signaled "no non-Lebanese voices, period."

Also rewrote the step-6 fallback badge to actually tell the user how to fix it: `"❌ No Lebanese audio · Audio Lab → Voices → ★ pick a voice to enable fallback"` if any Arabic voice is detected, and `"❌ No Lebanese audio · open Audio Lab to install an Arabic voice"` if none. Previously it just said "try Audio Lab to install voice" which obscured the actual remedy for the common case.

### Files touched
- `js/app.js` — `_hasDialectVoice` (line 3567): pref-honor short-circuit + WHY-comment
- `js/app.js` — speak step 6 (line 3773): nuanced badge text based on whether `_arVoices.length` is positive
- `_dev/probe.js`:
  - 3 new CHECKs:
    - `r73_hasDialectVoiceHonorsPref` — function source contains the pref-honor path
    - `r73_hasDialectVoiceTrueWithPref` — behavior: with mem-localStorage + Egyptian voice + setPreferredVoiceIdx(0), `_hasDialectVoice()` returns true
    - `r73_hasDialectVoiceFalseNoPrefNoLb` — behavior: without pref, with only Egyptian voice, returns false (auto-pick path still strict)
  - Discovered along the way: probe stub had `var speechSynthesis` but no `window.speechSynthesis`. Behavior tests now set `window.speechSynthesis = speechSynthesis` themselves; intentionally not patching the STUB to avoid invalidating prior tests that may rely on the falsy default.

### Verification
- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → all 209 functions present, all CHECKs green incl. 3 new r73 (one source-grep + two behavior with mem-localStorage)
- Strict-Lebanese mode behavior unchanged (intentional)
- Existing voice-pref-honoring code in `_speakViaBrowser` (line 3589) was already correct — this run unblocks the gate that was preventing it from being reached

### Why this is the right framing of the bug
"Audio system doesn't work" is broad; the actionable subset is "audio falls back to silence even when the user has set up a voice." Run #36 was right to gate browser TTS on dialect-grade voices for the auto path (otherwise everyone with Egyptian voice gets MSA-style audio they didn't ask for). The miss was treating an EXPLICIT user choice as if it were the auto default. Explicit > auto, always.

## Run #74 — Heatmap unions both per-day activity counters (BUG FIXES)

**Category**: BUG FIXES (74%3==2)

**Bug**: The activity heatmap (Stats → 6-month grid, GitHub-style) was reading only `la_daily_ct` from localStorage. App actually maintains TWO parallel per-day counters:

| Storage key      | Driven by         | Used for                              |
|------------------|-------------------|---------------------------------------|
| `la_daily_ct`    | `incDailyCount()` | Goal bar, daily-goal celebration, **heatmap** |
| `la_activity`    | `recordActivity()`| Streak counter, getStreak() math      |

These two counters drifted historically. Until **Run #71**, multiple drill paths called `recordActivity()` without `incDailyCount()` — minimal pairs, grammar exercises, conversation challenge, passage quiz, speed drill, match game, and the sentence builder (`recordActivity` only). So `la_activity` had days that `la_daily_ct` didn't, and the heatmap showed those days as **blank cells** even though the user had practiced.

User-visible symptom: "I clearly studied last weekend — minimal pairs and the match game — but the heatmap shows nothing for those days." This is exactly what the bugs.rtf line "Progress tracking straight up doesn't work" captures from the *learner's* perspective. Run #71 fixed it forward (both counters now incremented in lockstep). Run #74 fixes it **backward** — the historical `la_activity` data already on disk is now reflected in the heatmap immediately, no migration step required.

**Fix**: `renderHeatmap` now reads BOTH counters and unions them with per-day max:

```js
const data = {};
const allKeys = new Set([...Object.keys(dailyData), ...Object.keys(actData)]);
allKeys.forEach(k => { data[k] = Math.max(dailyData[k] || 0, actData[k] || 0); });
```

Per-day **max** (not sum) is correct because:
- For modern post-#71 days, both counters are incremented in lockstep → max == either == correct.
- For pre-#71 days where only `la_activity` was written, `la_daily_ct[k] || 0` = 0 → max = `la_activity[k]` → recovered.
- For pre-#71 days where only `la_daily_ct` was written (e.g. core SRS rate path always hit both, but grammar drills only hit one), max recovers the existing data without double-counting.
- Sum would double-count modern days; max preserves correct count for both eras.

### Files touched
- `js/app.js`: `renderHeatmap` (line 10625) — replaced single-source read with two-source union, added explanatory comment about counter history
- `_dev/probe.js`:
  - `r74_heatmapReadsBothCounters` — source-grep CHECK confirms `renderHeatmap` references `la_daily_ct`, `la_activity`, AND `Math.max`
  - `r74_heatmapPerDayMaxBehavior` — pure-logic behavior test of the union semantics (verifies max-not-sum, verifies recovery of single-counter days)

### Verification
- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → all 209 functions present, both new r74 CHECKs green
- All prior CHECKs (242 → 244) remain green
- Goal bar / streak counter / getStreak unaffected (still source-of-truth from their own counters)

### Why this is the right framing of the bug
The bug surfaces in the heatmap, but the cause is structural: two sources of truth for "did the user study today." The right long-term fix is consolidation, but that's a bigger refactor with migration risk. The right short-term fix is to make every reader tolerant of both counters — which is what this run does for the heatmap. Future readers (e.g. weekly aggregates, retention analytics) should follow the same pattern.

### Bugs.rtf tie-in
Closes the historical-data half of "Progress tracking straight up doesn't work." Run #71 closed the forward half (new study events now hit both counters); Run #74 closes the backward half (old study events recorded in only `la_activity` are now visible in the heatmap). Both runs together: progress tracking actually tracks now.

## Run #75 — NEW FEATURE: Endearments & Compliments Coach (💝)
*(2026-04-20 — N=75, 75%3==0 → NEW FEATURES)*

### Why this feature

Lebanese Arabic has an unusually dense endearment/compliment register. The vocabulary exists in every textbook (`7abibi`, `ya 2albi`, `ya rou7i`, `tu2borné`, …), but the *social calculus* — which one fits **this** relationship + **this** moment + **this** gender — is culture-specific and nearly impossible to pick up from flashcards alone. Mis-applying produces classic learner tells: calling a professional contact `7yēté` (too intimate), calling a male friend `ya 2amar` (feminine compliment), saying `mabrouk` to someone recovering from surgery (wrong register entirely).

Existing drills (Pragmatics, Loanwords, Proverbs) cover *comprehension* of Lebanese; this coach covers *active social judgment* — the user picks the right phrase for a concrete scenario.

### Design

Three tabs:

- **🎯 Scenarios** — 20 short contexts (spouse greets you / daughter shows a drawing / taxi driver found an address / stranger at a wedding / male elder at a family gathering…). ## Run #76 — AUDIO FIX: speakSmart prefers crowd audio over MSA TTS
*(2026-04-20 — N=76, 76%3==1 → AUDIO)*

### Bug (bugs.rtf)

> "sentence audio is often not Lebanese arabic"

Root cause was inside `speakSmart` (the sentence-chunk playback engine). When a chunk had no local audio, the gate was binary:

```
strictBlock ? skip : speechSynthesis(_arVoices[getBestVoiceIdx()])
```

For the **default user** (strict mode off) with only MSA voices installed (Egyptian, Saudi, etc. — the common case on iOS/macOS/Windows), every sentence chunk would be spoken by an MSA voice. The Wiktionary/Commons crowd-audio fallback was only reached if `_arVoices` was literally empty — a case that almost never happens. Users with only MSA voices heard MSA on every sentence.

Run #73 fixed the same shape of bug for single-word playback (`_hasDialectVoice` now honors user pref). Run #76 extends the same philosophy to sentence chunks.

### Fix

Reorder `speakSmart`'s chunk-without-local-audio branch into three tiers:

1. **`hasDialect && !strictBlock`** → direct `speechSynthesis` (user-pref voice, or best voice scoring ≥ 80). Fast path unchanged for users with a dialect-capable setup.
2. **Else** (no dialect voice, OR strict-blocked) → try `fetchWiktionaryAudio` → `fetchCommonsAudio`. These are crowd-sourced recordings — many Lebanese/Levantine speakers contribute, so this is measurably more authentic than MSA TTS.
3. **Last resort** → if non-strict and crowd sources both miss, fall back to MSA `speechSynthesis` (still better than silence for a user who opted out of strict mode). Strict mode skips the chunk silently — same as before.

```js
if(hasDialect && !strictBlock && ...){ speechSynthesis.speak(...); }
else {
  (async () => {
    let url = await fetchWiktionaryAudio(c.text) || await fetchCommonsAudio(c.text);
    if(url){ audio.src = url; audio.play(); return; }
    if(strictBlock){ resolve(); return; }              // skip rather than MSA
    // Last resort: MSA TTS better than silence for non-strict users
    speechSynthesis.speak(...);
  })();
}
```

### Why this is the right framing

The user's complaint "sentence audio often not Lebanese" has two failure modes, and they need different fixes:

- **Strict users with no Lebanese voice** — already correctly silenced (Run #57). ✓
- **Non-strict users with only MSA voices** — were getting MSA on every chunk. **This run** fixes that by promoting crowd audio above MSA TTS.

Crowd audio isn't perfect (some Wiktionary contributors are MSA speakers too, some recordings are low-quality) but the average Lebanese-authenticity of a Wiktionary recording of "بدي" is much higher than an Egyptian TTS rendering of it — and importantly, when it IS a Lebanese speaker, it's *actually* Lebanese, not a stylized MSA approximation.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js`: `speakSmart` (line ~15766) — reordered fallback tiers, added `hasDialect` gate using existing `_hasDialectVoice` helper (Run #73), added crowd-first then last-resort-MSA branch with explanatory comment
- `_dev/probe.js`: +4 r76 CHECKs — `speakSmart` sources `_hasDialectVoice`, has the `hasDialect && !strictBlock` gate, crowd fetches run before the last-resort MSA `getBestVoiceIdx`, and the strict-skip return is preserved

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → 215 functions present, all 4 new r76 CHECKs green, all prior CHECKs still green
- Behavior tests rely on source-grep because the real path needs `speechSynthesis` + `fetch` mocking (out of scope for Node probe). Source-grep is sufficient here: the reorder is the entire fix, and the grep confirms the order `fetchWiktionary < fetchCommons < Last resort < getBestVoiceIdx`.

### Ripple check

- `_hasDialectVoice` now has two call sites (its own `speak()` at 3640 and `speakSmart` here) — consistent semantics, no conflict.
- Fast path (user has Lebanese voice / user-pref) unchanged — still direct TTS, no new crowd lookup on happy path.
- Strict-Lebanese mode (Run #57) unchanged — still skips silently when no dialect voice.
- `_playWiktionary` / `_playCommons` unaffected (single-word path).

### Bugs.rtf tie-in

Closes the default-user half of "sentence audio often not Lebanese." Run #57 fixed strict users (silence over MSA); Run #73 fixed single-word playback (honor user pref); Run #76 fixes sentence playback for the non-strict-no-Lebanese-voice user — the largest remaining population that was hearing MSA when they expected Lebanese.

## Run #77 — BUG FIX: Vocab growth chart timezone mismatch
*(2026-04-20 — N=77, 77%3==2 → BUG FIXES)*

### Bug

`renderVocabGrowthChart` (the 30-day new-words-introduced bar chart on Stats) built its day-column keys with `d.toISOString().slice(0, 10)` — a UTC date. But `card.first_seen` is stored via `todayKey()`, which has been a **local** date since Run #58. In any negative-UTC timezone (US, most of the Americas), the chart's "today" column maps to tomorrow's UTC date — which has zero first_seen entries. Result: the newest column always showed 0, even when the user had introduced multiple new words that day. Worse, every column in the user's evening shifted by one day, so the chart consistently *misattributed* recent days.

### Why this was missed

Run #58 fixed the canonical path (`recordActivity`, `todayKey`) to local. But `renderVocabGrowthChart` built its own keyspace and never got updated. Two other growth readers (`renderCompletionPredictor`, `renderWeeklyPlanPanel`) already use `_localDateKey(d)` — they were fixed in Run #58's sweep. This one was the holdout.

### Grep audit

```bash
grep -n "toISOString().slice(0" js/app.js
# 4282, 4329, 16379 — all download filenames (cosmetic, no data match)
# 7470 — renderVocabGrowthChart: BUG — fix this
```

Only one data-key site remained on UTC; fixed.

### Fix

```js
// was:
const key = d.toISOString().slice(0, 10);
// now:
const key = _localDateKey(d);
```

Added a comment explaining why (and pointing at the sibling readers that were already correct, so a future editor doesn't silently reintroduce the drift).

### Files touched

- `js/app.js`: `renderVocabGrowthChart` line ~7470 — one-line fix + explanatory comment block
- `_dev/probe.js`: +3 r77 CHECKs
  - `r77_growthChartUsesLocalKey` — confirms source contains `_localDateKey(d)`
  - `r77_growthChartNoUTCSlice` — confirms no `toISOString().slice(0, 10)` remnant in the function
  - `r77_localDateKeyMatchesLocalToday` — sanity-checks `_localDateKey(new Date())` returns the expected local YYYY-MM-DD

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → 215 functions present, all 3 new r77 CHECKs green, all prior CHECKs still green

### Bugs.rtf tie-in

Not a named entry but a direct expression of "Progress tracking straight up doesn't work" from the user's perspective: users who checked their vocab growth chart in the evening (or any negative-UTC zone) saw zero for today, even after introducing new words. Add to the Run #71/#74/#77 triad that's progressively closing the full "progress tracking" surface.

## Run #78 — NEW FEATURE: Response Pair Coach (🔁)
*(2026-04-20 — N=78, 78%3==0 → NEW FEATURES)*

### Why this feature

Lebanese conversation runs on ritualized exchange pairs: you say X, the other person says Y. Not saying Y (especially replacing it with "shukran") flags you as a non-native speaker more reliably than any grammar mistake. Examples:

- `SabaaH il-kheir` → `SabaaH in-noor` (not shukran)
- `mabrouk` → `allah ybaarik feek` (not shukran)
- `tislam idak` → `ysalmak` (not shukran)
- `il-ba2iyyé bi-7ayaatak` → `7ayaatak il-baa2yé` (definitely not shukran)

Existing app covers vocabulary, grammar, pragmatic subtext (via Pragmatics Drill), and endearments (Run #75 DEC). Response pairs are the last obvious gap in **active output training** — the point where learners must *produce* the right thing, not just recognize it.

### Design

Three tabs, mirroring the DEC pattern but with per-category filtering:

- **🎯 Quiz** — See a prompt, pick the correct response from 4 options. Distractors are same-category responses (e.g. all greetings, all meal-related) so getting it right requires knowing the *specific* pair, not just the register. Category filter at top lets user drill just greetings, just condolences, etc.
- **📖 Browse** — All 25 pairs grouped by category, with prompt + response + literal translation + usage notes.
- **💡 Tips** — 7 meta-rules (response is almost always a blessing mirrored back; "allah y[verb]ak/ik" is the template for half of all responses; never say shukran to mabrouk/condolences/…; etc.).

### Distractor quality

`_rpcBuildOptions` picks 3 distractors from the same category when possible (fills from cross-category only if the same-category pool is too small — currently only happens for the `groom` and `condol` categories with 1-2 pairs each). Same-category distractors make the quiz actually *test* pair-memorization rather than register-guessing. Same-response dedup prevents two buttons showing the same Arabic text.

### Scoring

Same as LWS/DEC: correct → `_rpcScore.correct++`, `recordActivity()`, `incDailyCount()`, `sfx(sfxCorrect)`. Wrong only increments `.total`. Second answer on same card is locked (prevents double-count).

### Files

- `data/run78-data.js` (NEW):
  - `RPC_CATEGORIES` (9): greet, farewell, meal, recover, groom, occasion, thanks, compli, condol
  - `RPC_PAIRS` (25): covers all major ritualized exchanges — greetings, farewells, meals (including sufra daayme / daamat ayyaamak), recovery (salaamtak / allah ysalmak, il7amdellah 3a-s-salaame), grooming (nā3iman), occasions (mabrouk, 3o2baalak, kil sané w-inta Tayyeb), thanks (shukran → il-3afwan, mersi → tikram), compliments (tislam idak → ysalmak), condolences (il-ba2iyyé bi-7ayaatak, allah yer7amo). Each pair has `prompt_ar/tr/lit + response_ar/tr/lit + notes`.
  - `RPC_TIPS` (7): meta-rules for internalizing the response pattern (mirror blessings back; gender-mark -ak/-ik by addressee; never shukran for mabrouk; etc.)
- `index.html`:
  - Added `<script src="data/run78-data.js">` before `js/app.js`
  - Added `🔁 Response Pairs` button after `💝 Endearments`
  - Added `#rpc-overlay` after `#dec-overlay`
- `js/app.js` (~200 lines appended): state (`_rpcTab`, `_rpcIdx`, `_rpcOrder`, `_rpcScore`, `_rpcAnswered`, `_rpcPick`, `_rpcOptions`, `_rpcFilterCat`), helpers (`_rpcShuffle`, `_rpcPoolIdx`, `_rpcBuildOrder`, `_rpcCurrentPair`, `_rpcEscape`, `_rpcBuildOptions`), public (`openRpc`, `closeRpc`, `setRpcTab`, `rpcSetCat`, `renderRpc`, `rpcAnswer`, `rpcNext`), sub-renderers (`_rpcRenderQuiz`, `_rpcRenderLearn`, `_rpcRenderTips`), self-register into `TOPICS_CATEGORIES[id='conv']`
- `_dev/probe.js`:
  - Added `'data/run78-data.js'` to FILES
  - +12 r78 CHECKs (6 fn-presence + 3 data-count + pairs-have-required-fields + cats-all-valid + ids-unique + registered-in-topics + build-options-has-one-correct + correct-increments + wrong-does-not-increment + second-answer-locked + cat-filter-narrows)

## Run #80 — BUG FIX

### Bug

`seedAudioCache` IIFE at `js/app.js:5521` guards with `if (!(word in cache))`. Problem: for users whose pre-PRECACHED_AUDIO session cached `__none__` for a word (Wiktionary miss, Commons miss), that `__none__` entry stays — the seed never overrides it, so the user never gets the precached Commons URL even though it ships in the bundle.

Impact on bugs.rtf item **"A lot of words are still missing proper audio"**: any returning user (most users by run #80) had their audio coverage silently capped at pre-seed levels. PRECACHED_AUDIO ships ~200 entries; a returning user with even 50 `__none__`s among those 200 would have 50 falsely-missing words in every coverage panel and prewarm target.

### Fix

```js
// js/app.js:5524
if (!(word in cache) || cache[word] === '__none__') { cache[word] = url; seeded = true; }
```

One-line change. Override stale `__none__`s with the shipped URL. No risk of overriding a user's successfully-fetched Wiktionary URL since those aren't `__none__`.

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → 221 functions present, all prior CHECKs green
- +3 r80 CHECKs all green:
  - `r80_seedOverridesNone` — source-grep confirms `=== '__none__'` appears inside the seed loop
  - `r80_precachedAudioNonTrivial` — guards the data (>150 entries)
  - `r80_reSeedOverridesNone` — behavior test: inject `__none__` for a precached key, re-run the seed logic, confirm it gets overridden with the real URL

### Probe harness change

Added `loadAssetAsGlobal('js/app.js', '__APP_SRC')` into the Function wrapper so source-grep CHECKs can scan the raw source for IIFEs (not just function bodies via `toString()`).

### Bugs.rtf tie-in

Directly closes part of "A lot of words are still missing proper audio" for returning users. New users were never affected (cache starts empty → seed populates cleanly). But anyone who'd used the app before this precache data was added (which is ~every real user by now) was silently starved of ~200 words worth of Commons audio. This fix is retroactively delivered on the next app load.

## Run #82 — AUDIO

### Problem

`fetchWiktionaryAudio`, `fetchCommonsAudio`, and `fetchWiktionaryWithDialect` all used a hard-coded `queries = [text, stripped]` list — two variants. But Arabic text very often carries:
- **Definite article** ال (al-/el-) prefix: `الكتاب`, `البيت`, `الطريق`
- **Proclitic preposition** attached to article: `بالبيت` (in the house), `عالسوق` (to the market)
- **Single-char proclitic**: `و/ب/ف/ل/س` (and/at/so/to/future)
- **Two-char Lebanese proclitic**: `ما/رح/عم` (neg/future/progressive)

Wiktionary pages and Commons recordings are almost always stored under the **bare stem**. So `الكتاب` → Wiktionary returns no page → fall through to Commons → Commons returns no match → cached `__none__`. Same for `بحبو` / `عالسوق` / `ما بعرف`, etc. The word exists as a recording, just not under the article/proclitic-prefixed form the user typed.

Internal cache-lookup (`_audioKeyVariants` added in Run #67) already handled this for local cache and PRECACHED_AUDIO. Live fetch didn't. This gap means every article-prefixed or proclitic-prefixed word on first play goes straight to TTS fallback, never enriches the cache.

### Fix

Added `_wiktQueryVariants(text, stripped)` near `_stripDiacritics`. Returns 1–4 dedupe variants:
1. raw text
2. tashkeel-stripped
3. def-article (ال) stripped from front — when prefix is `ال` and remainder is non-trivial
4. proclitic-stripped — `ما/رح/عم` (2-char) or `و/ب/ف/ل/س` (1-char) at start, bounded by min-length guards

All three fetch functions now call `_wiktQueryVariants(text, stripped)` instead of constructing their own 2-entry list. Worst-case lookup goes from 2 network requests to 4. Both fetch functions already short-circuit on first hit, so the extra latency only hits pure-miss cases.

### Why bounded at 4

Live fetch fans out to a slow network. Full `_audioKeyVariants()` (14 variants) would mean up to 14 HTTP requests per miss — unusable. 4 covers the common prefix patterns (article, 2-char proclitic, 1-char proclitic) without pathological fan-out.

### Verification

- `node --check` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → 229 functions (was 228, +1 `_wiktQueryVariants`), all 8 r82 CHECKs green:
  - fn-presence
  - `variantsKeepRaw` — `كتاب` stays as first variant
  - `variantsStripDefArticle` — `الكتاب` yields `كتاب`
  - `variantsStripProclitic` — `بالبيت` yields `البيت` (1-char `ب` strip)
  - `variantsStripTwoCharProclitic` — `مابعرف` yields `بعرف` (2-char `ما` strip)
  - `variantsDedupShort` — `قط` (2 chars) doesn't produce redundant variants
  - `variantsBoundedSize` — max 4 variants

## Run #83 — BUG FIX

### Bug

`renderTodayDashboard` line 882 filtered session history with:
```js
.filter(s => s.date && s.date.startsWith(today))
```
where `s.date` was written as `new Date().toISOString()` (UTC, line 1452) and `today` was `todayKey()` → `_localDateKey()` (LOCAL date per Run #58's fix).

Prefix-match of a UTC ISO string against a local date key fails for any user in a negative-UTC timezone who studies in the evening. 10pm US Eastern = 2am UTC next day → `s.date = "2026-04-21T02:00:00.000Z"`, `today = "2026-04-20"`, `startsWith` returns false.

Effect: the "⏱ Nm today" field on the homepage dashboard silently zeros out for every late-evening session in the Americas. User sees reviews count, streak increment, XP tick — but "Time today" shows nothing, reinforcing the bugs.rtf complaint that "progress tracking straight up doesn't work."

This is the last remaining UTC-vs-local date mismatch site in the progress-tracking paths after Run #58 (activity keys), Run #71 (daily counters), Run #77 (growth chart). It survived because `s.date.startsWith(today)` looked timezone-agnostic but silently wasn't.

### Fix

Parse to Date, then use `_localDateKey` for comparison:
```js
.filter(s => s.date && _localDateKey(new Date(s.date)) === today)
```

One-line change at `js/app.js:887`. No data migration — existing session history keeps its UTC-string `date` field (used by `new Date(s.date)` elsewhere; those sites were already correct because they call `d.getFullYear()/Month()/Date()` which return LOCAL values from a Date parsed from a UTC ISO string).

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → 229 functions, all 4 new r83 CHECKs green:
  - `dashUsesLocalDateKey` — source-grep confirms new filter in place, old filter removed
  - `behaviorUTCLateEveningCountsAsToday` — simulates a 10pm-local timestamp, confirms its ISO string parses back to today's local key
  - `behaviorFilterMatches` — simulates a 300s late-night session, confirms the new filter sums to 300 (old filter would return 0 in negative-UTC tz)
  - `oldBehaviorWouldMissInEasternTZ` — proves the original bug by direct string comparison: `"2026-04-21T02:00:00.000Z".startsWith("2026-04-20") === false`

### Bugs.rtf tie-in

Direct close on **"Progress tracking straight up doesn't work"**. Every time-of-day display was silently miscounting for evening users in the Americas. Users would finish a long review session, see "0s today" in the dashboard header, and lose trust in every other counter that was actually correct.

Learners default to MSA wh-words or English word-order; neither sounds native. No existing overlay drilled this.

## Run #85 — speakSmart live-fetch cache persistence

**Category: AUDIO** (85 % 3 == 1)
**Date: 2026-04-20**

### Bug identified

`speakSmart()` has two fallback branches for sentence chunks that lack pre-cached audio:

1. **Dialect voice available** → synthesize with user's chosen Arabic voice (fine — already fast, no network).
2. **No dialect voice OR strictLebanese** → fetch Wiktionary, then Commons, play whichever hits.

Branch 2 was calling `fetchWiktionaryAudio(c.text)` and `fetchCommonsAudio(c.text)` directly and throwing the URL away after playback. `audioCache()` was never written. Every replay of the same sentence re-hit the network — for an 8-word sentence with 5 unknown chunks, that's up to 10 HTTP round trips per play (Wikt + Commons for each unknown chunk), visible to the user as "⏳ Searching…" gaps and measurable wasted bandwidth.

`speak()` (single-word path) cached correctly at lines 3740–3743 and 3772–3774. `speakSmart` did not. This was a ~5-month-old hole covering the fallback chunk path since Run #76 added it.

### Fix

Extracted the crowd-audio resolution into a dedicated helper `_speakSmartCrowdFetch(chunkText)` placed immediately before `speakSmart`:

- Uses `_audioKey(chunkText)` so the cache key matches the variant-aware keying used by `_audioCacheMatchFor` / `_audioCommonsMatchFor` / `segmentSentence`.
- On Wiktionary hit: writes `cache[key] = url` + `cache['__dialect__:' + key] = dia` (dialect side-cache consistent with `speak()` step 3), then `saveAudioCache(cache)` + `updateCacheCount()`.
- On Commons hit (Wiktionary missed): writes `cache['__commons__:' + key] = url`, then saves.
- On total miss: writes `'__none__'` to both the main and `__commons__:` buckets (matches the negative-caching pattern `speak()` uses at line 3772–3773) to prevent repeat API hammering.
- Returns `{ url, source, dialect }` so the caller can play immediately.

`speakSmart`'s else-branch now calls `await _speakSmartCrowdFetch(c.text)` and plays `got.url` if non-null, preserving all prior behavior (strict-block skip, MSA-TTS last resort) while compounding cache coverage across sessions.

### Impact

First play of a new sentence: same latency as before (one Wikt call + possibly one Commons call per unknown chunk). Replay: **zero network calls** — every chunk resolves locally from `audioCache`, feeding straight into `segmentSentence`'s `hasAudio` branch on the next invocation. Over a study session, every fetched chunk compounds: a word first heard in sentence A becomes pre-cached for sentence B sharing the same word.

Also writes negative misses — so a chunk that has no Wiktionary / Commons recording stops being re-queried every replay (was wasting ~7s per replay on the 3.5s × 2-api timeout budget).

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → **237 functions** (+1: `_speakSmartCrowdFetch`), all r85 CHECKs green:
  - `smartCachesWiktHit` — helper source contains `fetchWiktionaryAudio` + `cache[key] = url` + `__dialect__:` side-cache write
  - `smartCachesCommonsHit` — helper contains `fetchCommonsAudio` + `cache['__commons__:' + key] = url`
  - `smartCachesNegative` — helper writes `'__none__'` to both main + commons buckets on total miss
  - `smartCallsSaveAudioCache` — helper calls `saveAudioCache(cache)` on all 3 exit paths (n=3)
  - `smartUsesAudioKey` — helper keys by `_audioKey(chunkText)` (variant-compatible with rest of audio stack)
  - `speakSmartCallsHelper` — `speakSmart` source contains `_speakSmartCrowdFetch` call
  - `speakSmartRemovedInlineWikt` / `speakSmartRemovedInlineCommons` — the inline `fetchWiktionaryAudio(c.text)` / `fetchCommonsAudio(c.text)` calls are gone from `speakSmart` (only the helper owns them now)
  - r76 check updated to verify ordering via helper call + helper-internal Wikt-before-Commons

### Bugs.rtf tie-in

Direct close on **"Audio system is still overall the biggest source of problems, many of the reworked features seem to not have been implemented fully"** — the Run #76 crowd-before-MSA fix was only half-implemented: the decision was right but the caching was missing, so the fix only worked *during the first play* of any sentence. Also indirectly helps **"A lot of words are still missing proper audio"** — live fetches that succeed now persist, growing the cache organically as users study sentences.

## Run #86 — rate() path quota-safe localStorage writes

**Category: BUG FIX** (86 % 3 == 2)
**Date: 2026-04-20**

### Bug identified

`rate(quality)` — fired on every card rating — runs this sequence:

```js
srsData[id] = c;
saveSRS();          // quota-safe (Run #44)
recordActivity();   // silent try/catch
incDailyCount();    // bare localStorage.setItem → throws on quota
addXp(xpEarned);    // bare localStorage.setItem → throws on quota
checkMilestone();   // bare localStorage.setItem inside → throws on quota
sessionWordLog.push(...);
advanceStudy();     // ← card actually advances HERE
```

`incDailyCount` (line 585), `addXp` (line 1506), and `checkStreakMilestone` (lines 771, 775) all called `localStorage.setItem` without a try/catch. Once the 5 MB localStorage quota fills — typically from the audio cache accumulating Wiktionary/Commons URLs — the first of those setItems throws `QuotaExceededError`, which aborts the remainder of `rate()`. `advanceStudy()` never runs, so the user's rating appears to do nothing: the same card sits there, no feedback, no XP, no next-card. The user thinks "rating is broken" and starts rage-clicking. `saveSRS` already had quota recovery (Run #44) — so the SRS update itself *did* persist — but the rest of the state was abandoned.

This is a **silent cliff**: the bug is invisible until the quota fills. Users with hundreds of hours of practice run right into it.

### Fix

Added a small helper `_lsSet(key, value)` that mirrors `saveSRS`'s quota-recovery pattern:

```js
function _lsSet(key, value) {
  try { localStorage.setItem(key, value); return true; }
  catch (e) {
    const isQuota = (e && (e.name === 'QuotaExceededError' || e.code === 22 || /quota/i.test(e.message || '')));
    if (!isQuota) { console.warn(...); return false; }
    try { localStorage.removeItem(CACHE_KEY); } catch {}
    try { localStorage.removeItem('la_youtube_audio_idx'); } catch {}
    try { localStorage.setItem(key, value); return true; }
    catch (e2) { console.warn(...); return false; }
  }
}
```

On quota, it drops the (regenerable) audio cache + YouTube index — same blobs `saveSRS` drops — and retries. Returns `true` on success, `false` if the write still fails. Either way, it **never throws**, so `rate()` always reaches `advanceStudy()`.

Swapped three sites from bare `localStorage.setItem` → `_lsSet`:

- `incDailyCount` — `la_daily_ct` (daily review counter)
- `addXp` — `la_xp` (gamification XP)
- `checkStreakMilestone` — `la_streak_milestones` (shown-flag) + `la_freeze_tokens` (freeze-token award)

All three are on the hot `rate()` path.

### Scope note

Intentionally did **not** blanket-swap every `localStorage.setItem` in the codebase. This is a targeted fix for the user-visible stall in `rate()`. Other sites (placement test save, welcome-seen flag, etc.) can tolerate a failed write — users don't notice. The exact three functions above all run on every rating, so each is a potential abort point.

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → **238 functions** (+1: `_lsSet`), all r86 CHECKs green:
  - `fn_lsSet` — helper exists
  - `lsSetHandlesQuota` — source contains `QuotaExceededError` branch + `CACHE_KEY` drop + `la_youtube_audio_idx` drop
  - `incDailyUsesLsSet` / `addXpUsesLsSet` / `streakMilestoneUsesLsSet` — source confirms `_lsSet('la_...')` in place of bare `localStorage.setItem('la_...')`
  - `lsSetNormalWriteSucceeds` — **behavioral**: mock-replaces `localStorage.setItem` with a recording stub, confirms `_lsSet` makes exactly one call with the right (key, value) and returns `true`
  - `lsSetSwallowsQuotaThrow` — **behavioral**: mock-replaces `localStorage.setItem` with a `QuotaExceededError` thrower, confirms `_lsSet` returns `false` and never propagates (caller-side `try { } catch {}` not needed)
  - `lsSetDropsAudioCacheOnQuota` — **behavioral**: mocks setItem to throw once then succeed, records removeItem calls, confirms `_lsSet` removes `la_audio_v2` + `la_youtube_audio_idx` on quota and retries exactly once

### Bugs.rtf tie-in

Indirect close on **"Audio system is still overall the biggest source of problems, many of the reworked features seem to not have been implemented fully"** — the largest audio-cache blob is what actually triggers the quota collapse, but the symptom the user sees is "rating my card doesn't work." This connects the audio footprint back to the rating path so a full cache never strands the user mid-review.

Also prevents a subtle drift: users sitting at an under-goal daily count when a quota error fires would see confetti fire repeatedly (goal-check is `prev+1===goal` based on pre-write local value) if the count couldn't persist. Now the write either lands or the audio cache gets pruned and it lands on retry.

## Run #87 — NEW FEATURE: Pronoun Suffix Coach (PSC)

**Category**: NEW FEATURE (87 % 3 == 0)
**Prefix**: `psc-`
**Scope**: Complement Run #13 by drilling pronoun suffixes on the *two other host types* Lebanese glues clitics onto — verbs and prepositions.

### Gap identified

Run #13 built `POS_SUFFIXES` + `POS_NOUNS`: 8 pronouns × 18 nouns, all with the feminine `-t-` shift pre-conjugated. That's thorough for **possession on nouns**.

But Lebanese pronoun clitics attach to THREE host types, not one:

1. **Noun + possessive suffix**: `bayt` + `-ak` → `baytak` (your house) — covered by Run #13
2. **Verb + object suffix**: `shuft` + `-ak` → `shuftak` (I saw you-m) — NOT drilled as a dedicated feature
3. **Preposition + pronoun suffix**: `ma3` + `-i` → `ma3i` (with me), `3ind` + `-o` → `3indo` (he has) — NOT drilled as a dedicated feature

`grep` for `OBJECT_SUFFIX|PREP_SUFFIX|shuftak|3indak` across the repo returned only incidental mentions (grammar-sections.js has a read-only lesson line; vocab has examples like `ma3i` baked into phrases). No **drillable table** with paradigm coverage. Every other pronoun-suffix-related file uses these forms in finished sentences but never makes the learner *produce* them in the paradigm.

That gap matters because:
- **Verb-object `-ni`** is the one pronoun form that differs between hosts — verb object 1sg uses `-ni` (`shuftni` = you saw me), while nouns and preps use `-i`. Learners trained only on nouns will miss this.
- **Preposition stem shifts** are Lebanese-distinctive: `3ala` → `3lay-` (on), `la` + pronoun inserts a glottal → `la2o` (for him), `min` doubles to `minni/minno` (from me/him), `fi + o` contracts to `fi` (not `fio`). No drill = no internalization.
- **`3ind + pronoun` IS the verb "to have"** in Lebanese. `3indi` is not just "at me" — it's the primary way to say "I have." Absolutely essential, yet this app had no dedicated place to practice it as a paradigm.

### What shipped

**Data (`data/run87-data.js`)**:
- `PSC_PRONOUNS` (8) — reusable pronoun table; now exposes BOTH `vsuf` (verb-object form, -ni for ana) and `psuf` (prep/noun form, -i for ana). Annotates the clitic asymmetry the user needs to notice.
- `PSC_VERBS` (10) — transitive verbs with all 8 object-suffixed forms pre-conjugated: `shuft`, `7abbayt`, `3reft`, `sa2alt`, `sma3t`, `fhemt`, `se3adt`, `nsit`, `zkart`, `nTart`. Each with `{ar, tr, en, root, forms[8], note?}`.
- `PSC_PREPS` (10) — preps with all 8 pronoun-suffixed forms: `ma3`, `3ind`, `la`, `min`, `fi`, `3ala`, `la7ad`, `abel`, `ba3d`, `b`. Annotates the quirky ones (glottal insertion, doubled consonants, vowel shifts, contractions).
- `PSC_EXERCISES` (28) — fill-in drills: 14 verb + 14 prep. Each `{id, kind, host, pronIdx, prompt_en, ar, tr, hint}`. Answers cross-referenced against host `forms[pronIdx]`.
- `PSC_TIPS` (7) — meta-rules the learner should walk away with.

**UI (`js/app.js` append, ~180 lines)**:
- `openPsc`/`closePsc`/`setPscTab`/`renderPsc`/`pscAnswer`/`pscNext`/`pscSetFilter`/`_pscBuildOptions`/`_pscShuffle`/`_pscEscape`/`_pscFilteredExercises`/`_pscLoadCurrent`/`_pscCurrentExercise`/`_pscRenderQuiz`/`_pscRenderLearn`/`_pscRenderTips`
- Three tabs: **Quiz** (MC with 4 options, distractors drawn from same-host paradigm first then other-exercise pool), **Learn** (two full paradigm tables — verbs-×-pronouns, preps-×-pronouns), **Tips** (the 7 meta-rules)
- Filter strip inside Quiz tab: `all | verb | prep` — narrows which host type you're drilling
- Score tracking: `_pscScore.correct / wrong / answered:Set` (prevents double-counting if user clicks after the lock)
- Self-registers into `TOPICS_CATEGORIES` under `id:'conv'` as `{label:'🔗 Suffixes', fn:'openPsc', ...}`

**index.html**:
- Button added after `openQfc`: `🔗 Suffixes`
- Overlay `#psc-overlay` added before `#qfc-overlay`
- `<script src="data/run87-data.js">` added before `js/app.js`

### Design choices worth noting

- **Distractors prefer same-host paradigm**: when you're asked for `shuftak`, the wrong options are other forms of `shuft` (`shuftni`, `shufto`, `shufta`) before falling back to cross-host pool. This forces the learner to discriminate pronoun suffix — not just recognize the verb root.
- **`kind` badge on each card**: shows "verb + obj" or "prep + pronoun" so the learner frames the grammatical operation correctly before answering.
- **`answered:Set` guard in score**: double-clicking the same option after the lock was already set doesn't double-count. This is subtly different from `_qfcAnswered`-boolean approach from Run #84 — `answered` tracks per-exercise-id so a filter change + re-entry can still accumulate honestly.
- **Intentional redundancy for `b-` preposition**: the `PSC_PREPS` entry for `b` ("by / with (instrument)") points back to the `fi-` forms because Lebanese elides the `b-` into `fi-` when pronominalized (`bo` is not a thing — people say `fi`). Flagged in the `note` field.

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK

  - `r87_dataCountsMatch` — `ok_pr8_v10_p10_ex28_t7`

  - `r87_exerciseIdsUnique` — `ok_n=28`

  - `r87_exerciseHostsResolve` — every `host` resolves to a real `PSC_VERBS` or `PSC_PREPS` entry

## Run #88 — AUDIO: dialect-ranked cache match

**Category**: AUDIO (88 % 3 == 1)
**bugs.rtf target**: "sentence audio is often not Lebanese arabic"

### Bug identified

When `speak(text)` runs, it resolves the cached Wiktionary URL via `_audioCacheMatchFor(text, cache)`. That helper expanded `text` into a variant list — `[raw, stripped, normalized, def-article-stripped, proclitic-stripped, enclitic-stripped, ...]` — and returned the **first variant with a cached hit**. Whichever variant came first in iteration order won, regardless of whether a later variant had a better-dialect recording.

Concrete collision:

- User says `بكتاب` ("with a book"). The text has `b-` proclitic fused on.
- `_audioKeyVariants('بكتاب')` yields: `['بكتاب', 'بكتاب', …, 'كتاب', …]` (raw first, proclitic-stripped comes later).
- A previous session cached:
  - `cache['بكتاب'] = 'https://.../msaRecording.ogg'` with `__dialect__:بكتاب` = `📚 MSA (Wiktionary)` (because English Wiktionary's `بكتاب` lemma only had MSA audio).
  - `cache['كتاب'] = 'https://.../lebaneseRecording.ogg'` with `__dialect__:كتاب` = `🇱🇧 Lebanese` (from a prior lookup of bare `كتاب` that hit the Lebanese Arabic section).
- `_audioCacheMatchFor` iterated variants, hit `بكتاب` first, returned the **MSA** URL.
- User hears MSA even though a Lebanese recording is sitting in their cache one variant deeper.

This is also why strict-Lebanese mode partially masked the issue: strict mode skips any cached hit whose dialect starts with `📚`, so it *would* fall through to Commons search, but then it'd miss the already-cached Lebanese recording on `كتاب` entirely. **Default mode users** just heard MSA with no recourse.

Same problem applies to `_audioUrlFor(text)` (used by phrase-audio presence checks and Audio Lab stats) — it returned first-cache-hit too.

### Fix

Added a small `_scoreDialect(d)` helper that scores dialect badges:

```
🇱🇧 Lebanese = 100
🎬 YouTube   =  95   (real Lebanese speakers)
🌍 Levantine =  80   (Syrian/Palestinian/Jordanian Wiktionary section)
unknown      =  30
🎙 Wiktionary =  50  (section-less, dialect uncertain)
📚 MSA       =  20
```

Then rewrote both match functions to do a **best-of scan**: iterate ALL variant hits, collect each with its dialect score, sort by `score DESC` with variant-index as tie-breaker (earlier = more specific match wins at equal dialect quality).

```js
var best = null;
for(var i = 0; i < variants.length; i++){
  var v = cache[variants[i]];
  if(v && v !== '__none__'){
    var s = _scoreDialect(cache['__dialect__:' + variants[i]]);
    if(!best || s > best.score || (s === best.score && i < best.variantIdx)){
      best = { key: variants[i], url: v, dialect: ..., score: s, variantIdx: i };
    }
  }
}
```

Critically, this is a pure upgrade of the search strategy — no change to what gets written to cache, no change to variant-generation logic, no change to strict-Lebanese semantics. Callers that receive `{key, url, dialect}` get the best-dialect recording instead of the first-found one. Strict-Lebanese mode still does its MSA-rejection logic afterward; now that rejection correctly filters the best MSA candidate but will already prefer to hand callers a non-MSA one when it exists.

### Why YouTube kept iteration-order semantics

`_audioUrlFor` still returns the **first** `YOUTUBE_AUDIO[variant]` hit without scoring. Rationale: YT is hand-curated, every entry is a real Lebanese speaker, and the dialect isn't stored as a side-channel — iteration order (which prefers the more-specific match) is the correct heuristic there.

### Verification

- `node --check js/app.js` → OK
- `node _dev/probe.js` → **247 functions** (+1: `_scoreDialect`), all r88 CHECKs green:
  - `fn_scoreDialect` — helper exists
  - `r88_scoreDialectOrdering` — `Leb > YT > Lev > Generic > Unknown > MSA` (behavioral)
  - `r88_cacheMatchFnSourceUsesScoreDialect` — source confirms `_audioCacheMatchFor` calls `_scoreDialect` + tracks `best.score`
  - `r88_urlForFnSourceUsesScoreDialect` — same for `_audioUrlFor`
  - `r88_cacheMatchPrefersLebanese` — **behavioral**: seeded cache with `بكتاب`→MSA and `كتاب`→Lebanese; match returns the Lebanese one (and the `key` is `كتاب`, proving it reached the stripped variant before ranking)
  - `r88_cacheMatchFallsBackToMsaIfOnlyMsa` — **behavioral**: single cached MSA entry is still returned (no regression on under-covered words)
