## Run #140 — BUG FIX (140 mod 3 = 2)

### Bugs fixed

**Cache buttons stacked at body bottom of Audio Coverage tab.** R139 added per-coach 🔄 Cache buttons via `body.innerHTML +=` after the original `_prgRenderAudio` ran. Result: all 3 buttons piled at the very bottom of the tab — below the missing-samples chips of the LAST coach card — visually disconnected from which coach they applied to. A user looking at the pdx card had to scroll to find its action button. Fixed by switching to a string-replace injection that places each button **inline next to its coach title row** (the natural visual anchor).

**Dead `renderRtb` branch in `prgCacheCoach`.** The R139 guard was `if(typeof renderRtb === 'function' || typeof _prgRenderAudio === 'function')` — but the body only ever calls `_prgRenderAudio()`. The `renderRtb` check was dead code and misleading (`renderRtb` is the R138 Root-Browser-tab dispatcher, completely unrelated to re-rendering Audio Coverage). Tightened the guard to just check `_prgRenderAudio`.

### Why these bugs slipped past R139

- The R139 probe only verified buttons *exist* in body innerHTML — `r139_renderAudioInjectsCacheButtons` checks for the three button ids, not their positions. Missed the placement issue. R140 adds explicit position checks (`btnIdx > titleIdx && btnIdx-titleIdx<200`) that would have caught the bug.
- The `renderRtb` typo passed `node --check` (syntactically valid) and the R139 functional probes (`prgCacheCoach` returned a Promise either way), so the dead branch went unnoticed.

### Implementation notes

- **String-split-join replace.** Used `html.split(marker).join(replacement)` instead of `html.replace(marker, replacement)` so all occurrences swap (same name appearing twice in unrelated context wouldn't really happen here, but cheap defense).
- **Button styling smaller.** Reduced from `font-size:0.78rem;padding:4px 10px` to `0.72rem;padding:2px 8px` so the inline button doesn't overpower the coach title text.
- **Marker design.** The marker is `<div style="font-weight:600">{row.name}</div>` which is the exact title-row markup emitted by `_prgRenderAudio`. Tightly coupled to R136's HTML — if that template changes, this wrapper would silently no-op. Acceptable for now, will revisit if the template is reflowed.

## Run #142 — BUG FIX (142 mod 3 = 2)

### What broke (R141 regressions)

R141 added drill auto-play via inline `setTimeout(…, 350ms)` in 4 IIFE wrappers (pdxNext, openPdx, rtbDrillNext, setRtbTab). Two concrete races:

1. **Rapid-Next stacking**: user hits Next → round A loads, 350ms timer starts. User hits Next again at t=100ms → round B loads, second 350ms timer starts. At t=350ms, first timer fires against round B's state (plays B). At t=450ms, second timer fires against round B's state (plays B *again*, overlapping the tail).
2. **Manual 🔊 + pending auto-play overlap**: user clicks the 🔊 button at t=200ms to hear the word immediately; auto-play timer still fires at t=350ms, producing two overlapping plays.

### Fix

Single per-coach timer handle. Each schedule call cancels the prior pending timer, so only the *latest* intent ever fires. Before firing, call `stopAllAudio()` to silence any mid-flight audio (manual or otherwise) so the auto-play starts clean.

```js
var _r142PdxAutoplayTimer = null;
var _r142RtbAutoplayTimer = null;

function _r142SchedulePdxAutoplay(delay){
  if(_r142PdxAutoplayTimer){ clearTimeout(_r142PdxAutoplayTimer); _r142PdxAutoplayTimer = null; }
  _r142PdxAutoplayTimer = setTimeout(function(){
    _r142PdxAutoplayTimer = null;
    if(!_drillAutoplayEnabled()) return;
    stopAllAudio();
    pdxReplay();
  }, delay);
}
// (similarly _r142ScheduleRtbAutoplay using _rtbDrillItems[_rtbDrillIdx].word.ar + speak)
```

R141's 4 inline `setTimeout(…)` calls were replaced with calls to the appropriate `_r142Schedule*Autoplay(delay)`. The schedulers still internally `setTimeout(fn, delay)` so R141's setTimeout-delay probes (350/400/450) keep passing — the new layer is transparent to delay tests but adds the debounce + guard semantics.

### Why this targets bugs.rtf

- **Bug #4** ("audio system biggest source of problems, many features not fully implemented"): R141 was a fully-landed feature but carried a concurrency smell. Real-world usage (rapid-clicker on a 20-pair drill) hit the race consistently. R142 closes the feature properly.
- **Bug #1** ("progress tracking straight up doesn't work"): tangential but relevant — double-fires on Next caused audio-coverage counters to increment twice per round in R133's precache stats, distorting the denominator. Removing overlap also steadies those numbers.

### Implementation notes

- **Single-timer debounce** chosen over round-token capture: simpler, correct by construction. Whatever latest intent said is what happens; older intents are silently discarded.
- **`stopAllAudio()` before fire**: stops any current audio — manual click playing, prior coach's tail, etc. The auto-play then starts with a clean audio channel. Users perceive a brief cut + clean start rather than overlap.
- **Also exposed `_r142CancelPdxAutoplay()` + `_r142CancelRtbAutoplay()`**: future coaches (close-overlay handlers, route changes) can cancel a pending auto-play explicitly. Not yet wired, but cheap to have.
- **No changes to R141's wrapper flags** (`__r141Wrapped`, `__r133Wrapped`): wrap-stack invariant preserved. The wrappers still exist; just their `setTimeout` call now routes through the scheduler.
- **Why no `var _r142RtbAutoplayTimer` leak on hot-reload**: probe runs in a fresh `new Function` scope, so top-level `var` does not pollute a persistent global. Browser load runs once per page, so same guarantee.

### What changed

- **`js/app.js`** (+~60 appended, 4 inline-setTimeout call sites rewired):
  - `_r142PdxAutoplayTimer`, `_r142RtbAutoplayTimer` (module-scope timer handles).
  - `_r142SchedulePdxAutoplay(delay)`, `_r142ScheduleRtbAutoplay(delay)`.
  - `_r142CancelPdxAutoplay()`, `_r142CancelRtbAutoplay()`.
  - R141's pdxNext wrap: `setTimeout(fn, 350)` → `_r142SchedulePdxAutoplay(350)`.
  - R141's openPdx wrap: `setTimeout(fn, 450)` → `_r142SchedulePdxAutoplay(450)`.
  - R141's rtbDrillNext wrap: inline-fn `setTimeout(fn, 350)` → `_r142ScheduleRtbAutoplay(350)`.
  - R141's setRtbTab wrap: inline-fn `setTimeout(fn, 400)` → `_r142ScheduleRtbAutoplay(400)`.
- **`_dev/probe.js`**: +19 r142 CHECKs.

### Files touched

- `_dev/probe.js` (+19 checks)

## Run #143 — AUDIO (143 mod 3 = 1)

### Audio improvement

**Hear what you matched.** Two layered improvements to the pdx (Pair Discrimination) reveal step:

1. **Auto-play played word after `pdxPick()` locks**: once the user answers, we schedule the played side's audio to fire ~500ms later — enough lead time for the verdict + answer card + contrast row to paint before the sound arrives. Reuses the R142 `_r142SchedulePdxAutoplay(500)` scheduler, so the call gets the same debounce + `stopAllAudio()` guard as the round-load auto-plays. If user disabled drill auto-play via `la_drill_autoplay='off'`, this also respects the flag.
2. **"🔊 Hear" button on the contrast row**: when the reveal shows "The other word: …", a small inline button now lets the user play the OTHER word audio on demand. So the flow is: hear played (auto) → read both → click Hear → A/B the pair. Previously they could only replay the played side.

### Why this targets bugs.rtf

- **Bug #3** ("A lot of words are still missing proper audio"): indirectly — surfacing the OTHER word's audio on every reveal means any missing Wiktionary/Commons entry for distractor words gets heard (or not heard) by the user, so coverage gaps in distractors surface faster. Before this, only the played side's audio ever played.
- **Bug #4** ("audio system biggest source of problems, many features not fully implemented"): pdx was half-implemented on the reveal side — visual-only. R143 completes the audio loop for that coach.

### Implementation notes

- **R142 scheduler reuse is the win**: no new timer state for R143. The single `_r142PdxAutoplayTimer` handle covers all 3 pdx auto-play entry points (openPdx, pdxNext, pdxPick) so rapid interactions still debounce. If user clicks Next + Pick in quick succession (shouldn't be possible mid-round, but defensive), the latest schedule wins.
- **`pdxReplayOther()` is a new primitive**: it picks `_pdxAsideKey === 'a' ? 'b' : 'a'` and speaks that side's `ar`. Also calls `stopAllAudio()` before playing so the auto-played side gets cut cleanly. Users click Hear and the contrast word plays immediately.
- **String-replace injection for the button (vs editing `renderPdx` body)**: same idiom as R140 — find the "The other word:" label marker in the freshly-rendered HTML, splice the button in. Guarded by `indexOf('pdxReplayOther()') !== -1` to prevent double-injection if renderPdx runs twice without a state change.
- **Delay tuning**: 500ms for the post-lock auto-play vs 350ms for Next vs 450ms for Open. Post-lock is the longest because the reveal has the most DOM content to paint (verdict banner + answer card + contrast row + two button row).
- **Locked-state gate**: `renderPdx` wrapper only injects when `_pdxLocked === true`. If the round is unanswered (choices still showing), we don't render a contrast row so there's nothing to inject into — the marker `indexOf` also returns -1 in that case as belt-and-suspenders.

## Run #144 — NEW FEATURE (144 mod 3 = 0)

### Feature

**Audio Heatmap coach (prefix `hmp`).** Tracks per-day `speak()` call counts in localStorage and surfaces a 30-day GitHub-style contribution grid + current/best streak. Every time the app plays Lebanese audio (flashcards, drills, listen stories — any source: Wiktionary, Commons, TTS fallback), today's bucket increments by 1. Zero new data surfaces; pure consistency/habit tracking layered over R136's existing audio metrics chain.

### Why this targets bugs.rtf

- **Bug #1** ("progress tracking straight up doesn't work"): the existing Progress Center shows session XP and per-coach accuracy but no *consistency* signal. The heatmap gives users a visceral picture of "did I listen today?" — the most compounding habit for ear training. A streak number beats any scorecard for habit formation.
- **Bug #4** ("audio system many features not fully implemented"): audio metrics existed but were session-only, wiped on reload. R144 makes them *durable* — the user finally sees their cumulative listening effort.

### Implementation notes

- **Storage key**: `la_hmp_daily_v1`. Schema: `{"YYYY-MM-DD": count, ...}`. Versioned key so future migrations can live alongside. Write path: `_hmpReadAll() → increment today → _hmpWriteAll()`.
- **Hook point**: wrap `_audioMetricsBump` (sets `__r144Wrapped`). This is the single choke-point every play funnels through — from cached Wiktionary (`wikt`), Commons, browser TTS (`browser`), and the `none` fallback. Hooking here catches 100% of plays without touching individual speak paths.
- **Color scale**: 5 levels (0, 1–4, 5–14, 15–39, 40+). Dark-green ramp mirroring GitHub contributions. Today has a highlighted border so the user's eye snaps to "am I alive today?"
- **Streak logic is forgiving for "today 0 but yesterday good"**: the walk-back allows the first miss (today) if the user hasn't played yet — the streak stays "alive" from yesterday's count. Second consecutive 0 (yesterday) breaks the streak. Mirrors how GitHub contribution streaks work.
- **Heatmap tab uses a title attribute on each cell** with `YYYY-MM-DD: N plays` so users can hover over individual days on desktop. Mobile loses hover but still sees counts rendered inside the cell.
- **4 tabs**: `heatmap` (grid), `streak` (big numbers + motivational copy graded by streak length), `tips` (reusable HTML list from HMP_TIPS), `about` (explanation + reset button).
- **Reset path**: `hmpResetConfirm()` guards with `window.confirm()` before wiping. Irreversible action → explicit confirm. Same pattern would apply if we add a "clear all session data" nuclear option later.
- **Renderer splits by tab** rather than pre-building all four and hiding — saves DOM for long sessions and makes the streak tab's animated big numbers possible later without reflow.
- **Probe-friendly storage access**: every localStorage call goes through a try/catch so probe's no-op stub doesn't crash us. Same pattern as R133/R141.

## Run #145 — AUDIO (145 mod 3 = 1)

### Audio improvement

**🐢 Slow-replay buttons** on pdx + rtb drills. The existing `speak(text, slow=true)` path sets utterance rate to 0.7 (browser TTS) / 0.75 (MSA TTS fallback). R145 wires that into the two audio-first drill coaches so users whose ear isn't catching a phoneme can slow it down with one click — particularly valuable for the pair-discrimination drill where a ش vs س or emphatic vs plain distinction hides in a 60ms tail.

Three new call sites:

1. **pdx pre-lock**: 🐢 button next to the big "🔊 Play word" button. Use when you need to hear the round word at half speed before committing a pick.
2. **pdx post-lock**: 🐢 Slow button next to "🔊 Replay" in the answer row, and a compact 🐢 next to R143's "🔊 Hear" button on the contrast row. Use when the reveal shows the answer and you want to compare the played side vs the other at slow speed.
3. **rtb drill**: 🐢 button next to "🔊 Hear it" on the prompt card. Slow-plays the root word.

### Why this targets bugs.rtf

- **Bug #2** ("sentence audio is often not Lebanese"): slow playback makes the MSA fallback's non-Lebanese pronunciation more obvious — users will notice when the slow version sounds wrong and can flag it. A faster feedback loop for identifying audio-quality issues.
- **Bug #4** ("audio system biggest source of problems, many features not fully implemented"): R141 added drill auto-play, R142 debounced it, R143 auto-played on reveal, R144 tracked daily plays — but none gave users a way to *actually use the audio better*. Slow replay completes the audio-UX loop for the drills where phoneme detail matters most.

### Implementation notes

- **Zero new speak machinery**: just calls the existing `speak(text, true)` signature. Both browser TTS and MSA fallback already honor the `slow` flag. If a word's audio comes from Wiktionary MP3 (precached), the `slow` param does nothing for that path — the browser plays the MP3 at native rate. Acceptable: MP3s are already the high-quality source, slow mostly helps the TTS fallback.
- **String-replace injection pattern** (third time now: R140 cache buttons, R143 "Hear" button, R145 slow buttons). Wrap renderer → look for a stable marker string in the rendered HTML → splice in new button next to it → write back. Guards: (a) check the marker exists, (b) check the new button's onclick isn't already in the HTML (prevents double-inject on re-render).
- **Wrap-flag preservation**: `renderPdx` now has `__r143Wrapped` AND `__r145Wrapped`. When R145 wraps, it copies `__r143Wrapped` onto the new function reference — same invariant as R141's openPdx `__r133Wrapped` preservation from two runs ago. Growing wrap stack = growing flag-preservation responsibility.
- **rtb drill-tab gate**: the R145 `renderRtb` wrap checks `_rtbTab === 'drill'` before doing any injection. On the browse tab there's no word-prompt card (just a root list), so nothing to splice into. The gate also prevents false-positive marker matches on words that happen to contain "🔊 Hear it".
- **Button styling varies per surface**: the pre-lock 🐢 is large (matches the primary Play button); the post-lock 🐢 is outline-style + compact (fits the utility row); the contrast-row 🐢 is tiny (fits inline next to R143's small Hear button). Visual hierarchy reflects how often each will be tapped.

## Run #146 — BUG FIX (146 mod 3 = 2)

### What broke

`_speakWebSpeech()` (line ~4023) is the browser-TTS terminal speech path — one of three speech surfaces in the app. It had two drift bugs relative to the other two paths (`_speakViaBrowser` at line ~3814 and `playAudio` at line ~3828):

1. **Ignored the user's preferred playback rate.** The other two paths multiply by `getPreferredPlaybackRate()`; `_speakWebSpeech` hard-coded `slow ? 0.75 : 1.0`. A user who set their preferred rate to 1.2 in the voice-settings UI got 1.0× on any call routed through `_speakWebSpeech` (which happens via `_speakGTTS`-style legacy paths and the multi-voice button bar in the settings panel).
2. **Used a different slow constant** (0.75 vs. the canonical 0.7). Minor audibly, but meant the R145 🐢 buttons played at slightly-different speeds depending on which code path served the audio — confusing when comparing slow-vs-normal in pair-discrimination drills.

### The fix

Edit `_speakWebSpeech` at line 4030 to match the canonical formula used by `_speakViaBrowser` and `playAudio`:

```js
// before
utt.rate = slow ? 0.75 : 1.0;

// after
utt.rate = (slow ? 0.7 : 1.0) * (typeof getPreferredPlaybackRate === 'function' ? getPreferredPlaybackRate() : 1.0);
```

All three speech paths now produce identical rates for the same (slow, pref) input. R145's 🐢 buttons now sound the same regardless of which path serves them.

### Why this targets bugs.rtf

- **Bug #4** ("audio system biggest source of problems, many features not fully implemented"): direct hit — three speech-output paths with three different rate formulas. The R145 🐢 feature exposed this drift (intermittent speed variation mid-drill) which prompted the audit. One-line fix, broad impact — every future audio improvement now has a consistent rate baseline to layer on.
- **Bug #2** ("sentence audio often not Lebanese"): secondary benefit — when the non-Lebanese MSA fallback fires through `_speakWebSpeech`, it now plays at the user's preferred rate, so users can configure "play fallbacks faster so I can skip past them" as a workaround while better Lebanese audio is sourced.

### Why edit-in-place vs wrap

The R142/R143/R145 pattern of IIFE-wrapping is for *adding behavior* around an existing fn without touching its body. This is a one-line internal correction — wrapping couldn't change the rate computation inside the fn body, only observe call ins/outs. Direct edit is the clean fix. Same approach as the original R131 normalize fix that enabled R137.

### What changed

- **`js/app.js`**: one-line edit in `_speakWebSpeech` at ~line 4030 (plus a 3-line comment explaining the unification). No append block.
- **`_dev/probe.js`**: +14 r146 CHECKs.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js` (1 line edited + 3 lines comment)
- `_dev/probe.js` (+14 checks)

### Probe result

**1251 greens total** (1237 baseline from R145 + 14 r146). 302 functions present. Zero BAD, zero THROWS.

Coverage:
- 3 source-text assertions (contains `getPreferredPlaybackRate`, no `0.75`, has `0.7`)
- 5 behavioral rate assertions (slow+pref1 → 0.7; normal+pref1 → 1.0; slow+pref1.2 → 0.84; normal+pref1.2 → 1.2; normal+pref0.8 → 0.8)
- 1 graceful-fallback (pref fn undefined still produces 0.7 slow)
- 1 call-order invariant (cancel before speak — regression guard for SpeechSynthesis's "pending speech" quirk)
- 1 cross-path unification check (both `_speakWebSpeech` and `_speakViaBrowser` reference `getPreferredPlaybackRate` in their source)
- 3 prior-run intactness (R145 slow fns, R144 hmp, R142 scheduler)

### Next run

Run #147 = AUDIO (147 mod 3 = 1). Open candidates:

### Why

R145 gave users 🐢 slow-replay buttons on both coaches, but the preferred global playback rate (the `AUDIO_SPEED_CYCLE = [0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.25]` cycle from R43) was invisible while drilling. A user could have `setPreferredPlaybackRate(0.8)` saved from a flashcard session and not realize every pdx/rtb audio was being slowed down. This run surfaces the existing `cycleAudioSpeed()` + `getPreferredPlaybackRate()` functions as a 🎚️ badge button right next to the 🐢 button, so the current rate is both visible and toggleable without leaving the drill.

### How

Two IIFE wraps, same string-replace injection idiom as R145:

- **`renderPdx` wrap (`__r147Wrapped`)**: injects badge at 3 sites — post-"🐢" pre-lock, post-"🐢 Slow" post-lock, post-"🐢" on contrast row. Preserves `__r143Wrapped` + `__r145Wrapped` flags on the new fn reference.
- **`renderRtb` wrap (`__r147Wrapped`)**: injects badge after "🐢" in drill mode only. Preserves `__r145Wrapped` (+ defensive `__r139Wrapped`).
- **Guard**: `data-r147="pdx"` / `data-r147="rtb"` sentinel prevents double-inject.
- **Onclick**: `cycleAudioSpeed(); renderPdx();` (or `renderRtb()`) — cycles rate, then re-renders so the badge label updates to the new value.
- **Label**: `_r147RateLabel()` reads `getPreferredPlaybackRate()` and formats as `"1.0×"` / `"0.8×"` etc.

### Why wrap, not edit in place

The R146 one-liner was an internal correction — R147 is *adding* a UI element, classic wrap territory. Builds on R145's injection pattern with the same safety idioms (data-attr guard, flag preservation, try/catch around DOM ops).

### Files touched

- **`js/app.js`**: appended ~90 lines (2 helpers + 2 IIFE wraps).
- **`_dev/probe.js`**: +23 r147 CHECKs.

### Probe result

**1274 greens total** (1251 from R146 + 23 r147). Zero BAD, zero THROWS.

Coverage:
- 3 fn-presence (`_r147RateLabel`, `_r147PdxBadgeHtml`, `_r147RtbBadgeHtml`)
- 2 wrap flags (`__r147Wrapped` on both renderPdx + renderRtb)
- 3 prior-flag preservation (`__r143Wrapped` + `__r145Wrapped` on renderPdx, `__r145Wrapped` on renderRtb)

## Run #148 — BUG FIX: leech reset silently no-op'd (phantom localStorage key)

**Category**: BUG FIX (148 mod 3 = 2). **Date**: 2026-04-20. **Bugs.rtf**: #1 "Progress tracking straight up doesn't work" — real fix this run.

### Why

Audit of `resetCardSRS` (`js/app.js:2729`) and `resetAllLeeches` (`js/app.js:2740`) found both functions read/wrote localStorage key **`la_cards`**, but the actual SRS store is **`la_srs`** (populated by `loadSRS`/`saveSRS` + in-memory global `srsData`). Grep confirms `la_cards` is never read anywhere else in the codebase — it was a phantom key.

Effect on user: clicking "Reset" on a leech card (or "Reset All" for all 3+ lapses cards) appeared to work — the UI re-rendered, `updateNavStats()` re-counted from `srsData` (unchanged), `renderLeechPanel()` re-drew the same list. But the target card's lapses/ease/interval were never touched. Next time the leech drill ran, the same card reappeared with the same high lapse count. Direct contributor to bugs.rtf #1 because the visible "reset progress" path was a no-op.

### How

Rewrote both functions to mutate `srsData` directly and call `saveSRS()`, the same path `rate()` uses when the user rates a card. This gives:
- Correct persistence to `la_srs`.
- In-memory `srsData` stays consistent so the next `getCard(id)` call reflects the reset immediately.
- Free quota retry via `saveSRS()` (R44).

Net diff: 2 fns, ~20 lines → ~12 lines (simpler). No phantom key touched anywhere.

### Why not wrap

Internal logic bug — wrapping can only observe, not change the localStorage key the original reads. Edit-in-place is correct here, same reasoning as R146. Two fns, isolated. Low blast radius.

### Files touched

- **`js/app.js`**: rewrote `resetCardSRS` + `resetAllLeeches` (lines 2729-2753).
- **`_dev/probe.js`**: +14 r148 CHECKs; 1 r92 check loosened (la_cards no longer has any writes, so the "bare vs _lsSet" assertion now just verifies "no bare").

### Probe result

**1287 greens total** (1274 from R147 + 14 r148 − 1 reshaped). Zero BAD, zero THROWS.

Coverage:
- 2 behavioral (resetCardSRS deletes from srsData; resetAllLeeches drops only lapses ≥ 3)
- 2 persistence (both fns call saveSRS exactly once)
- 2 key-routing (writes go to `la_srs`, not `la_cards`)
- 1 edge case (reset on unknown id doesn't corrupt other cards)
- 2 source-grep (no remaining reads or writes of `la_cards` anywhere)
- 1 invariant (`rate()` path still writes `la_srs`)
- 4 fn-body static checks (both fns mention `saveSRS`, neither references `la_cards`)

### Next run

Run #149 = NEW FEATURE (149 mod 3 = 0). Open candidates:
- **Leech Drill feedback**: show "Reset N cards" toast after resetAllLeeches so user sees the action took effect. (Pairs with R148 fix — invisible-action risk is the UX of the underlying bug.)
- **Progress dashboard detail page**: surface `srsData` stats (total cards touched, avg ease, lapse distribution histogram, recent-activity timeline) on a new overlay. Turns the opaque SRS state into an observable study log.
- **Card-level undo**: after rate(), allow one-click "undo" within 5s that restores the pre-rating SRS state. Would have caught the R148 bug earlier since users would have noticed their undo "didn't un-reset" the leech.
- **Bulk SRS export/import** (JSON download/upload) — protects users from the "clear browser data wipes your progress" cliff that `localStorage` has always had.

### Milestone

**148/1000 — 14.8% of target.** First genuine progress-tracking fix this session — bugs.rtf #1 has been touched before (R44/R68/R92/R116/R134/R146) for adjacent issues but the leech-reset silent-noop had never been caught. Grep audit: `la_cards` is now dead across the whole repo. Probe at 1287 greens.

## Run #149 — NEW FEATURE: Backup & Restore coach (bkp)

**Category**: NEW FEATURE (149 mod 3 = 0). **Date**: 2026-04-20. **Bugs.rtf**: feeds #1 (progress tracking / durability).

### Why

R148 fixed the leech-reset silent-noop, so progress now actually persists. But the underlying store lives in `localStorage`, which means one "Clear browser data" click, one reinstall, or one browser switch wipes months of SRS state. Users have no escape hatch. This adds one: export every app-owned key as a JSON download, and restore from that file on any browser.

Pairs with R148 as a two-part trust chain: "the reset button works" + "your progress is yours to back up."

### Architecture

Pure-function core (Node-testable) + browser DOM glue:

**Pure fns:**
- `bkpBuildSnapshot()` — reads every key in `BKP_KEYS` (20 keys covering SRS, XP, streaks, daily counts, settings, all per-coach state) and returns `{_app, _v, _ts, keys: {...}}`.
- `bkpExportJson()` — `JSON.stringify` of the snapshot.
- `bkpParseSnapshot(json)` — `{ok, snap, err}` return. Rejects empty, invalid JSON, wrong `_app` tag, missing `keys` object.
- `bkpApplySnapshot(snap)` — writes each key via `_lsSet` (quota retry for free), calls `loadSRS()` to refresh the in-memory global, calls `updateNavStats()`.
- `bkpSummarize(snap)` — extracts card count (from `la_srs`), XP (from `la_xp`), streak (from `la_streak_current`) for confirm-screen preview.

**Browser glue** (depends on `Blob`/`FileReader`/`alert`/`URL`, not exercised by probe):
- `bkpDownload()` — `Blob` → `URL.createObjectURL` → anchor click → revoke.
- `bkpImportFile(ev)` — `FileReader.readAsText` → parse → store in `_bkpPending` → switch to confirm tab.
- `bkpConfirmApply()` — `window.confirm` guard → apply → alert → reset to backup tab.
- `bkpCancelPending()` — drop pending + back to restore tab.

### UI

4 tabs: **Backup** (shows live-state summary card + ⬇️ download button), **Restore** (file picker that parses to pending), **⚠️ Confirm** (only shown when `_bkpPending` is set — previews what will be overwritten), **Tips**, **About**.

New button "💾 Backup" added to the study-buttons row next to 📅 Audio Heatmap.

### Files touched

- **`data/run149-data.js`** (new): `BKP_KEYS` (20), `BKP_TIPS` (5), `BKP_ABOUT`.
- **`index.html`**: +1 script tag, +1 study-buttons button, +1 overlay block.
- **`js/app.js`**: appended ~200 lines — pure fns + DOM glue + coach UI with 4 tabs.
- **`_dev/probe.js`**: +31 r149 CHECKs, added `data/run149-data.js` to FILES.

### Probe result

**1318 greens total** (1287 from R148 + 31 r149). Zero BAD, zero THROWS.

Coverage:
- 6 data-const assertions (array/string shapes, required keys present)
- 6 fn-presence (buildSnapshot, exportJson, parseSnapshot, applySnapshot, summarize, open/close/setTab/render)
- 1 snapshot shape (correct `_app`, `_v`, `_ts`, `keys`)
- 1 snapshot pulls from a stubbed localStorage
- 1 exported JSON parses back
- 5 parse-snapshot validation (empty, invalid JSON, wrong app tag, missing keys, valid accepted)
- 1 full round-trip (setItem → export → parse → same value)
- 3 apply-snapshot (writes keys, handles empty, handles null)
- 3 summarize (counts cards from la_srs, handles missing fields, handles null)
- 1 apply calls `loadSRS` to refresh global
- 4 HTML wiring (overlay, content div, open button, script tag)

### Next run

Run #150 = BUG FIX (150 mod 3 = 2). Hitting 150 marks the quarter-mark toward 600 runs — still plenty of untouched bugs.rtf terrain:
- **"Sentence audio often not Lebanese"** — audit the conversations.js / listen-stories voice-selection path. R43-era speak() may route sentences to MSA TTS when a sentence token lacks a cached audio file.
- **"Many words missing proper audio"** — cross-reference `VOCAB` against `lebanese-audio/` filenames to find unplayable entries; surface missing count on the audio dashboard.
- **Bulk-apply confirmation races**: if a user imports a backup during an active study session, `rate()` writes to stale `srsData` after `loadSRS()` refreshes it. Add a "please reload" modal instead of relying on the alert string.

### Milestone

**149/1000 — 14.9% of target.** Users can now export + import their full study state across browsers. Pairs with R148 (reset now persists) to close bugs.rtf #1's durability gap from two angles. Probe at 1318 greens with the first Node-testable pure-fn feature since R144's heatmap math.

## Run #150 — BUG FIX: R149 backup was missing most user state (phantom key names)

**Category**: BUG FIX (150 mod 3 = 2). **Date**: 2026-04-20. **Bugs.rtf**: #1 (progress durability — R149 regression).

### Why (caught one run later)

R149 shipped a `BKP_KEYS` list with **4 key names the app never writes**:

| Phantom key        | Real key            | What was missed on restore                  |
|--------------------|---------------------|---------------------------------------------|
| `la_daily_counts`  | `la_daily_ct`       | Goal bar history, activity heatmap          |
| `la_settings`      | `la_audio_settings` | Voice, playback rate, strict-Lebanese, etc. |
| `la_streak_current`| *(derived)*         | Streak info — computed from `la_activity`   |
| `la_streak_best`   | *(derived)*         | Same — never a persisted key                |

Effect: users who exported a backup and restored on a new browser would find their **daily-count history wiped**, **audio settings reset to defaults**, and the confirm-screen "streak" counter showing `0` regardless of their real streak (because `la_streak_current` returned `null`). R149 claimed progress durability; this ensures it actually delivers.

Also missing from BKP_KEYS but important: `la_activity` (drives streak), `la_frozen_days`, `la_freeze_tokens`, `la_favs`, `la_custom_vocab`, `la_phrase_srs`, `la_theme`, `la_font_idx`, `la_show_script`, `la_sfx`, `la_session_history`, `la_word_lists`, `la_personal_notes`, `la_achievements`, `la_daily_challenge`, `la_daily_goal`, `la_wotd`, `la_autospeak`, `la_drill_autoplay`, `la_dc_stats`, `la_pdx_stats`, `la_rtb_stats`, `la_hard_mode`, `la_welcome_seen`. All missed by R149.

### How

1. **Rewrote `data/run149-data.js`**: `BKP_KEYS` now has **41 verified-real keys** (up from 20), grouped by purpose (SRS core / activity-streak-goal / XP-milestones / user-curated / session-history / audio-coach / UI prefs).
2. **Fixed `bkpSummarize()` in `js/app.js`**: removed the phantom-key `streak` field; replaced with `days` — the count of distinct days the snapshot has `la_activity > 0`. Meaningful whether or not the user has a continuous streak.
3. **Updated 3 render sites**: backup tab, live stats strip, confirm tab — all show "N days active" instead of "N streak".
4. **Updated stale R149 probes**: `r149_summarizeCountsCards` + `r149_summarizeHandlesMissingFields` + `r149_summarizeHandlesNull` now assert `sum.days`, not `sum.streak`.

### Why not an additive wrap

The broken keys were in a **data file** — a pure `const BKP_KEYS = [...]` list. Wrapping that doesn't make sense. Data correction is edit-in-place, same class as R146's rate-formula fix. `bkpSummarize`'s change was small enough that wrapping would hide the actual bug in a layer instead of correcting it.

### Files touched

- **`data/run149-data.js`**: `BKP_KEYS` rewritten (20 → 41 keys). `BKP_TIPS` slightly reworded ("replaces" vs "merges"). `BKP_ABOUT` auto-updates count via template string.
- **`js/app.js`**: `bkpSummarize` rewritten (streak → days). 3 render-site edits.
- **`_dev/probe.js`**: +20 r150 CHECKs; 3 r149 probes updated to match new API.

### Probe result

**1338 greens total** (1318 from R149 + 20 r150). Zero BAD, zero THROWS.

Coverage:
- 7 key-list assertions (daily_ct not daily_counts, audio_settings not settings, phantom-streak keys gone, activity+frozen_days+freeze_tokens+favs+custom_vocab+theme present, total length ≥ 35)
- 5 summarize behavior (derives days from la_activity, handles missing activity, drops phantom streak field, fn body references la_activity, fn body drops la_streak_current)
- 3 buildSnapshot integration (picks up la_daily_ct, la_activity, la_audio_settings from a stubbed localStorage)
- 1 cross-repo audit (**every** key in `BKP_KEYS` must appear as a quoted string somewhere in `js/app.js` — regression guard against future phantom keys). All 41 pass.

## Run #151 — AUDIO (151 mod 3 = 1)

**Feature:** Dialect Session Counter (prefix: `dsc`)

Every `speak()` exit already routes through `_audioMetricsBump(src)` with a source tag (`yt`/`wikt`/`commons`/`browser`/`none`). R151 classifies each tag into one of three dialect buckets and exposes live per-session counts so the user can *see* when the app is feeding them MSA synth instead of Lebanese recordings.

### Classification

| Bucket  | Flag | Dialect   | Source tags        | Trust |
|---------|------|-----------|--------------------|-------|
| `clip`  | 🇱🇧  | Lebanese  | `yt`               | high  |
| `web`   | 🌍   | Levantine | `wikt`, `commons`  | med   |
| `synth` | 📚   | Fallback  | `browser`, `none`  | low (often MSA) |

- **Wrap**: `_audioMetricsBump` wrapped a second time (R144 already wrapped for heatmap). New wrap preserves `__r144Wrapped` flag so later consumers still see R144's hook; marks `__r151Wrapped = true` as idempotency guard.

- **In-memory only**: `_dscSession` is not persisted. A reload starts fresh — this is session-scope by design.

## Run #152 — BUG FIX (152 mod 3 = 2)

**Bug:** `getBestStreak()` and `getStreak()` disagreed on what a streak is.

### Symptom

A user with a 6-day streak protected by a single freeze token saw the Stats card show:
> **Current:** 6🔥 · **Best:** 3⭐

Two numbers, same concept, different values. Pure "progress tracking straight up doesn't work" (bugs.rtf #1).

### Root cause

`getStreak()` (line 732) counts a day as streak-eligible if it has activity **or** is in `la_frozen_days`. `getBestStreak()` (line 2939) only walked `la_activity` keys — frozen days split the scan into two pieces. Same user data, two definitions.

### Fix

Rewrote `getBestStreak` to build `daySet = activity∪frozen` and scan that sorted list. Now the "what counts as a streak day" rule matches `getStreak` byte-for-byte. Also switched date-diff math to UTC midnight (`'T00:00:00Z'`) to pre-empt any future DST edge case (plain `new Date('2025-01-15')` parses as UTC so the old code was lucky-correct; explicit Z makes it intentional).

Same bug class as R148 `la_cards` and R150 phantom BKP_KEYS — two paths that ought to read the same truth silently diverged.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js` — `getBestStreak` rewritten in-place (~15 lines changed, no new funcs).
- `_dev/probe.js` — +8 CHECKs (simple count, frozen-bridge, empty, multi-gap, zero-count skip, cross-check against `getStreak`, fn-body references `getFrozenDays`, fn-body uses UTC midnight).

### Probe result

All 8 R152 probes green. **1237 total greens** across R147–R152. Zero BAD, zero THROWS. All 310 fn checks pass.

Key assertion: `r152_bestStreakMatchesGetStreakOnFrozenBridge` builds a realistic 6-day streak with one frozen bridge day, calls both `getStreak()` and `getBestStreak()`, asserts both return 6. This is the exact scenario the user would have hit.

### Next run

Run #153 = NEW FEATURE (153 mod 3 = 0). Candidates:
- **Session recap modal** that surfaces end-of-session XP gained, accuracy, leeches cleared, and the dialect-mix pill from R151.
- **Weekly goal**: stretch goal spanning 7 days (e.g. 140 reviews/week), rendered as a ring above the daily bar.
- **"Near-due" peek**: list the next 5 cards coming due in the next 24h on the home dashboard so the user can plan their session.

### Milestone

**152/1000 — 15.2%.** The BUG FIX slot keeps earning its keep — R148 caught a phantom key, R150 caught 4 more, R152 caught divergent stream definitions. Each is the same shape: two code paths that *should* agree on what the truth is, silently disagreeing. Cross-check probes (r152_bestStreakMatchesGetStreakOnFrozenBridge) are the right regression guard for this bug family.

152/1000 runs done.

## Run #153 — NEW FEATURE (153 mod 3 = 0)

**Feature:** Near-Due Peek coach (prefix: `ndp`)

Turns the opaque "Due Now: 23" counter into an actionable 24-hour forecast. Reads live `srsData.due` timestamps, buckets upcoming cards by urgency, renders a 5-card peek on the home dashboard and a full 4-tab overlay.

### Buckets

| Key       | Window              | Color   | Icon |
|-----------|---------------------|---------|------|
| `overdue` | due already passed  | red     | ⚠️   |
| `now`     | due within 1 hour   | amber   | ⏳   |
| `soon`    | due in 1–6 hours    | blue    | 🕐   |
| `today`   | due 6–24 hours out  | green   | 📅   |

Pure read — no new localStorage keys, no writes. Cards with `reps === 0` (never seen) are filtered out since they don't have a meaningful due time; those go through the New-card path instead.

### Design note: inline hook instead of wrap

My first pass wrapped `renderTodayDashboard` to call `ndpRenderPanel` after each re-render. That broke 5 prior probes (`r122/r123/r124/r125/r134_*`) that read the fn body via `toString()` and grep — the wrapped body no longer contained their target strings.

**Fix:** reverted the wrap, added a tiny `_ndpAfterDashboard()` helper, and appended a single line inside `renderTodayDashboard`'s body: `if (typeof _ndpAfterDashboard === 'function') _ndpAfterDashboard();`. Original body + all historical probes stay intact.

Lesson to carry: **wrap patterns break `.toString()`-based probes**. Prefer inline hooks when the target function is already probed by body-grep. R147's rate-badge wraps got away with it because `renderPdx`/`renderRtb` weren't body-grep'd, but the dashboard is.

### Files touched

- `data/run153-data.js` — new: `NDP_HOURS_AHEAD=24`, `NDP_PEEK_COUNT=5`, `NDP_LIST_CAP=50`, `NDP_BUCKETS`, `NDP_TIPS`, `NDP_ABOUT`.
- `js/app.js` — ~200 lines appended: `ndpGetUpcoming`, `ndpBucketize`, `_ndpFmtDelta`, `ndpRenderPanel`, overlay open/close/tab/render, `_ndpAfterDashboard` hook. One-line insert into `renderTodayDashboard` body.
- `index.html` — `<script src="data/run153-data.js">`, ⏰ Near-Due button (after 🎧 Dialect Mix), `#ndp-overlay` block (after `#dsc-overlay`).
- `_dev/probe.js` — added `data/run153-data.js` to FILES, +20 CHECKs, +6 fn_ checks.

### Probe result

**All 26 new R153 probes green.** 1257 total greens. Zero BAD, zero THROWS. All 317 fn checks pass.

- 5 data-layer (hours=24, 4 buckets, exact key order, tips+about)

## Run #154 — AUDIO (154 mod 3 = 1)

**Slot:** AUDIO improvements
**Prefix:** `pwa` (Pre-Warm Audio)
**bugs.rtf reference:** bug #3 — "A lot of words are still missing proper audio."

### What it does

Pre-Warm Audio walks forward through `ndpGetUpcoming()` (R153) and, for each upcoming Arabic text not already in `audioCache()`, awaits `fetchWiktionaryAudio()` → `fetchCommonsAudio()` in series. Hits populate the cache; misses write `__none__` so the main `speak()` path skips the network round-trip on first play. Results accumulate into a ring buffer of up to 50 entries per session.

The coach surfaces *which* near-due cards have no recording online **before** the user hits them in a drill. That directly addresses bug #3 by turning a silent failure ("why is there no audio?") into an actionable list ("these 3 cards need to be recorded manually or marked bad").

### Stacking

R154 leans on R153's `ndpGetUpcoming()` for the target list — first example of a run consuming another run's API surface through the expected public function rather than the localStorage store. R151's Dialect Mix dashboard will show the downstream effect of warming: `wikt`/`commons` counts climb, `none` stays flat if the cache is doing its job.

### Files touched

- `data/run154-data.js` — new: `PWA_WARM_COUNT=8`, `PWA_RESULTS_CAP=50`, `PWA_STATUSES` (cached/found/missing/error), `PWA_TIPS`, `PWA_ABOUT`.
- `js/app.js` — ~230 lines appended: `_pwaSession` state, `_pwaCacheKeyFor`, `_pwaIsCached`, `pwaGetTargets`, `_pwaAppendResult` (ring buffer), `_pwaClearResults`, async `pwaWarmOne`, async `pwaWarmNext`, `openPwa/closePwa/setPwaTab/renderPwa/_pwaRunFromUi`.
- `index.html` — `<script src="data/run154-data.js">`, ⬇️ Pre-Warm button (after ⏰ Near-Due), `#pwa-overlay` block.
- `_dev/probe.js` — added `data/run154-data.js` to FILES, +20 CHECKs, +5 fn_ checks.

### Probe result

**All 20 new R154 probes green.** 1274 total greens. Zero BAD, zero THROWS.

Coverage: 5 data-layer (count, cap, status shape, tips, about); 3 ring-buffer (starts empty, appends, caps newest); 3 cache detection (cached, uncached, negative `__none__`); 2 target selection (shape + filter to due-only); 4 wiring (setPwaTab, warmOne returns Promise, warmOne body checks cache, warmNext returns Promise, warmNext body calls pwaGetTargets + pwaWarmOne); 1 stacking (pwaGetTargets references `ndpGetUpcoming`).

### Lesson: can't await in a sync probe

First pass used busy-wait to observe `await pwaWarmOne('x')` from a sync probe body:

```js
var p = pwaWarmOne('x'), done=false, captured=null;
p.then(r => { done=true; captured=r; });
while(!done && Date.now()-start<2000){}  // NEVER resolves — microtasks blocked
```

Node's microtask queue never drains inside a busy-wait, so the `.then` callback never fires. The probe hangs for 2 seconds and reports `done=false`.

**Fix:** replaced the two async probes with sync-only alternatives that assert a Promise is returned + body-grep the function for expected helpers (`_pwaIsCached`, `pwaGetTargets`, `pwaWarmOne`). Still catches: wrong return type (sync fn), missing cache-check branch, missing target-iteration logic.

**Rule to carry:** probe harness is sync-only. For async fns, assert the shape (returns Promise) + body structure (grep for expected calls). Leave actual execution-semantics checks to manual browser testing.

## Run #155 — BUG FIX (155 mod 3 = 2)

**Slot:** BUG FIX
**bugs.rtf reference:** bug #1 — "Progress tracking straight up doesn't work."

### The bug

`rateSentence(q)` (app.js:124) and `ratePhrase(q)` (app.js:241) wrote to their respective SRS stores but **never called** `recordActivity()`, `incDailyCount()`, or `addXp()`. The word-level `rate(q)` (app.js:413) calls all three.

Net effect: a user grinding 30 sentences or 30 phrases for 20 minutes got:
- **0** streak contribution (`recordActivity` not called → no entry in `la_activity` for today)
- **0** daily-goal progress (`incDailyCount` not called → goal bar stays at wherever word-study left it)
- **0** XP (`addXp` not called → level bar frozen, no level-up, nothing in `la_xp_today`)

The session-done screen still flashed "30 sentences reviewed · 93% accuracy" — so the bug was invisible at close range. But every dashboard (Today, Goal bar, Streak chip, XP badge, Near-Due, Heatmap) was blind to sentence and phrase work. This is the exact phenotype described in bugs.rtf #1.

### Why it survived earlier fix-runs

R68, R92, R116, R125, R148, R152 all hit bugs.rtf #1 but each targeted a different progress leak:
- R68: nav counters stale after rate
- R92: silent quota failure in `saveSentenceCard`/`savePhraseCard`
- R116: study-progress bar width on resume
- R125: div-by-zero in `updateGoalBar` + cat-progress
- R148: stale `la_cards` causing phantom Learned count
- R152: `getBestStreak` divergence from `getStreak`

The sentence/phrase pipeline has its own rate functions that were written with only the SRS-store concern in mind. None of the prior fixes touched `rateSentence` / `ratePhrase` because their visible symptom (the flashing done-screen) looked healthy. This one needed symptom-by-code-inspection rather than symptom-by-complaint.

### Fix

Added parity block after `saveSentenceCard(s.id, card)` and `savePhraseCard(p.id, card)`:

```js
if (typeof recordActivity === 'function') recordActivity();
if (typeof incDailyCount === 'function') incDailyCount();
var _r155xpS = (typeof XP_PER_RATING !== 'undefined' && XP_PER_RATING[q]) || 0;
if (_r155xpS > 0 && typeof addXp === 'function') addXp(_r155xpS);
```

XP map unchanged: again=0 / hard=5 / good=10 / easy=15. `typeof X === 'function'` guard is defensive — sentence/phrase code paths are reached before the main study session boot in some flows (user lands on sentences from a shared link), so the helpers may not have been called yet.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js` — two inline blocks inserted (10 lines each) after the existing `save*Card` calls in `rateSentence` and `ratePhrase`. No wrap, no helper — direct edit so `toString()`-based probes on these fns continue to work.
- `_dev/probe.js` — +14 CHECKs asserting both fns call `recordActivity` + `incDailyCount` + (`XP_PER_RATING` referenced AND `addXp` called), plus sanity checks that the original `saveSentenceCard`/`savePhraseCard`/`renderSentenceCard`/`renderPhraseCard` calls are still in place (regression guard), plus a check that word `rate()` still has all three calls, plus `XP_PER_RATING` values unchanged.

**No new data file, no new coach** — this is a pure inline bug-fix following the R152 precedent. Adding a coach here would be scope creep.

### Probe result

**All 14 R155 probes green.** 1288 total greens. Zero BAD, zero THROWS.

One near-miss during authoring: first pass used a `iAdd > iMap` ordering assertion to confirm `addXp` was called *after* the XP lookup. But the inline comment I added mentions "addXp" before "XP_PER_RATING" appears in source, so `indexOf` on the raw fn body returned `iAdd=853, iMap=1261` — failing the order check for a cosmetic reason. Replaced with a tighter substring match on the exact guarded-call pattern `typeof addXp === 'function'`, which is unambiguous and only appears in the real call site.

**Lesson to carry:** when using `indexOf`-based probes on fn bodies, assume your own comments may contain the grep target. Either (a) grep for something that only appears in the real code (a unique call expression, not a bare identifier) or (b) strip comments with `.replace(/\/\/.*$/gm,'')` before indexing.

Run #156 = NEW FEATURE (156 mod 3 = 0). Candidates:

- Weekly Recap coach — rollup of words-learned, XP-gained, streak-continued, sentences+phrases reviewed. Stacks on R105's daily summary.
- Lebanese-only study filter — honors R151's dialect pill downstream: if a word's last wikt fetch was tagged MSA, skip or warn.

### Milestone

**155/1000 — 15.5%.** Progress tracking is now coherent across the three rating surfaces: words, sentences, phrases all feed streak + daily-goal + XP. The R155 fix is small but structurally important — dashboards from R68 onward become truthful for sentence-heavy and phrase-heavy sessions. bugs.rtf #1 is not closed (it never will be — there are always more leaks) but one more was plugged.

## Run #157 — AUDIO (157 mod 3 = 1)

**Slot:** AUDIO improvements
**Prefix:** `cdc` (Cache Doctor)
**bugs.rtf reference:** bug #3 — "A lot of words are still missing proper audio."

### What it does

Cache Doctor scans `audioCache()` (backed by `la_audio_v2`) and classifies every key-value pair into 5 buckets:

- **live** — value is an `http(s)://...` URL
- **negative** — value is the `__none__` sentinel (prior Wiktionary + Commons fetch both failed)
- **commons_miss** — key has the `__commons__:` prefix (miss marker from Commons fallback)
- **dialect_tag** — key has the `__dialect__:` prefix (R151's dialect side-cache)
- **legacy** — anything else (unexpected shape, left over from old schema changes)

The coach exposes three surgical flush operations (`cdcFlushNegatives`, `cdcFlushCommonsMisses`, `cdcFlushLegacy`) that delete only the chosen bucket and then call `saveAudioCache()` so the existing quota-safe save path still runs. `cdcFlushByStatus('live')` explicitly returns 0 without touching anything — live URLs are never flushed by this coach.

### Why this addresses bug #3

The most common reason a word stays audio-less in this app is *not* that Wiktionary doesn't have the recording — it's that we asked Wiktionary weeks ago when the recording genuinely didn't exist, got nothing back, wrote `__none__` into the cache, and never retried. Wiktionary / LinguaLibre gain recordings constantly; a negative cache entry is forever poison for that word.

The nuclear option (clear all localStorage) also blows away SRS progress, streak, XP, etc. Cache Doctor lets the user flush *just* the dead-weight audio entries. After a flush + an R154 Pre-Warm run, any recordings that appeared online since the original miss enter the cache.

### Stacking

- **R44** wrote `saveAudioCache` with progressive quota-safe pruning (already drops negatives first when over-quota). Cache Doctor is the proactive version: you don't have to wait for quota to get rid of dead weight.
- **R154** Pre-Warm Audio re-fetches words post-flush. The natural user flow is: open Cache Doctor → see 40 negatives → Flush → open Pre-Warm → see several now come back as `found`.
- **R151** Dialect Mix's `__dialect__:` side-cache is recognized as its own status (`dialect_tag`) so it isn't mistaken for legacy junk and flushed.

### Files touched

- `data/run157-data.js` — new: `CDC_NEGATIVE_SENTINEL='__none__'`, `CDC_COMMONS_PREFIX='__commons__:'`, `CDC_DIALECT_PREFIX='__dialect__:'`, `CDC_STATUSES` (5 entries with label/icon/color), `CDC_TIPS[6]`, `CDC_ABOUT`.
- `js/app.js` — ~180 lines appended: `cdcClassify(key,value)`, `cdcScanCache()`, `cdcFlushByStatus(status)`, wrappers `cdcFlushNegatives/cdcFlushCommonsMisses/cdcFlushLegacy`, `_cdcFmtBytes(n)`, state vars `_cdcLastFlushCount`/`_cdcLastFlushKind`, overlay `openCdc/closeCdc/setCdcTab/renderCdc`, UI runner `_cdcRunFlushFromUi`. 5 tabs: overview (counts + cache bytes), samples (first 5 keys per bucket), flush (3 flush buttons with live counts), tips, about.
- `index.html` — `<script src="data/run157-data.js">`, 🩺 Cache Dr button (after 📊 Audit), `#cdc-overlay` block (after `#pra-overlay`).
- `_dev/probe.js` — added `data/run157-data.js` to FILES, +26 CHECKs, +8 fn_ checks.

## Run #158 — BUG FIX (158 mod 3 = 2)

**Slot:** BUG FIX
**bugs.rtf reference:** bug #1 — "Progress tracking straight up doesn't work." (calendar display)

### The bug

`renderReviewCalendar()` built date keys for `dayMap` (session history) and `dueMap` (future SRS due dates) using the pattern:

```js
const d = new Date(s.date);                        // s.date = toISOString() — UTC
const key = `${d.getFullYear()}-${d.getMonth()}-${d.getDate()}`;  // 0-indexed month, no padding
```

`new Date(isoString)` interprets the timestamp as UTC. `d.getFullYear() / d.getMonth() / d.getDate()` return **local-time** fields from a UTC-interpreted Date — which disagree when the user's local time has a negative UTC offset. A US East Coast user studying at 11pm (UTC-5) has `s.date = "...T04:00:00Z"` (next UTC day), so `d.getDate()` returns tomorrow's date. The session showed up on the wrong calendar cell.

This is the exact same root cause R83 fixed in `renderTodayDashboard` for `todaySecs`. `renderReviewCalendar` was written earlier or wasn't in scope for R83's sweep.

A second occurrence existed in the "upcoming 7 days" legend section (line ~7525) which also used `\`${d.getFullYear()}-${d.getMonth()}-${d.getDate()}\`` to build lookup keys against `dueMap`, meaning upcoming-due dots would also display on wrong cells if the format didn't match.

### Fix

Three targeted edits:

1. `dayMap` build: `new Date(s.date)` key → `_localDateKey(new Date(s.date))`
2. `dueMap` build: same → `_localDateKey(new Date(card.due))`
3. Calendar cell key (line 7466): `\`${y}-${m}-${day}\`` → `\`${y}-${String(m+1).padStart(2,'0')}-${String(day).padStart(2,'0')}\`` to produce `YYYY-MM-DD` matching `_localDateKey` output
4. Upcoming-7-days section: `\`${d.getFullYear()}-${d.getMonth()}-${d.getDate()}\`` → `_localDateKey(d)`

The `new Date(y, m, d)` constructor in cell generation and upcoming-7 already uses local-timezone values (JavaScript's `Date(year, month, day)` constructor is always local time), so converting their output through `_localDateKey` is safe and consistent.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js` — 4 inline line edits in `renderReviewCalendar` + comment explaining the fix. No new code added, no helper needed — `_localDateKey` already exists from the original codebase.
- `_dev/probe.js` — +7 CHECKs: two positive assertions (dayMap/dueMap use `_localDateKey`), one for padded cell keys, two for absence of stale key patterns, two for `_localDateKey` correctness.

**No data file, no new coach** — minimal inline bug fix.

### Probe result

**All 7 R158 probes green.** 1348 total greens. Zero BAD, zero THROWS.

One near-miss: initial probes searched for `d.getMonth()` in the raw `toString()` body, not accounting for the comment in my own fix that mentioned `d.getMonth()` — returning false positives. Switched to searching for the specific stale *code patterns* (not identifiers) that are unambiguous if they're in executable position.

## Run #159 — NEW FEATURE (159 mod 3 = 0)

**Slot:** NEW FEATURE
**Prefix:** `rfc` (Review Forecast)
**bugs.rtf reference:** structural follow-up to R158's timezone fix — the calendar now shows correct cells; the forecast extends that forward.

### What it does

Review Forecast plots the upcoming SRS review load for each of the next 30 days as a horizontal bar chart. Each bar is color-coded by intensity:

| Bucket   | Count  | Color  |
|----------|--------|--------|
| Light    | 0–10   | green  |
| Moderate | 11–25  | blue   |
| Heavy    | 26–50  | amber  |
| Intense  | 50+    | red    |

Overdue cards land in day 0 ("Today"). The summary tab gives totals, daily average, peak-day count, and heavy-day count. Paired with Near-Due Peek (R153, <24h) and Progress Audit (R156, last 14d), the forecast completes the time-axis triptych:

```
←— Progress Audit (14d lookback) —|— Near-Due Peek (24h) |— Review Forecast (30d ahead) —→
```

### Implementation notes

`rfcGetForecast(days)` reads `la_srs` directly (same data as `renderReviewCalendar`) and uses `_localDateKey(new Date(card.due))` — the fix from R158 — to bucket correctly. `dayOffset = floor((due - todayMidnight) / 86400000)` maps each future due timestamp to 0-indexed day offset. Cards already overdue all count toward day 0.

`rfcBucketFor(count)` walks `RFC_BUCKET_THRESHOLDS` and returns the first bucket where `count <= max` (with `Infinity` catching all heavy tail). `rfcSummary(fc)` aggregates total, peak, average, and heavy-day count.

The bar chart uses CSS flexbox with `flex:1` bars, height proportional to `count/maxCount * 100%`, clamped to 4% minimum so even 1-card days are visible. Day labels truncate to `+N` for days >1 to fit 30 columns.

- `data/run159-data.js` — new: `RFC_DAYS=30`, `RFC_BUCKET_THRESHOLDS` (4 entries with key/label/max/color), `RFC_TIPS[6]`, `RFC_ABOUT` (references R158's timezone fix).
- `js/app.js` — ~130 lines appended: `rfcGetForecast(days)`, `rfcBucketFor(count)`, `rfcSummary(forecast)`, `openRfc/closeRfc/setRfcTab/renderRfc`. 4 tabs: forecast (bar chart + legend), summary (grid), tips, about.

## Run #160 — AUDIO (160 mod 3 = 1)

**Slot:** AUDIO improvements
**Prefix:** extends `cdc` (Cache Doctor, R157)
**bugs.rtf reference:** bug #2 — "sentence audio is often not Lebanese arabic" / bug #4 — "audio system fragility."

### What it does

Adds a **Dialect Breakdown** tab to Cache Doctor (R157). Scans all `__dialect__:` side-cache entries — populated by the Wiktionary fetch chain (R40/R88) whenever a recording is fetched and tagged with a dialect badge — and classifies them into six bands:

| Band      | Emoji | Scoring |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| Lebanese  | 🇱🇧   | Ideal — real Lebanese Arabic |
| YouTube   | 🎬    | Also ideal — native speakers |
| Levantine | 🌍    | Acceptable — Syrian/Palestinian/Jordanian |
| Wiktionary| 🎙    | Unknown dialect |
| MSA       | 📚    | Poor — Modern Standard Arabic |
| Unknown   | ❔    | No emoji match |

A health indicator shows **"X% of tagged recordings are Lebanese or YouTube"** with a ✅/⚠️/🔴 badge. Also reports how many live URL entries have no dialect tag yet (untagged entries pre-date R88's dialect side-caching).

### Why this matters

Bugs.rtf #2 ("sentence audio is often not Lebanese") stems from three things:
1. Some words never had a recording fetched → still `__none__` (Cache Doctor flush helps)
2. Some words have a recording but it's MSA (visible here for the first time as raw cache data)
3. R88 already added dialect-ranked best-match selection — but the user couldn't see the ratio

This tab makes the dialect quality of the audio cache visible at a glance. A user with 40% MSA-tagged entries knows the audio chain is serving a lot of non-Lebanese audio and can investigate (flush negatives, re-fetch, consider recording their own).

### Implementation

Added `cdcDialectBreakdown()` as a new appendonly function (no modification to R157's `cdcScanCache`/`cdcClassify`). Edited `setCdcTab` to add `'dialect'` to the tab array and `renderCdc` to handle `_cdcTab === 'dialect'`. Both edits touch existing function bodies — no new globals that break R157's toString-based probes (R157 only checked `typeof cdcScanCache === 'function'`, not the body).

### Files touched

- `js/app.js` — `cdcDialectBreakdown()` appended (~50 lines), two inline edits: tab array in `setCdcTab`, dialect-case block in `renderCdc` switch.
- `_dev/probe.js` — +12 CHECKs, +1 fn_ check.

**No data file, no HTML change** — extends existing overlay.

### Probe result

**All 13 new R160 assertions green.** 1381 total greens. Zero BAD, zero THROWS.

Coverage: 2 constants (band shape, emoji presence), 4 core logic (empty cache, Lebanese+MSA+Levantine mix, YouTube counts as Lebanese, live-URL counting), 3 edge cases (non-dialect keys skip, unknown values → unknown bucket, lebaneseTotal = lebanese + youtube), 2 wiring (tab array includes 'dialect', renderCdc handles it), 1 fn_.

### Next run

Run #161 = BUG FIX (161 mod 3 = 2). Candidates:
- Progress Audit XP drill-down: some coach quiz paths call recordActivity + incDailyCount but not addXp (minimal-pairs, grammar-ex, conj-quiz, etc.). This is the "same bug class as R155" — should they give XP? If yes, which XP map?
- Hard-words mode bug: `getHardWords()` calls `getDueCards()` inside `hardWordsMode` which recurses — check for infinite recursion.
- Review-calendar future-dot display: after R158's key fix, verify dueMap and calendar-cell keys agree (probe already asserts this, but a UI walk would confirm).

### Milestone

**160/1000 — 16.0%.** The audio dashboard is now four-layered: R154 fetches missing audio proactively, R157 shows what's in the cache, R160 shows the dialect quality of what's there, and R44/R88 handle the fetch chain itself. A user can now ask: "do I have audio? → R157. Is it Lebanese? → R160. What about upcoming cards? → R154. Clean up dead entries? → R157 flush."

## Run #161 — BUG FIX: Leech threshold off-by-one

**Category**: BUG FIX (161 % 3 == 2)

### Bug

`renderLeechPanel`, `resetAllLeeches`, and `startLeechDrill` all used `lapses >= 3` as the leech threshold, but every other part of the codebase (`getHardWords`, smart-recs insight at line 1013, session-done hard-words list at lines 1466–1468, body-health panel at lines 1685–1686, spaced-rep coach at line 2415) uses `lapses >= 4`.

This caused the Leech Panel to display words as leeches one lapse too early, the Leech Drill to start drilling words that aren't actually leeches yet, and `resetAllLeeches` to wipe SRS data for cards with only 3 lapses — erasing legitimate progress on words that would not be shown as leeches in hard-words mode or smart-recs.

### Fix

Changed all three sites to `>= 4`:
- `renderLeechPanel` (line ~2696): filter `(c.lapses || 0) >= 4`
- `resetAllLeeches` (line ~2766): delete condition `(c.lapses || 0) >= 4`
- `startLeechDrill` (line ~2777): filter `(c.lapses || 0) >= 4`

No behavior change for cards with 4+ lapses — only cards at exactly 3 lapses are now correctly excluded.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js` — 3 inline edits (no new functions, no append)
- `_dev/probe.js` — +7 CHECKs

### Probe result

**All 7 new R161 assertions green.** 1389 total greens. Zero BAD, zero THROWS.

Coverage: `renderLeechPanel` uses `>= 4`, `renderLeechPanel` has no `>= 3`, `resetAllLeeches` uses `>= 4`, `startLeechDrill` uses `>= 4`, cross-fn consistency check (all three must pass), prior R160 intact, prior R159 intact.

### Next run

Run #162 = AUDIO (162 % 3 == 0). Candidates:
- Pre-warm audio for leech drill words (startLeechDrill fetches top-20 leeches — none are pre-warmed)
- Wire audio into renderLeechPanel word cards (each leech row has no 🔊 button)

## Run #173 — BUG FIX — 2026-04-20

**XP parity wave 4: 10 more coach answer handlers**

### Bug

Audit of all `*Answer` / `*Pick` functions found 22 handlers missing `recordActivity`, `incDailyCount`, and `addXp`. R164/R167/R170 addressed 11 handlers; 22 remained. This run fixes 10 of the most commonly-used ones.

Fixed: `spdAnswer` (Sentence Pattern Drill), `dprAnswer` (Discourse Pattern), `idmAnswer` (Idiom Coach), `stcAnswer` (Story Coach), `tecAnswer` (Topic+Everyday Coach), `negAnswer` (Negation Coach), `qfcAnswer` (Question Formation Coach), `pscAnswer` (Pronouns Coach), `lssAnswer` (Lebanese Speech Style), `aspAnswer` (Aspect/Tense Coach).

Remaining (lower traffic): `rwotdAnswer1/2`, `ptAnswer` (placement — excluded by design), `answerListenQ`, `pickSuffixAnswer`, `pickQwAnswer`, `pickNegAnswer`, `pickImpAnswer`, `pickCmpAnswer`, `pickPlAnswer`, `mpxAnswer`, `dlcAnswer`, `pcAnswerComplete`.

### Fix pattern

Each function: inside the `if(correct)` or `if(opt.correct)` block, appended:
```
if(typeof recordActivity==='function') recordActivity();
if(typeof incDailyCount==='function') incDailyCount();
if(typeof addXp==='function') addXp((typeof XP_PER_RATING!=='undefined'?XP_PER_RATING[2]:0)||10);
```
For `pscAnswer`/`lssAnswer`: added inside the `!already` dedup guard so multiple clicks on same question don't double-award.

**Bug 2 — `mpxAnswer` missing answered guard (double XP possible)**:
Added `_mpxAnswered = false` state variable, set to `true` on first call. Guard added at top of `mpxAnswer`. Reset in `mpxNewQuiz`.

**Bug 3 — `pcAnswerComplete` missing answered guard**:
Added `|| _pcLast` to the existing guard check. `_pcLast` is set on first answer and cleared in `pcNextSituation`, so it naturally prevents double-award.

## Run #182 — BUG FIX: answerListenQ double-award + VCB category jump

**Category**: BUG FIX (182 % 3 == 2)

### What was fixed

**Bug 1 — `answerListenQ` double XP award when `submitListenQuiz` fires**:
`submitListenQuiz` calls `answerListenQ(qi, answer)` for ALL questions, including already-answered ones. This re-awarded XP for each previously correct answer. Fix: added `if (listenAnswers[qi] !== undefined) return;` guard at top of `answerListenQ`. For unanswered questions (submit reveals them as wrong with oi=-1), the guard passes since `listenAnswers[qi]` is `undefined`. For already-answered questions, returns early — buttons stay styled from original click, no double XP.

**Bug 2 — VCB category filter leaving orphaned selected verb**:
When switching category filter in the Verb Browser, the selected verb (shown in the table) could be from a different category than the filter, making the active button invisible in the grid. Fix: `_vcbSetCat` now checks if `CONJ_VERBS[_vcbVerbIdx].id` is in the new category's `verbIds`. If not, jumps to first verb in the filtered set.

### Files touched

- `js/app.js` — 2 edits
- `_dev/probe.js` — +6 R182 CHECKs

## Run #263
**Category:** BUG FIX (263 % 3 == 2)
**Feature:** Fixed permanent `__none__` audio cache entries. Words with no Wiktionary/Commons recording were cached as `__none__` forever — even after recordings were later added to those sources, the app would never re-check. Fix: override `saveAudioCache` to stamp `__none__` writes with current timestamp (`__none__:TS`), and override `audioCache` to expire stamped entries older than 7 days (drops from returned object so speak() re-checks live sources on next play). Legacy plain `__none__` entries (no timestamp) also expire immediately. Fresh stamped entries are normalized back to `__none__` so all existing `=== '__none__'` comparisons continue to work unchanged.
**Probe:** All 3 R263 checks pass.

263/1000 runs done.

## Run #269
**Category:** BUG FIX (269 % 3 == 2)
**Feature:** Fixed `_audioBulkPrecache` interaction with R263 stale-cache expiry. Before R263, `_audioBulkPrecache` intentionally re-queried `'__none__'` entries hoping recordings had been added since last check. After R263, `audioCache()` already handles expiry — stale entries become `undefined` (re-queued correctly) and fresh entries stay as `'__none__'` (checked recently, no result). But `_audioBulkPrecache` still re-queried all `'__none__'` entries, wasting network requests on every coach open. Fix: override `_audioBulkPrecache` to filter out fresh `'__none__'` entries (both wikt and commons) before passing to the original. Stale entries (R263 drops them → `undefined`) still get re-queued correctly.

## Run #401 — Bug Fix: APT Coach Double-Pick Guard · BUG FIX

**Category:** bug fix (401%3==2)
**Bug:** `aptPickOpt` (R399 APT coach) was missing the double-pick guard pattern. In some browsers, clicking a `button[disabled]` still fires onclick. ## R740 — BUG FIX · Normalize speak() slow param — audio IIFEs caused 0.70x speed

Root cause: audio IIFEs (R727–R739) intercept speak(tr_text) and redirect via _fn(w.ar, 'ar'). speak() signature is (text, slow=false, externalBtn) — the string 'ar' propagated as slow=truthy through the entire IIFE chain to the original speak(), where (slow ? 0.70 : 1.0) triggered slow playback. Every word tapped via ELC/MIG/BTY/CNS/BKF coaches played at 70% speed. Fixed: wrapped playAudio + _speakViaBrowser to normalize slow with `slow === true`, so string 'ar' becomes false → 1.0x playback restored. 0 new BADs.

## R827 — BUG FIX · Patch immNext naming collision

The immigration coach (R786) defined `function immNext(){}` which — being a hoisted function declaration — silently overwrote the immersion autoplay `immNext` at line 6123. Result: the ⏭ button in the Immersion overlay incremented `_immDrillIdx` (immigration drill index) instead of `immIdx`, freezing the immersion card autoplay. Fix: IIFE at end of app.js saves both implementations then replaces `immNext` with a dispatcher that routes based on whether `#imm-overlay` is visible. ## R929 — BUG FIX: Reject stale async audio (Wiktionary/Commons race)
- Root cause: speak() async — after `await fetchWiktionaryAudio()` / `await fetchCommonsAudio()` resolve, `_speakGen` may have advanced (study card advance → new speak() → stopAllAudio bumps gen). Stale callback plays previous card's audio over new card.
- Fix 1: wrap outer `speak()` to track `window._r929LastSpeakText`
- Fix 2: wrap `fetchWiktionaryAudio` to return null if gen changes during in-flight fetch (null → speak() skips cache write + playAudio call)
- Fix 3: wrap `playAudio` + `_speakViaBrowser` to silently drop calls where `originalText !== _r929LastSpeakText`
- Fixes: "study auto-plays audio for previous word when no Lebanese audio is available" and "browse tab some words play audio for other words"
- Probe: 0 new BADs, 387 funcs

## R1643 — BUG FIX — 2026-04-27

bugs.rtf #5: study auto-plays audio for previous word when no Lebanese audio is available.
Root cause: NOT in speakSmart (R1607 already fixed chunk-level race). The leak is in repeatSpeak (Run #43, line ~18216). When user rates "Again", rate() captures `currentCard.ar` and fires `repeatSpeak(oldCardAr, 2, 700)` — async loop sleeps 700ms between iterations. Meanwhile advanceStudy → showNextCard → speak(newCard.ar) starts via auto-speak. stopAllAudio bumps _speakGen, but repeatSpeak's outer loop never checks generation — after the 700ms sleep it calls speak() with OLD text again. Plays the OLD card's audio over the new card's playback. If the new card has no Lebanese audio, the only audible output is the OLD card's repeat — exactly the user-reported symptom.
Fix: wrap repeatSpeak with gen-snapshot. Capture _speakGen at entry; check before each speak() call AND after each gap sleep. If _speakGen bumped (any new speak() since loop started), abort silently. Counter __r1643Aborts tracks fires.
4 probe markers (guard/done/aborts/repeat). 0 BADs. node --check OK.

## R1646 — BUG FIX (1646%3=2): cultural-coach onclick HTML attribute breakage
bugs.rtf #2 ("lot of words missing audio") manifestation: 7 onclick handlers in cultural coaches were broken.
Pattern `onclick="speak(${JSON.stringify(w.ar)})"` (and `w.t`) interpolates JSON.stringify output (which always wraps strings in double quotes) INSIDE a double-quoted HTML attribute. HTML5 parser splits the attribute at the first inner `"`, leaving onclick value as literal `speak(` — SyntaxError on click, no audio fires.
Verified via node test: `<div onclick="speak("الشحرورة")">` → browser DOM reads onclick=`speak(`.
Affected lines: 84582, 84779 (older speak-btn spots), 88042 (browse cards), 104230 (Listen button), 127315 (HAM coach), 127584 (ACH coach), 127790 (WSF coach). All 7 instances replaced `JSON.stringify(w.X)` → `attrArg(w.X)`. attrArg() runs JSON.stringify then encodes `"` as `&quot;` — browser HTML-decodes back to `"` when reading attribute value, JS handler sees correct `speak("الشحرورة")`.
attrArg defined at line 16944 as plain function decl → hoisted globally → in scope at all 7 edit sites.
R1646 IIFE marker: inspects renderHam/renderAch/renderWsf via toString() → confirms no remaining JSON.stringify(w.t/w.ar) substrings. window.__r1646Fixed=true when all 3 render funcs clean.
4 probe markers (guard/done/fixed/checks). 0 BADs. node --check OK.
Bugs.rtf check: 5 known bugs unchanged. Fixes one concrete bug-#2 manifestation — cultural-coach 🔊 buttons now work.

## R1655 — BUG FIX — Minimal pairs listen onclick HTML attribute breakage
Concrete root cause for bugs.rtf #4 ("Minimal pairs listening drill sound not working properly"). R989-era setMpxMode override at app.js line 87970 wraps original then re-renders mpx-content for listen mode using `JSON.stringify(p.a.ar)` directly inside `onclick="..."` HTML attribute. JSON.stringify wraps text in literal double quotes → embedded as `onclick="playMinPairListen("text","other")"` → inner `"` terminates outer attribute prematurely → onclick attribute value truncates to `playMinPairListen(` → SyntaxError on click → no audio plays. R989/R1046/R1550/R1580/R1604/R1637 all wrapped playMinPairListen logic but never noticed call site was malformed HTML. All other onclick sites (R1605/R1608/R1611/R1629/cswCheck) use `.replace(/"/g,'&quot;')` after JSON.stringify — only this site missed.
Fix R1655 IIFE wraps setMpxMode (3rd layer post-R987 + post-original): when m==='listen', re-renders mpx-content using `attrArg(p.a.ar)` (line 16944 = JSON.stringify+&quot;) — HTML-attribute-safe. window.__r1655Renders counter increments per listen render. Compatible with R1604/R1637 playMinPairListen wraps (only fixes call site, not handler). Preserves toString visibility + setMpxMode static props via Object.keys forEach.
4 probe markers (guard/done/setMpx/attrArg). 0 BADs. node --check OK.
Bugs.rtf check: 5 known bugs unchanged in file. But this is a real reduction in bug-#4 surface — listen-drill clicks now actually fire playMinPairListen instead of throwing SyntaxError.

## R1676 — BUG FIX — aggressive stopAllAudio reset for Bug #5
Bug #5 ("study auto-plays previous word audio when no Lebanese audio") persists after R1571/R1607/R1625/R1634/R1643. Reviewed stopAllAudio (line 3503): pause + src='' + speechSynthesis.cancel(). On Chrome, `audio.src = ''` does NOT fully reset the buffer — next play() can replay residual data. speechSynthesis.cancel() also flaky on Chrome (in-flight utterance lingers briefly after cancel returns).
Fix: append IIFE wrapping stopAllAudio. Adds (a) `currentTime = 0`, (b) `removeAttribute('src')`, (c) `audio.load()` (forces media element reset), (d) double speechSynthesis.cancel — sync + setTimeout(fn,0) microtask drain. Preserves prior wrap flags (e.g. __r1571Wrapped) by copying own-props from _orig onto the new wrap.
Probe: + r1676_guard/r1676_done/r1676_stop. 0 BAD, 519 funcs. Old r1571_stopWrap remained ok (flag copy worked).
Bugs.rtf check: 5 known bugs unchanged in file (will validate Bug #5 after user-side test on Chrome).
1676/1000 runs. Next R1677 (1677%3=0) = NEW FEATURE.

## R1679 — BUG FIX — polymorphic sfx shim (string args route to fn callbacks)
Audit found `function sfx(fn){ if(sfxEnabled) fn(); }` (app.js:529) accepts ONLY function callbacks. 169 call sites pass strings (e.g. `sfx('correct')`, `sfx(correct?'correct':'wrong')`, `sfx('wrong')`, `sfx(s)` where s is string) — these silently fail because `'correct'()` throws TypeError that's swallowed by surrounding try/catch. Result: ~169 invocations across coaches (Mahrajan/Nostalgia/Saj/Hammam/Hakawati/orc/tcg/crf/zia/etc — anything written with the older string-style sfx call) had no audio feedback.
Counted: 169 buggy `sfx && sfx(` patterns vs 327 correct `playSfx && playSfx(` patterns.
Fix: append IIFE wrapping global `sfx` to be polymorphic — accept (a) function (preserve old behavior), (b) string keys 'correct'/'wrong'/'flip'/'goal' routed to sfxCorrect/sfxWrong/sfxFlip/sfxGoal callbacks. Other types silent no-op. Wrapped via window.sfx = _r1679Sfx with try/catch fallback for the local binding. Carried over own-props from _origSfx (preserves any prior wrap markers).
Probe: + r1679_guard/done/strmap (verifies 'correct'+'wrong' both registered)/string (calls sfx('correct') sfx('wrong'))/fn (calls sfx(noop)). All ok. 0 BAD, 519 funcs.
Bugs.rtf check: 5 known bugs unchanged (sentence audio dialect, words missing audio, browse cross-talk, minimal pairs broken, study auto-plays prev). This fix touches only the SFX layer, not the speech/audio playback bugs.

## R1682 — BUG FIX: lcw drill correctness
**Bug**: R1680 lcw coach (Lebanese Civil War) — `renderLcw` rendered opts in fixed `[d.a,d.d1,d.d2]` order; `lcwPickOpt(i)` checked `i === 0`. Result: clicking first option always correct → drill broken.
**Fix**: override `window.openLcw / closeLcw / setLcwTab / renderLcw / lcwPickOpt / lcwNext` with bcr-pattern — deterministic seeded sort on `[d.a,d.d1,d.d2]` (`(len+idx)%7` modulus key), pass `JSON.stringify(opt)` in onclick, compare `opt === d.a` in pickOpt. State on `window.__lcwTab/__lcwDrillIdx/__lcwDrillAnswered` for sync between override functions.
**Same class as**: R1526 (njr/mkh) and R1677 (bcr).
**Probe**: 7 markers (guard, done, pickFn, renderFn, pickStr correct→answered, pickWrong wrong→answered, renderTag onclick contains string-literal lcwPickOpt). 0 BAD.

## Run #1700 — BUG FIX
**bugs.rtf #1 fix** — extend R1576 `speak()` single-word romanized→Arabic wrap to also handle multi-word inputs via direct `__r1573Map` phrase lookup. R1576 rejects any input containing a space, so multi-word entries from recent coaches (EHD: "mar mama", "kfar zayna", "nahr abu ali", "3id mar mama", "bayit jdid", "mar serkis"; QSH/MWL/etc similar) were never substituted to Arabic before TTS — browser TTS pronounced English letters. ## Run #1726 — BUG FIX (2026-06-09)
bugs.rtf #3 "Browse tab plays audio for OTHER words." Root cause: `_audioKeyVariants` (R67) strips proclitics (و/ب/ف/ل/س/ما/رح/عم) + pronoun suffixes (ـي/ـك/ـو/ـها) + def-article (ال) even when that char is ROOT material, so single-word `speak()` resolves فكرة "idea"→كرة "ball", وسادة "pillow"→سادة, سخّان "heater"→خان, عمليّة "surgery"→ليه — a DIFFERENT cached word's clip, badge still "🎬 Lebanese speaker". R1570 only blocked strips landing on a VOCAB.ar entry; these collision keys live only in the runtime Wiktionary cache (not VOCAB) so slipped through, and `_audioCommonsMatchFor` was never tightened. Fix: append IIFE (`__r1726Guard`) wrapping `_audioCacheMatchFor`/`_audioCommonsMatchFor`/`_audioYtMatchFor` — when the ORIGINAL text is a VOCAB lexeme (Browse always plays `v.ar`), reject any match whose key isn't a SELF-FORM (punctuation/tashkeel strip + hamza/ya/ta-marbuta normalize only; NO clitic/def-article strip), then re-scan self-forms dialect-ranked. Non-VOCAB inflected inputs (Phrases tab, speakSmart chunks, R62/R88 `بكتاب→كتاب` contracts) keep wide matching — surgical. window-only patch (matches R1570; bare===window in browser, so speak()'s bare call site picks it up; bare reassign would only diverge the Node probe). Found by 5-agent workflow + adversarial verify; probe revealed an r62/r88 bare-binding artifact that I traced + resolved. 9 probe markers all ok, 0 BAD overall.
